entities.name: Tag-Along Freddy
entities.description:
is a brand of animatronic toys manufactured by Fazbear Entertainment. One of these is featured in The Cliffs, the first story of the Fazbear Frights book of the same name. They are an electronic toy version of Freddy Fazbear.

Tag-Along Freddy is a small, plushy version of the classic Freddy Fazbear. He is a plush brown bear with wide smiles, thick black eyebrows, a black top hat, and blank, empty googly eyes.

Robert buys one for his son, Tyler, and after Tyler disappears the toy begins to torment Robert. At first Robert attempts to burn the bear, which only smolders its foot at first but eventually the bears becomes charred with an intact grin. Robert later uses scissors to stab into the bear’s chest, slashing it open and revealing bits of stuffing through the tears.

Tag-Along Freddy is very aware on what a child is doing whenever he's watching. He can tell if a child is playing, eating food, or sleeping. He texts those messages to the parent through the Tag-Along Time wristwatch so the parents can monitor their child's activities.

entities.description:

is an amalgamation of Andrew's infected objects. It's possessed by William Afton. It appeared in the epilogues in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird and Fazbear Frights 7: The Cliffs.

The Agony is a vaguely man-shaped structure of trash primarily made from everything Andrew infected and the remaining junk and debris in the factory. Standing at nearly fifteen feet tall, its body is formed with moving animatronic body parts, joined in a haywire way. Heads are used as joints, arms as legs, and legs as arms. A torso forms from the hips, chest, and belly of three animatronics but their parts are put in the wrong places. Hands are inserted at random all over the structure. Wires and gears are woven through all the misplaced pieces, creating a labyrinthine circulatory system connecting hinges to gears and screws and nails to eyes, noses, and mouths. It has a neck made from shins and feet with mouths. The Agony’s head is made of animatronic fingers, toes, wires, and hinges, and resembles William Afton’s face. Its eyes are two gaping black holes made of metal sockets and spark plugs. The Agony's mouth is formed from long pistons, and its cheekbones are composed of large gears and bolts. Its face is held together with bits of pointed metal and rusted pipes. The Agony has two rabbit ears, one made of three-quarters of a metal hand and the other with a metal jaw. It has a hand composed of a foot with sharp metal toes and hip joint, and its feet are composed of hands, jaws, and joints. There’s a kneecap with an eye on it where a shoulder should have been. While the hybrid lacks the remains of the Stitchwraith endoskeleton, having ejected it from its own body, it contains the limbs and circuitry of at least four animatronics in a disorganized fashion. It's implied many other animatronics are inside, but the four animatronics that are confirmed and named to comprise the Agony's parts are Fetch, Ella, Foxy, and the Plushtrap Chaser. Part of it is made from Eleanor’s battered, rusting, long-necked, and vaguely female-shaped endoskeleton.

As the Agony pursues Larson, it contains to add parts to its body. A rat skeleton gets attached to an animatronic elbow acting as a chin, and a bird's foot is affixed to part of a motor acting as an eyebrow. It then absorbs a forklift into its body.

entities.name: The Blackbird
entities.description:
is the main antagonist in Blackbird of the Fazbear Frights series, featured in both the book and its story of the same name.

The Blackbird is an animatronic costume hand-made by Sam O'Neil to resemble a giant blackbird. It has long black feathers covering its body, two wide, dead beady yellow-and-black eyes, a tiny pointed orange beak, and oversized proportions. The curve of the Blackbird's belly comes all the way down to below Sam's knees so the legs start at his shins to convey realistic proportions. It also has black rubber bird feet attached to stretch-to-fit water shoes and extra-extra-large black tights with a scale pattern. It's inspired by the Freddy's animatronics, various comments made about the length of Sam's legs reminding people about various long-legged bird species, and Edgar Allan Poe's The Raven.

According to the story Nole and Sam make up, the Blackbird stalks its victims and punishes them for something they've done wrong in the past. They either must atone for their sins or suffer the consequences. When manifesting before Nole, they fill an identical role, trying to force Nole to atone through apologizing to Christine for his actions.

The Blackbird was created to serve as the main villain in a horror film college project by Sam and Nole after the pair remembered the creepiness of the Freddy Fazbear's Pizza animatronics. They decided he would punish his victims because of their past acts after Nole brought up he had seen one while planning on not attending class, and its gaze had made him feel guilty enough to return. In their project, the Blackbird would stalk the main character Floyd for past transgressions. Three days later, Sam creates the costume of the character. He weaves long black feathers into a netted black fabric which will be sewn onto a black body-hugging suit. To make its feet, Sam and his mother make bird toes out of black rubber, carving deep grooves into them. They then create bird claws and insert them into the rubber toes. He attaches the bird feet to a pair of stretch-to-fit water shoes and put on extra-extra-large black tights with a scale pattern. Adding the eyes and beak last, Sam puts on the costume scaring himself when looking in the mirror.

entities.name: The Stitchwraith
entities.description:
is an animatronic endoskeleton who was brought to life with "agony" by Dr. Phineas Taggart. He contains the soul of Jake, Andrew, and William Afton. He appears in all the Stitchwraith Stingers epilogues of the Fazbear Frights books and as an easter egg in Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit.

The Stitchwraith is a mysterious figure wearing a long and voluminous wool hooded trench coat that originally belonged to Phineas. Its body is a broken, ruptured man-sized endoskeleton of unknown origin. The Stitchwraith's head is that of the Real Jake Doll, being placed on top of the endoskeleton’s head. He has a bulky, round white face with features drawn onto the curved surface with thick black marker. The doll has sunken black eyes, one of which is blackened to resemble a black eye the "real Jake" got by standing up to a bully. It has a mouth with a missing tooth and something stuck between the remaining front teeth, which is meant to be a popcorn kernel. Larson mistakes the pizza stains around the mouth for blood stains. The last component of the Stitchwraith is Fetch’s large plastic-encased battery pack, which is placed in a port in the endoskeleton’s chest. His battery pack pulses bright red when first activated, and the Stitchwraith can use the battery back to make his hand can glow red with heat.

The Stitchwraith is often dismissed as an urban legend. He is often seen in garbage dumps, scavenging them for personal intentions. It's been caught on picture dragging a mannequin out of a dumpster in one instance. There are also five murders associated with the Stitchwraith, in which the victims' bodies all appeared withered, with "eyes that bled black down the sides of the face."

It is later seen by a homeless man, Grim, pulling animatronic parts from the destroyed Plushtrap Chaser into a bag, after the events of Out of Stock.

entities.name: VR Springtrap
entities.description:
(simply referred to as Springtrap in the story) is a smaller version of Springtrap who was originated from a video game known as Springtrap's Revenge. He is the main antagonist of In the Flesh, the second story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call.

Much like his game counterpart, VR Springtrap is a large green rabbit with the better part of one ear missing. Unlike his game counterpart, VR Springtrap doesn't contain the corpse of William Afton. Instead, his tattered costume reveals mechanical parts underneath the fabric. VR Springtrap has a wide grin, a tongue, and eyes that glow green when he spots the player.

When Springtrap emerges from Matt’s body in the real world, he is wet and slimy with mucus and the size of a healthy, newborn infant. He is also more organic than the one in the video game.

Despite being very similar to Springtrap from the games, VR Springtrap has a different origin. According to Matt, his design was inspired by his fear of people wearing animal mascot costumes, as one of his earliest fears was inspired from a Mall Easter Bunny that his mother took a picture of him with when he was young. VR Springtrap's murderous nature was inspired by horror movies and real-world serial killers, as Matt wanted to immortalize him as a terrifying character.

entities.name: Wooden Puppets
entities.description:
The only puppet to appear in the story is described as a fully jointed, wooden and human-like figure, resembling a small man. It's said to be pretty crude and basic, and similar to the drawing models used in Porter's high school class.

The wooden puppet appears for the first and only time when Porter shows to Sage how the puppet carver, his new invention able to make low-cost animatronics out of wood, works. He puts a wood log into the machine, and the wooden puppet comes out of it. Porter then pushes a button on the puppet's lower back, and the wooden animatronic starts to move and dance.

entities.name: Yarg Foxy
entities.description:
Yarg Foxy is a variant of the original Foxy animatronic. He appears in Lonely Freddy, the second story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch.

Yarg Foxy is an orange pirate fox with an eyepatch, a peg leg, and a hook. He can either be an animatronic, a human-sized plush, or a smaller plush toy depending on the location.

Official artwork for the Foxy variant portrays him as similar to Captain Foxy, albeit more simplified with a different hat and a peg leg.

Yarg Foxy plays different roles in every Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. At Freddy Fazbear's Family Pizzeria, he's a human-sized plush figure propped by the stage, presumably for taking with. In other locations, Yarg Foxy can greet visitors at the door or play in the band onstage with the others. A smaller plush toy of Yarg Foxy can also be found at the prize counter as the rarest toy. It has the ability to swing its hook. It can be won by getting 10,000 tickets or redeeming a Yarg Foxy ticket, which can only be found in the wind tunnel at the location.

entities.name: Yellow Rabbit
entities.description:
The Yellow Rabbit is the main antagonist of Into the Pit, the first story of the book of the same name, as well as the video game adaptation of the story. It is a supernatural entity that stalks Oswald during his visits to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza and eventually follows him home.

In the story, the Yellow Rabbit is described as a yellow version of Bonnie with fuzzy yellow fur and big paws and feet. It's currently unclear if it's an animatronic, a living creature, or both. The Yellow Rabbit has blank and dead eyes that "didn't feel like a living creature's eyes." He usually has an unchanging grin, but he can unhinge his jaw and open it incredibly wide to reveal double rows of sharp fangs. The Yellow Rabbit wears a purple bow tie. After his death, he's nothing more than a dirty, empty mascot costume.

On the cover and in the unused illustration, its head is large and body rotund, similar to Nightmare Fredbear's. Its eyes are blue, with organic material surrounding them. Inside of its grinning jaw are huge square-ish teeth. It also has two black buttons under his purple bow tie. On the cover, a black blood is leaking out of its right eye socket.

In the videogame, it is shown that both the suit and monster are not completely different entities. This is seen more clearly through its large variety of jumpscares where the suit is seen having organic gums for its teeth, and using real muscles to join the jaw with the skull. Those muscles can partially be seen during cutscenes or jumpscares. This indicates that the Spring Bonnie suit is the skin of the creature itself rather than an actual costume. It is seen more clearly during the good ending cinematic when the creature is choking with the strings of the ball pit.

entities.name: Dreadbear
entities.description:
, formerly known as Franken Freddy in early development, is a Nightmare/Halloween animatronic and the titular antagonist of Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted's DLC, Curse of Dreadbear. He is a Halloween-themed variant of Nightmare Freddy.

Dreadbear's appearance is similar to that of the classic horror movie icon Frankenstein's monster, sharing properties such as screws stuck to his jaw and stitches all around the body. He's also similar to Nightmare Freddy in terms of his head shape, but with flatter teeth, thicker brows, and bright yellow eyes.

Like the nightmare animatronics, he supports five clawed fingers, but has three-toed feet that are similar in fashion to the toy animatronics.

Unlike other Nightmare Animatronics, Dreadbear (as well as the Jack-O's) is an in-universe character made for the VR Games, not physically existing.

entities.name: Grimm Foxy
entities.description:
is a Halloween/Nightmare animatronic and a major antagonist of Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted's DLC, Curse of Dreadbear. He is a Halloween-themed variant of Nightmare Foxy.

From his multiple renders and official art, Grimm Foxy appears to hold a sort of "Jack-O-Foxy" role. He is a large, bipedal animatronic fox sporting orange-red fur, similar in structure to Nightmare Foxy. Rips and tears are strewn across his suit, with most of the damage being on his torso. Similar to the other Halloween-themed nightmare animatronics, he is missing his endoskeleton head, and a bright orange glow emanates from inside the suit.

His left hand is structured in a similar way to the other nightmare animatronics, with five segmented fingers ending in sharp claws on each finger, while his right hand bears a large sickle, in contrast to his usual hook. He wears brown pants that are ripped from the knees down, and his legs end in trapezoidal feet with four claws protruding out of it.

His head is split into two segments, with the fabric on his muzzle gone, revealing the metal frame underneath. The fur on his ears is also nearly gone, revealing the metal framework. Unlike Nightmare Foxy, Grimm Foxy retains his eye patch, and the tops of his eye sockets are intact, giving him a much angrier look. As a visual aesthetic, flames stream out from inside him whenever he walks or runs. Another added detail is the black spikes that extend out from his shoulders. Unlike Jack-O-Bonnie and Jack-O-Chica, Grimm Foxy has flames coming out of him.

entities.name: Jack-O-Bonnie
entities.description:
is a Halloween/Nightmare animatronic and a major antagonist of the Five Nights at Freddy's series, first appearing in the Halloween Update. He is a Halloween-themed reskinned variant of Nightmare Bonnie who first appeared in Five Nights at Freddy's 4 where he replaced his original counterpart for the Halloween Edition.

His appearance looks exactly like his original variant with the exception of Halloween-themed colors. Rather than being blue-purple, Jack-O-Bonnie is brownish-orange in color. His muzzle, chin, stomach, and the insides of his ears are colored in red-orange. In place of his normal endoskeleton eyes, the eye sockets glow orange and yellow, like an actual Jack-o-lantern. His teeth glow a light-yellow allowing his endoskeleton jaw to glow in low light.

He lacks both a nose and an endoskeleton head, with his endoskeleton teeth being the only exception. His endoskeleton chest is also absent which exposes his backbone with two strings of red wire visible from under his bowtie. A similar effect appears to have been applied to his overall body colored in shining yellow tints, as they can be seen within the torso as well as some endoskeleton parts. A couple of parts on Jack-O-Bonnie's left hand appear to be green instead of brownish-orange.

His bowtie glows in an orange/yellow color. Unlike Nightmare Bonnie, the texture for Jack-O-Bonnie's suit is slightly smoother with no sign of any scratches.

entities.name: Jack-O-Chica
entities.description:
is a Halloween/Nightmare animatronic and a major antagonist of the Five Nights at Freddy's series, first appearing in the Halloween Update. She is a Halloween-themed reskinned variant of Nightmare Chica who first appeared in Five Nights at Freddy's 4 where she replaced her original counterpart for the Halloween Edition.

The first notable difference is her color designs being completely orange in Halloween-style. Her skin color is dark golden rather than yellow. In place of her normal endoskeleton eyes, the eye sockets are quite brightly glowing orange, much like a jack o'lantern. A similar effect appears to have been applied to Jack-O-Chica's overall body, as it can be seen very prevalently around her shoulder sockets and tears from her stomach. Her endoskeleton head is entirely absent while her endoskeleton teeth remain. If one looks closely, they can see that her endoskeleton chest is also absent. Few glowing yellow tints can be seen from her teeth and mouth, allowing her endoskeleton jaw to glow in a slightly dimmed light. The only other noticeable difference is that Jack-O-Chica's feet and lower legs are slightly darker in color than that of Nightmare Chica's. The color of her beak is also darker. The texture for Jack-O-Chica's suit is slightly smoother with a lack of nearly-visible scratches, unlike Nightmare Chica. Her bib is the only feature that remains unchanged.

A large green Jack o'lantern serves as a replacement for Nightmare Chica's cupcake. Interestingly, her Jack o'lantern is nearly identical to the actual pumpkin from the Five Nights at Freddy's 3 Halloween update where it can be seen on The Office desk. It has triangular eye-sockets with round eyes emitting a white glow and a nose like that of a stereotypical Jack-o'lantern, as well as a typical zig-zag mouth and an orange glow emitted from the inside.

In Ultimate Custom Night, her appearance remains the same, but she is missing her third row of teeth.

entities.name: Jack-O-Moon
entities.description:
Jack-O-Moon is one of the halloween animatronics and a minor antagonist that first appeared in Five Nights at Freddy's: Help Wanted 2. He is a Halloween-themed variant of the Moon side of the Daycare Attendant.

Jack-O-Moon shares a similar style to the Halloween Animatronics. He sports the Sun's rays around his face, with them now colored purple. His face is colored half pumpkin orange, half grey. His pants now have dirt covering them and look to be made out of potato sacks, giving him a scarecrow-like appearance. His pants have holes which have been repaired/covered with a dark grey colored fabric. His eyes and mouth show a burning fire from inside of his head. His body features a dusty grey colour and also features a dim orange color and his boots have a purple shade and yellow moons overlaying on them.

Jack-O-Moon first appears in the Captain Foxy's Log Ride level. There are three Helpy cutouts in total that can be hit, taking the player to alternate paths. Jack-O-Moon resides in all of them, and must be stopped before he either makes his way to the log flume, or the player is close enough for Jack-O-Moon to attack. This can be done by either hitting a yellow panel to close a door or window, or activating lights that cause him to flee.

He also appears in the Cinder Carousel level, a hardmode variant of the original. Replacing the original Moon, Jack-O-Moon stalks the player and has to have the flashlight shined on him to scare him off. Aside from the carousel being on fire, the game plays relatively the same.

entities.name: Bouncepot
entities.description:
is an enemy encountered in FNaF World. It is encountered in Fazbear Hills.

Bouncepot has the appearance of a onion-like plant creature with a spiraled stem, two vines waving around that appear to act as its arms, and flies that swirl on either side of it. Its eyes are black with white pupils, and its body is green, with the head being a lighter shade. It is seen inside a wooden pot shaped like a beehive. On the top of its head, it has two leaves that are constantly bouncing around.

"You've been through a lot. I am ready to reveal myself."

"You see. I've been there all along. It was me."

entities.name: Kids at Play Figure
entities.description:
The is an inanimate entity in Kids at Play, the second story of Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster. It appears as an Easter Egg in Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit.

Kids at Play figures are three-foot-tall, neon-yellow-green plastic figures vaguely shaped like kids. They hold a triangular orange flag with the words “KIDS AT PLAY” printed in black. The color of these signs match the orange hat that is molded across of the Kids at Play Figures’ plastic heads. Across the figures’ hips, the word “SLOW” is printed and shines under a red reflector. Kids at Play Figures have no nose, no cheeks, and no chin, and instead only have round, bulging black eyes and gaping empty mouths. The figure Chief Montgomery finds is taller and oddly contorted.

The figure is part of the Freddy Fazbear Public Safety Initiative, created to deter reckless drivers in areas where kids are running around on roads. It punishes reckless drivers who don't listen to the sign and hit a kid by taking control of their body at some point afterwards, bringing them to the site of the collision, and transforming them into another "Kids at Play" figure.

entities.name: Minor Characters
entities.description:
This is a list of minor characters in Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit.

A woman who angrily talks on the phone on Night Two, and has musophobia. She complains about the length of time it takes to get her pizza, and says she hears rats in the walls. She worries if the cooks may be rats, and Oswald says that she seems distracted and paranoid. In order to cause a distraction, Oswald steals a rat from the past and releases it near the Enraged Customer. She screams, cries, and panics, as Jeff runs to fight the rat with a newspaper.

On Night Three, a man is seen sitting at a table. He remarks that the town used to "really be something," but now it's a dump, and he'd get out of town if he could find any work.

A woman eating at Jeff's Pizza on Night Three. She remarks that the pizza used to be better in the old days, but Jeff made it cheaper, so "quantity over quality."

entities.name: Trash and the Gang
entities.description:
are a series of poorly-made "animatronics" built from mundane everyday objects. They first appeared in Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator.

Bucket Bob has multiple wooden broomsticks connected with tight ropes. He has a silver bucket for a head with a scribbly-drawn face on it and has hands which are just two blue-turquoise checkered oven mittens.

Mr. Can-Do has a silver-colored trash bin for a body, with a pinkish-red balloon with a smiley face drawn on it for his head. He has also two wooden bars which acted as hands or supporters.

Mr. Hugs is a teal-shaded vacuum cleaner bot which has two silver poles, which is connected to the handle with two white plastic arms, two plastic googly eyes with a brown bag connected at the vacuum cleaner.

entities.name: 8-Bit Fredbear
entities.description:
is an 8-bit rendering of Fredbear in FNaF World. He only appears if the player idles instead of clicking "DONE" at the end of Fredbear's dialogue. He tells the player to find the clocks in order to get a special ending.

8-Bit Fredbear is identical to his Five Nights at Freddy's 4 and Sister Location counterparts, but appears to be pixelated and his eyes are black with yellow dots for pupils. The way he is animated is very glitchy, with his right foot and arm, left hand, and both ears splitting out, similar to RWQFSFASXC from the "Glitch Minigame" in the third game of the core series.

8-Bit Fredbear tends to use figurative language as he speaks.

entities.name: Adventure Balloon Boy
entities.description:
, commonly referred to as Adventure BB, is an unlockable character in FNaF World and minor character in the Gravity Vortex, Lemonade Clown, and Fruit Punch Clown minigames in Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator.

Balloon Boy has an almost identical appearance to his counterpart from the main Five Nights at Freddy's series, but is smaller and cuter. All of his distinct features remain, such as the red-blue vertically striped shirt, two white buttons, propeller cap, blue pants, and brown shoes. He doesn't carry the "Balloons!" sign from his original appearance, and his hair color has been brightened. His eyes aren't as round as his original counterpart, and he has a bigger smile than usual.

Balloon Boy relies on attacking groups of enemies. His Balloons is mainly useful to one enemy as it summons 3 Balloons to random targets. Each Balloon can do random damage from weak as 1 damage to huge as around 100. Because of these numbers, Balloon Boy does not do too much damage on bosses, so be careful. Hot Cheese and Munchies are useful on groups of enemies.

entities.name: Adventure Bonnie the Rabbit
entities.description:
is one of the starter characters in FNaF World, and is one of the selectable protagonists in the troll game FNaF World: Halloween Edition.

Bonnie is a blue-colored rabbit animatronic with magenta eyes, appearing as a smaller version of his counterpart from the Five Nights at Freddy's series. He wears a red bowtie and carries a red V-shaped guitar. He also has two buck teeth, like his Toy counterpart.

Bonnie's overall character focuses on crowd control. All of his attacks can hit multiple targets, whether his allies (Happy Jam) or his foes (Bite and Bash Jam). His move, Bite, focuses damage on one or two (occasionally 3) with relatively low damage. It is more powerful than Bash Jam, as it focuses on limited targets, but it is not as powerful as the average 1-target attack due to its possibility of hitting multiple enemies. It's best for finishing off those last one-or-two enemies quickly. However, if you're feeling lucky, you can try your hand at using it at a group of three or more enemies to deal significant damage. Bonnie's second attack has less of a spin on chance. It deals low damage to each of the enemies, lower than Bite. If you're not doing very well, it's safer to use this to weaken all of the enemies, rather than to focus all your power into one or two. His third move, Happy Jam, heals your party members and lets them fight for longer. Use Bonnie sparingly in the later game, as there are better alternatives available.

entities.name: Adventure Chica the Chicken
entities.description:
is one of the starter characters in FNaF World, and is one of the selectable protagonists in the troll game FNaF World: Halloween Edition.

Chica is a yellow-colored chicken animatronic with purple eyes, appearing as a smaller version of her counterpart from the core game series. She wears a bib reading "LET'S EAT!!!" and carries a plate with a pink cupcake. She also sports two buck teeth and has three toes instead of two, unlike her counterpart from the first game. Another difference is that there are no white claws on her feet, again unlike the counterpart. She also lacks eyebrows. Like Adventure Toy Chica, her cupcake has blue eyes. Also unlike the her core series counterpart, Chica has a set of eyelashes, much like the rest of Chica's counterparts in FNaF World.

Chica revolves solely around healing and is great for the beginning part of the game. She's an average addition to the party for the first quarter of the game, but can be easily replaced with better counterparts like Adventure Withered Chica. Cupcake and Regen Song are great healing moves for the start of the game but Party Favors is a very lackluster move and deals little damage and little healing, so when starting a new game Adventure Toy Chica would be better, seeing that she can heal, buff up teammates and has Waterhose, which kills all enemies under 30% health. As soon as a new character is unlocked, the player should replace her with them, and try and get a Medpod, so that they do not have to rely on healing as much.

entities.name: Adventure Endo-01
entities.description:
is one of the playable characters in FNaF World.

Endo-01 has mostly the same appearance as his core series counterpart except smaller and with a red button on the torso.

Endo-01 is a huge companion for a supporting character. His newest attacks; Power Song and Armor Song can increase Attack or Defense to all characters for one turn.

Endo-01 also has an attack that can summon an Endo Army, which can deal damage to enemies over time (around 30 seconds) which can deal roughly around 200-500 damage for each shot each endoskeleton randomly shoots.

entities.description:
is an endoskeleton and one of the unlockable characters in FNaF World.

Endo-02's has almost an identical appearance to its counterpart from Five Nights at Freddy's 2 but smaller and "cuter." The wires from its core series character are missing, and the endoskeleton frame is much simpler.

{| class="article-table" border="0" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="1" style="width: 55%;"

Endo-02 is a really good character by itself. It has Speed Song which can increase the speed for all characters for 1 minute (useless if using a Speed Chip). Like Adventure Endo-01, it can also summon endoskeletons using Endo Army to deal huge damage to enemies over time.

entities.name: Adventure Endoplush
entities.description:
is one of the unlockable characters in FNaF World.

Endoplush is a very small endoskeleton, with a pair of green eyes and a pair of small antennae from the top of its head. It also has a green button on its chest.

Endoplush is an interesting character to use. Like Adventure Withered Bonnie, he has Eye Beam, which can do a wide range of damage to an enemy in front of it, usually ranging from 100 to 1200. In order for Eye Beam to be effective, try to play Endoplush in the 3rd spot in the party to ensure it hits a target.

Like Adventure Endo-02, he has Neon Wall, which is important for the final boss or glitched worlds, as it blocks the Alarm attack used by the final bosses and the glitched enemies. Neon Wall also raises the characters defenses, blocking 50% damage for thirty seconds.

entities.name: Adventure Foxy the Pirate
entities.description:
, also known as Baron Foxy in Foxy Fighters, is one of the starter characters in FNaF World.

Foxy is a red-colored fox animatronic with orange eyes, appearing as a smaller version of his counterpart from the main series. The holes on his body are noticeably gone and he also lacks eyebrows and freckles. Similar to his core series counterpart, Foxy has three stray tufts of fur sticking out of the top of his head and similar to Phantom Foxy from Five Nights at Freddy's 3, his eyepatch doesn't flip up.

Foxy isn't the strongest starter in the game, but he is great as a supportive attacker. Hook does very little damage but has minor helpfulness at the start of the game. His best attack in the game is Jumpscare, which is great for stunning, although it does no damage, and Hot Cheese is great for damage over time. He's an OK starter character, but can be replaced with better characters like Adventure Mangle. If the player wants to use him, they should be sure to put stronger supporting characters in their party.

entities.name: Adventure Fredbear
entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World. He is a guide who explains how the game works as the player progresses through it.

Fredbear is a golden-colored animatronic bear, with cyan eyes, wearing a purple bowtie and a top hat, appearing as a smaller version of his counterpart from the Five Nights at Freddy's 4 minigames. Also, if one looks closely, he lacks some joints (such as his kneecaps), and unlike his core series counterpart, he has two buttons and only four fingers.

Fredbear is a powerful and helpful character. His Mega Bite can deal large amounts of damage, making him useful at attacking groups of enemies, and Mimic Ball helps by doubling the attack. Mimic Ball is also great as it helps out the party and stays for up to twelve uses. Regen Song makes the party's health regenerate over time, making Fredbear a good healer as well. Fredbear is an all-around character being very strong and assists the party.

entities.name: Adventure Freddy Fazbear
entities.description:
is the titular protagonist and one of the starter characters in FNaF World, and is one of the selectable protagonists in the troll game FNaF World: Halloween Edition.

Freddy Fazbear is a brown animatronic bear with blue eyes, appearing as a smaller version of his counterpart from the Five Nights at Freddy's series. He wears a black top hat, and carries a microphone in his right hand. He has two buttons on his chest, unlike his main series counterpart.

Freddy is a great starting character both for offense and buffs. It is recommended to use Birthday as his first move, as this will raise the stats of the entire party. A well-timed Birthday can pull a losing team out of impending doom. Mic Toss is recommended when quickly finishing off a single enemy is necessary, but it is most useful for a starting player who has not made it to Choppy's Woods. Pizza Wheel deals relatively decent damage to enemies, having a chance to deal damage up to six times for each enemy. It is a very powerful move for starting players, and with characters that apply debuffs/damage over time (e.g. Adventure Foxy) can easily drain the HP of groups of enemies. It is not recommended for use at the very beginning, as its starter damage is considerably low in comparison to Mic Toss.

Because of the stronger enemies and limited attacks, however, Freddy is not recommended for the later part of the game.

entities.name: Adventure Funtime Foxy
entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World, and the intact version of Adventure Mangle.

Funtime Foxy is a fox animatronic with the majority of its fur colored white. It has a pink snout with a small black nose, three small fluffs of fur on top of its head, pink toes and stomach, pink markings inside its ears and around its eyes and midriff, and at the tip of the tail. It has bright red cheeks and red lipstick on its snout, long eyelashes, a red bow tie, and wears a hook on its right hand. It has minor endoskeleton pieces exposed, such as the "kneecaps," which have no costume, despite other animatronics having these parts.

{| class="article-table" border="0" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="1" style="width: 55%;"

Funtime Foxy was one of the best characters before Update 2. Happy Jam 2 is the best healing attack in the game. Gift Boxes are very useful for resurrecting your party members with full health. Cosmic Song is an attack that should deal a rather boss amount of damage.

entities.name: Adventure Golden Freddy
entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Golden Freddy is a golden-yellow-colored variant of Adventure Freddy, using the almost exact same model, albeit with different coloring and eyes being a bit smaller, as well as being in a slouched, sitting position; similar to his counterpart from the first Five Nights at Freddy's. Golden Freddy has a black top hat, one button on his chest and a microphone in his right hand. He seems to be lacking a bowtie, due to his lower jaw covering the majority of his chest. He has black eyes with glowing white pupils.

Golden Freddy is a good support character, but not great. Jumpscare and Haunting can stun enemies and delay their attacks, which can be useful, and Rainy Day 2 decreases the defense of enemies and damages them. Combined with other characters, Golden Freddy can be a good character, but on his own, he's not very good.

Haunting is really useful against single targets as it has double the duration of jumpscare and it can even work on bosses (even if the boss is moving, it won't attack for a couple of seconds). Therefore, he is really useful to bring against bosses or groups of enemies.

is an unlockable character in FNaF World. He can be unlocked by beating FNaF 57: Freddy in Space with at least one, but not all, cupcakes collected.

Jack-O-Bonnie is a re-skin of Adventure Nightmare Bonnie to resemble his appearance in Five Nights at Freddy's 4: Halloween Edition. He is a brownish-orange color with hollow eyes and an orangish-yellow glow emanating from him, in a similar fashion to a jack-o-lantern.

entities.name: Adventure JJ
entities.description:
, also known as Adventure JayJay in full, is an unlockable character in FNaF World and minor character in the Gravity Vortex minigame in Freddy Fazbear's Pizzeria Simulator.

JJ seems to have the appearance that acts as a recolor to Adventure Balloon Boy, with her eyes pink, hat and shirt in a blue and pink pattern, and her nose and cheeks in a pink color. Her eyes also sports with eye-lashes. The stem from the hat is noticeably gone. JJ's shirt has two golden-yellow buttons. JJ's mouth is different compared to Adventure Balloon Boy's. Her mouth is more like a trapezoid while Adventure Balloon Boy's mouth is more like a semicircle.

JJ is an interesting party member to use. Like Adventure Balloon Boy, she has Balloons that can do random damage from low as 1 to as high like 100. She can also use Poppers early which can do some big damage to enemies although it ranges from 50-150. Her best attack that she has is Unscrew as it has a 1/3 chance to destroy a single target. It also works on bosses, but the chances are much lower. This is also useful against new challengers that appear as the player can defeat them quickly to obtain new party members.

is a NPC in FNaF World. They are the owner of Lolbit's Byte Store and appears in several locations throughout the game, each one selling all three tiers in a set of Bytes.

Lolbit is a recolor of Adventure Funtime Foxy, with most of their body colored white, a purple bowtie and cheeks, and black eyes with white pupils. The hook remains unchanged, save for the fact that it is on the opposite hand.

entities.name: Adventure Mangle
entities.description:
is one of the starter characters in FNaF World, and the mangled version of Adventure Funtime Foxy.

Mangle is almost identical in appearance to its core series counterpart, except for the fact that it is quite smaller. It has a left eye, switched from its core-series version (where it has its right eye intact). Its right eye is seen on its endoskeleton head, a similar switch from its core series version. It wears a red bow tie, and possesses three legs similar to its Five Nights at Freddy's 2 version. It also has three white tufts of fur on its head, a contrast to the original, which had none.

Mangle is a decent party member to have in the party. It is recommended to use Poppers early in order to damage weak enemies or bosses as soon as enough Poppers are set. Prize Ball is also useful, as it can have a chance to heal or release a random Basic Attack. Hook is relatively weak, but is recommended to use to finish off a single weak enemy.

entities.name: Adventure Marionette
entities.description:
, also referred to as Adventure Puppet, is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

The Marionette has a very similar appearance to his counterpart from the core series, being smaller, having slightly thicker limbs, and a rounder mask. He appears to have stumps at the end of his legs. He also has fewer stripes than the Marionette from the core series, having a total of twelve instead of twenty-eight.

Marionette's only attack that deals damage is Prize Ball 2, which deals a randomly selected attack. The "esc" key is good against groups of difficult enemies. If the party is about to be destroyed, players can use Mystery Box to randomly select party members to assist during battle.

entities.description:
is one of the unlockable characters in FNaF World.

Nightmare looks almost identical to his core series counterpart, but smaller and glossier. He is simply a recolor of Adventure Nightmare Fredbear, with the fur colored black, the bowtie and hat colored yellow, and the stomach, along with the inside of his ears, colored gray. Like many of the other Nightmares, he has claws and tears on his body. His eyelids appear to be lowered, giving him an angry look. He also lacks the transparency his core version has, as well as the black stripe that appears on his hat.

Nightmare is very powerful to use. Like Adventure Nightmare Fredbear, he has Toxic Bite 2, which can poison and damage a target and others nearby. They also share Mega Bite, which does more damage to groups of enemies than Toxic Bite 2 without inflicting poison.

In addition, Nightmare also has Rainy Day 2, which can do lots of damage to all enemies as well as lowering their defenses.

is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Phantom Foxy's appearance is almost identical to his core series counterpart but he is smaller. Like the other Phantoms, his eyes are white dots surrounded by white rings. Similar to his core series counterpart, his right forearm is absent, with his remaining upper right arm attached, albeit being more tattered and possessing more wires than his core series counterpart. In addition, his body is completely covered in red and brown stripes.

Phantom Foxy is a fairly decent character. Like Adventure Foxy, he has Jumpscare, which can stun enemies for a bit. He can also poison enemies with Toxic Bite, dealing damage with the initial bite as well. Unscrew is good in certain situations, having a 30% chance of an instant kill to one enemy. Overall, Phantom Foxy is a good character for the early part of the game.

entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Phantom Freddy's appearance is almost identical to his core series counterpart but smaller. Like most of the Phantoms, his eyes are big white dots with single white rings around them. His left ear has been completely removed, replaced by wires. Aside from his missing ear, Phantom Freddy is completely intact.

Phantom Freddy is a great character for giving enemies status effects, as his entire arsenal of attacks is just status effect moves like lowering Attack, Speed, and Defense from enemies, each of them can last around 1 minute when used. However, this makes Phantom Freddy incredibly useless in combat, as none of his attacks deal any damage at all. Because of this, try to use him as a supporting party member while the player should bring other strong party members such as Adventure Withered Bonnie or Adventure Nightmare Freddy. He is also useful for lowering an enemy's attack status effect in Hard Mode.

entities.name: Adventure Phantom Mangle
entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Phantom Mangle's appearance is almost identical to their core series counterpart, but it is smaller. Like most of the Phantoms, its eyes are white dots surrounded by a single white ring. The same goes for the endoskeleton head. It looks identical to Adventure Mangle in design, similar to its core series counterpart, albeit with a charred and ghostly look to it.

Phantom Mangle is more powerful than Adventure Mangle, and a good character to use throughout most of the game. Its best attack is Pizza Wheel 2, as it deals large damage over groups of enemies. Toxic Bite can damage a few enemies as well as inflicting poison on them, being a relatively good attack. Mystery Box swaps the player's party members for random party members, even ones that the player has not obtained yet. While this can be good in a pinch, it is a luck-based attack, and is risky to use, as it can often give the player an unbalanced or below-average party.

entities.description:
, also commonly referred to as Adventure Phantom Puppet, is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Phantom Marionette's appearance is almost identical to its counterpart from the core series but it is smaller. Oddly enough, it possesses many short-looking teeth and has rosy cheeks, white, unburned buttons, and tear-stripes don't look burnt at all. Like the other Phantoms, its eyes are just one big white dot containing a white ring around it.

Phantom Marionette is more useful to bring as its attacks are quite powerful. It can stun groups of enemies with Jumpscare as well as doing high damage to enemies using Hot Cheese 2.

It also has Mystery Box 2 as unlike the first Mystery Box, it has a more chances to swap for new and better party members that can include Adventure Springtrap and above. This will also prevent the starting party members to be summoned so the party won't be weaker, unlike Mystery Box 1.

is an unlockable character of FNaF World.

Plushtrap is a neat character to use as he has attacks that rely on poisons and slowing down enemies. His sludge can lower the enemies' speed while Bad Pizza can do huge damage to all enemies as well as poisoning them. Toxic Bite is weaker than Bad Pizza but it is more quicker to attack than Bad Pizza that takes time.

entities.name: Adventure RWQFSFASXC
entities.description:
, shortened to Adventure RXQ and commonly referred to as Adventure Shadow Bonnie, is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

RWQFSFASXC's appearance is almost identical to his counterpart from the core series but he is slightly smaller and his teeth are different. RWQFSFASXC is nothing more than a silhouetted Shadow version of Adventure Toy Bonnie with glowing white eyes and teeth.

RWQFSFASXC is a very good support character to have in any party. Even though he cannot do any direct damage his Gift Boxes ability can revive fallen allies and his Mimic Ball can copy Attacks, including Gift Boxes. His Haunting Ability can temporarily freeze an enemy giving the player's party an advantage, especially on some bosses that attacks fast like Supergoon.

When using RWQFSFASXC, the player should use Gift Boxes at the start of a battle (the Auto:Gift Boxes chip is also recommended). After Gift Boxes is used, Mimic Ball can be used to double every attack and can help stack Gift Boxes. Use Gift Boxes again if a party member has fallen and use Mimic Ball again if it's gone. With Mimic Ball and Gift Boxes already set, the player can then use Haunting to temporarily freeze enemies, giving the player's party an advantage.

entities.name: Adventure Shadow Freddy
entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Shadow Freddy's appearance is almost identical to his core series character from Five Nights at Freddy's 2, but he is smaller. The inside of his mouth appears to have red lining, although it is shown to contain black in most images of the core series.

Similar to Shadow Freddy's core series Five Nights at Freddy's 2 counterpart, he shares the same model with Adventure Golden Freddy, although he is recolored in dark purple. His FNaF World appearance still holds as such, and like the original games, is shared with Adventure Phantom Freddy. However, unlike his core series counterpart, he doesn't have wires hanging from his right eye. Also, he is shown standing up, unlike his core series counterpart, who is sitting in a slumped position, similar to Adventure Golden Freddy. His attack animation shows him leaning forth and spinning his head once, counter-clockwise.

With Shadow Freddy as a party member, bringing additional party members with powerful attacks is a must, as none of Shadow Freddy's attacks can deal damage, and heavily rely on luck to even work. Esc Key is useful against groups of enemies, even though it has a 15% hit rate. On the other hand, Unscrew has twice as much of a chance to hit as Esc Key, but can only hit one target.

entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Spring Bonnie is an animatronic rabbit with green eyes, appearing as a smaller version of their counterpart seen in the Stage01 minigame from Five Nights at Freddy's 3. They have a gold tone and wear two purple buttons and a purple bow tie. They also have eyelashes, much like the Toy animatronics in Five Nights at Freddy's 2.

Spring Bonnie is incredibly strong, and was probably the best character in the game before Update 2. They focus mainly on massively damaging foes and have one very good heal move: Happy Jam 2. This makes Spring Bonnie incredibly varied with their move pool. Cosmic Song and Springlocks do a heavy amount of damage to groups of enemies, while Happy Jam 2 is one of the better heals in the game and increases the Speed of allies.

Grouped with a character who uses Mimic Ball, Spring Bonnie is a very good addition for the team for racking up damage and healing if needed.

entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Springtrap is an olive rabbit animatronic with gray eyes, appearing as a smaller version of his counterpart from the Five Nights at Freddy's series. He has several holes and wires poking out, and wears a single button. He also wears the large portion of his ear that was once gone from the original game. The innards of William Afton inside him are noticeably missing. He also has four fingers, rather than five. He bears regular animatronic feet, while his original counterpart had bare endoskeleton feet from the shin down.

Springtrap is a good character, mainly useful for damaging enemies. Bite 2 can do solid damage, while Rainy Day helps the party members by lowering all the enemies' defenses.

His best attack is Springlocks, which can do 100 to 1500 damage to an enemy and other nearby. This makes Springtrap a very powerful character to use, as a hard hitting character is required in the team. However, Adventure Spring Bonnie makes a great alternative.

entities.description:
is one of the starter characters in FNaF World.

Toy Bonnie's appearance is almost identical to his core series counterpart, but he is smaller and has a much rounder head. He bears a red bowtie, cheeks, and guitar. Most of his body is a light blue color, excluding the white highlights he has, such as his white stomach, chin, snout and paw highlights. He also has purple eyeshadow and small eyelashes.

Toy Bonnie is a good starter character, mainly focusing on attacking. Bash Jam and Munchies deal good damage for the start of the game, while Prize Ball can do some healing moves, if lucky. If the Prize Ball did not give out the healing move, it's very likely that the party get an attack, like Munchies, from it instead. Toy Bonnie is great but can easily be replaced with other characters later in the game.

is one of the starter characters in FNaF World.

Toy Chica is almost identical to her counterpart from the core game series but she is smaller. She is a yellow chicken with cyan eyes. She wears neon pink shorts along with a bib displaying text reading "LET'S PARTY!" Toy Chica's lower legs and feet are colored orange, although her core series counterpart has only her feet colored orange. She also lacks eyebrows and has pink eyeshadow.

Toy Chica is a good backup character to bring in the party. Like Chica, she can use Cupcake to heal up the party, but the ones can also boost the party stats using Birthday for a short time. Waterhose is also really useful to bring in order to destroy enemies quickly that has taken severe damage. The ones can use Toy Chica in the later game, but be sure to bring other strong supporting party members in order to provide help.

is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Withered Chica's appearance is almost identical to her core series counterpart's, but she is smaller. Her jaw is completely unhinged and her arms appear to be permanently outstretched, similar to her counterpart's arms. Her hands are missing entirely, with wires protruding from her wrist stumps. There's also a lack of toenails from Chica's feet. Unlike her core series counterpart, she has no rips on her body whatsoever.

Withered Chica is similar to Adventure Toy Chica in that she acts as a supporting character. Like Adventure Chica and Adventure Toy Chica, her Cupcake can heal up all party members. Prize Ball 2 is useful as it unleashes a random strong attack such as Freddles, Pizza Wheel 2, or Waterhose 2. Seeing as Withered Chica can be obtained relatively early in the game, it is good to have stronger, end-game attacks early on, making Prize Ball 2 a good option.

Bite inflicts only small damage to an enemy, being considerably weaker than some of the moves that can be used via Prize Ball 2.

entities.description:
is an unlockable character in FNaF World.

Withered Foxy's appearance is almost identical to his core series counterpart's, but he is smaller, tattered, and in even worse condition. He has a major tear on his chest, along with a few holes on his arms and upper legs. He has a large hole at the left side of his head, which removes the fur off his left ear and reaches down to his eyebrows, exposing part of his left eyeball.

Withered Foxy isn't as useful to bring but still better than Foxy. Unlike Adventure Foxy, he does not have Jumpscare and most of his attacks are slightly weak. Hook does really small damage, which isn't that useful against a strong enemy or groups of enemies.

His only usefulness is Rainy Day which can lower the enemies' defenses as well as Hot Cheese 2, which can do massive damage to enemies over time. Because of this, if the ones are using him, treat him as a supporting character while the ones bring strong party members like Adventure Marionette or Adventure Nightmare Freddy.

entities.description:
is an unlockable titular character in FNaF World.

Withered Freddy is similar in appearance to his core series counterpart, although he is much smaller and appears to have darker fur. Unlike the other Withered animatronics, Withered Freddy does not have many rips and tears on his body, only having one major rip on his left thigh. In addition, he has some wires poking out from his suit in a few places on his body. He has gray-ish pupils that appear to be glowing white, albeit faintly. His attack animation shows him leaning forward and enlarging his head.

Withered Freddy is a decent character, working best as support. Mic Toss is his only actual attack move, although it is fairly weak and overshadowed by other stronger moves that the player should have access to by the time they unlock Withered Freddy.

However, Withered Freddy can lower enemies' attack with Gloom Song, although this is only temporary.

Dee Dee is a humanoid-looking animatronic. She is similar to BB and JJ. She has purple pants, a yellow and pink pattern on her shirt and hat, light brown hair, green eyes, pink cheeks, a large, pink propeller on her beanie and a single large dark-violet button on the shirt.

She is a recolor of Adventure JJ, but with only one big button on her chest instead of two, and the ball on top of her propeller being much bigger.

is an endoskeleton exclusive to FNaF World. It is the owner of Mendo's Endo-Upgrades, a store located in Fazbear Hills that sells items which raise the player's party defense.

Mendo's appearance appears to be a blue recoloring of Endo-01 but has some notable differences. It has bigger arms, a yellow/orange antennae, a green button on its chest, and black eyes with yellow pupils.

entities.name: Virtua-Freddy
entities.description:
Virtua-Freddy is a secret character in FNaF World. Unlike the rest of the characters, he is unplayable and only appears in the "Mimic Ball" attack.

Virtua-Freddy's appearance seems to be oddly similar to Freddy Fazbear's, but his entire body is changed into a green wireframe with his endoskeleton visible inside. Some parts of his body are incredibly hard to see, like his hat.

Virtua-Freddy does not have a standard set of attacks. Instead, he is summoned by the Mimic Ball to use the most recent attack used by the player. If Mimic Ball is used while a Mimic Ball is already out, the current Mimic Ball will be replaced and Virtua-Freddy will not copy the attack. Also, Virtua-Freddy cannot copy the "Mystery Box" and "Mystery Box 2" attack. Other than this, he has the ability to perform any attack that the rest of the player's team has.

entities.name: Bonnie the Rabbit
entities.description:
Bonnie the Rabbit is a major antagonist of Interactive Novel #1: The Week Before and a minor character in Interactive Novel #2: Return to the Pit. He is the guitarist at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza.

Bonnie appears identically to his other iterations, being a six-foot-tall blue rabbit animatronic with a red bow tie. His eye sometime turn into a glowing red. He appears to have another set of teeth deep inside his maw ressembling human teeth, which are either the remain or a ghostly manifestation of the remain of Jeremy, the child inside of him.

Bonnie debuts on stage with Freddy and Chica before quickly leaving alongside with Chica.

IF YOU CHECK THE CAMERAS AGAIN- Ralph monitors the security cameras to track the animatronics’ movements before considering leaving the office. When checking the other feeds, Ralph realizes that Bonnie is missing from his usual post. He locates the blue rabbit animatronic in the West Hall, heading directly toward the Security Office.

entities.name: Chica the Chicken
entities.description:
Chica the Chicken is a major antagonist in Interactive Novel #1: The Week Before and a minor antagonist in Interactive Novel #2: Return to the Pit. She is one of the entertainers at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza.

Chica's appearance is similar to her game counterpart, being a six-foot-tall yellow animatronic chicken. Chica is bulky with thick black eyebrows, purple eyes, and a beak with teeth. She wears a white bib that reads "LET'S EAT!!!".

At the start of his first night shift, Ralph familiarizes himself with the security office. He uses the control panel to cycle through camera feeds, beginning with the show stage. His pulse quickens when he notices that Bonnie and Chica are missing, confirming that the footsteps he had heard earlier were theirs. Before he could finish locating the two animatronics, another urgent matter arises: the lights in the men's restroom are out. Realizing this is a task he cannot postpone, Ralph makes it his first mission to replace the bulbs before his shift ends.

GAME OVER- If Ralph attempts to cross the dining area to reach the men's restroom, he quickly discovers how dangerous the open space can be. The squeaking of his shoes across the red-and-blue vinyl tiles draws attention, and before he can reach safety, Chica ambushes him from behind. The animatronic's powerful yellow arms seize Ralph mid-run, cutting him off before he can react. His bloodcurdling scream echoes through the restaurant, momentarily overpowering the mechanical whir of servos and the sound of bones snapping under pressure.

entities.name: Foxy the Pirate
entities.description:
Foxy the Pirate is a major antagonist in Interactive Novel #1: The Week Before. He is an out-of-order, pirate-themed entertainer at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, held in the Pirate Cove stage.

Foxy is a red, pirate-themed, anthropomorphic animatronic fox with a dilapidated and tattered look. He has two fox-like ears with a lighter red inner ear, three small tufts of hair on the very top of his head, two black eyebrows, yellow eyes, and an eye patch covering his right eye. Foxy has large tufts of hair on the lower sides of his head and a long snout. His lower jaw is separated from his head, allowing for his jaw to freely move in an up-and-down motion. He has a single row of sharp white teeth on his upper and lower jaw and what seems to be a tongue printed on the floor of his jaw. His chest is battered, with a large hole in the center, revealing his endoskeleton; parts of his arms also reveal the endoskeleton underneath, with a sharp, silver hook on his right arm and a fully endo hand on his left. His legs lack the bottom half of his suit, revealing the endoskeleton's legs and feet, with the remains of his brown, pant-like suit being tattered, as if they were ripped off.

Ralph told himself to not forget about Foxy. When checking the cams, Foxy begins behind the curtain of Pirate Cove.

IF YOU CHECK THE CAMERAS AGAIN- Before leaving the office, Ralph checks the security monitors to track the animatronics’ movements. Over in Pirate Cove, a pair of glowing white eyes peer from behind the curtain in Pirate Cove and then blink out.

entities.name: Minor Animatronics
entities.description:
This is a list of minor animatronics and bots from the Interactive Novel series. They have a very small role in the series.

A lone endoskeleton sits on the end of the workbench in the backstage room.

Fredbear was the animatronic mascot of Fredbear's Family Diner, the predecessor to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. Ralph finds a Fredbear's Family Diner ticket on Night 4. On Night 5, if Ralph dials in the code 1-9-8-3 on the phone, he ends up listening to a recording of "The Big Bite" an incident where Fredbear crushed a child's head. On Night 6, Ralph describes one of the Freddy heads in the backstage room as being from "the Fredbear days".

After Oswald sees the bodies of the Missing Children, he can choose to use the exit on his right and run out into the streets. He hears a girl's voice calling for help, and can choose to follow it. The voice leads him to a cellar in the alleyway. As he climbs down the steps, Oswald sees the voice come from a toy doll with a white face, red pigtails and a red dress. Before he can leave, the Yellow Rabbit appears behind Oswald and pushes him down the stairs, cracking his head on the floor. As the rabbit approaches Oswald to attack him, the doll starts laughing in a high pitch louder and louder.

entities.name: Reagent
entities.description:
Reagent is a major antagonist in Interactive Novel #3: Escape the Pizzaplex. It is a S.T.A.F.F. Bot that was created to remove organic matter around Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex using toxic gas.

Reagent is described to be a S.T.A.F.F. Bot with big dark gray metal, blank, buggy eyes and two "arms" that end in nozzles to spray out a toxic chemical within tanks attached to Reagent's back. It has wheels to help it move around the Pizzaplex.

Reagent was made to remove any and all organic matter from the Pizzaplex using a toxic chemical, described to have a sickening, chemical smell, that it has at all times on its back in tanks. Upon spraying at an alive being, it can burn the eyes and throat of whoever gets sprayed, sending them into vertigo and making their arms seemingly feel heavy, inevitably knocking them out for hours or killing them.

entities.name: Very Informative Pig
entities.description:
, also known as VIP, is the main antagonist of Five Nights at Freddy's: VIP.

VIP appears on the cover as a pink cartoon pig with large round glasses, a purple suit jacket, and a purple bowtie with slightly lighter purple polka-dots. However, in the book it describes him as having a black suit jacket with a loose red tie.

VIP presents himself as friendly, helpful, and lonely. He also claims to be able to predict what guests want, such as predicting that Devon should come to the Pizzaplex and that Ike needs to use the restroom. He is also shown rewarding what he deems is a good discovery with a cookie that resembles his own face. "A smart cookie for a smart cookie." He is described as sounding like a "Little kid with a stuffy nose".

VIP initially comes off as quirky and friendly, if a little bossy and cynical. However, he is shown to have a vicious temper and is extremely manipulative. He is willing to lock away Ike for hours (even suggests days) just so he can convince Devon to play along with his game so that he can fabricate reviews and get his VIP program going again.

, also known as VIP, is a digital version of Very Informative Pig that resides in the MOE.

Virtual Informative Pig is much kinder than Very Informative Pig with him trying to help Devon to beat Very Informative Pig.

entities.name: Yellow Rabbit
entities.description:
The Yellow Rabbit is the main antagonist of Interactive Novel #2: Return to the Pit.

As Return to the Pit is an Interactive Novel, there are many possible routes and endings depending on readers' choice. The book's lore is more similar to the Fazbear Frights version than the game, as the Rabbit's attack only occurs over two days rather than five, and the original short's storyline can be followed very closely. The different routes show more of the Rabbit and clues as to how the Pit functions, reveals what happened to Chip in the future, or features the Rabbit actually capturing Oswald.

When Oswald enters the pit, but before The Missing Children Incident, there are a few new routes which feature the rabbit:

Two specific routes can be taken on the first morning where Oswald sees the Rabbit at his breakfast table. In one route, he can refuse to accept the rabbit as his father, throw pancakes at it, and then flee the house. If he goes to a neighbor for help, he finds that the neighbor was replaced by Chica who helps the Rabbit kill him. If he runs down the street, he can either be hit by the Rabbit in a car, or can join up with an adult version of Chip. Chip had heard rumors of the Yellow Rabbit, and has joined a team of vengeful adults who are prepared to finally kill the creature. When going to Chip's hideout, he meets Gabrielle, his daughter, and goes to join the final team meeting, only to find that the team's leader has been replaced by the Yellow Rabbit, and he is the only one who can see it. (Whether this means his father was the team's leader, or that the Yellow Rabbit can replace more than one person at a time, is never specified.) Attempting to call out the replacement will result in Oswald being imprisoned and killed by the Rabbit. Attempting to attack the Rabbit with Gabrielle will result in both of them being killed. If Oswald plays along and follows the group to Jeff's Pizza, the Rabbit bites off Chip's head and starts a gunfight.

entities.name: Amalgamation
entities.description:
The is the merged endoskeletons of Freddy Fazbear, Chica, Bonnie, Foxy, and Golden Freddy.

It was used as a source of remnant by William Afton to experiment on the moving of souls, and is a major protagonist/anti-hero in the third novel.

The Amalgamation is a mass of metal that is a melted, clumpy skeleton of metal bulges and blobs, barely resembling anything at all. It has extensions that can be interpreted as arms and legs, but with no defined mechanism of movement. The Amalgamation has no joints, no muscles, no skin or coverings, just masses of undefined tangles and cords, melted into one another and fused together. Most of it seems fused to the table it lays on, burned and blackened at the edges where it touches it, melting into and seemingly inseparable from it. A leg, finger, and eye socket can be seen in the melted mass. Its center glows orange.

In the graphic novel, the Amalgamation is depicted with the heads of Chica, Bonnie, Freddy Fazbear, and Foxy. Its body is worn and dull-colored, with holes revealing the inner workings featured across the rusted shell. Possibly resulting from the merging of four various animatronics, the Amalgamation features differences in limb design, as its left arm seems to be of Foxy's , while its right Bonnie's. Chica's cupcake is also fused with her head.

entities.name: Baby Crawler
entities.description:
The s are minor antagonists in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Fourth Closet. They serve as the alternate counterparts of the Bidybabs from Sister Location and one of the mascots at Circus Baby's Pizza.

The Baby Crawlers are small, baby-like animatronics made of metal with plastic faces painted like clowns and greatly exaggerated features. One has a round, red nose that covers half its face and a white wig of synthetic curls. Another has a molded smile on its face and a painted red grimace. A third, a red-cheeked, smiling clown with a rainbow-colored wig, has a gigantic spring that replaces the middle of its torso, bouncing up and down each time it moves. All of the crawlers have black eyes, with no iris or pupil. They also have two rows of pointy teeth.

Three different types of Baby Crawlers are first seen in Chapter 12 after Marla and Carlton arrive at Circus Baby's Pizza. They're seen playing on the monkey bars of a jungle gym in the dinning room. The crawlers don't see Carlton and Marla because of the illusionary devices in their ears.

In Chapter 13, Marla and Jessica leads the missing children to the dining room, where two of the Baby Crawlers are still playing on the monkey bars. While they can't see Marla and Jessica due to the devices, they can see the children, as the third manages to bite Alanna. The two on the bars begin to approach Lisa and Ron, and the third corners them. While Marla goes to protect Lisa and Alanna, Jessica picks one up and throws it into a four or five feet deep ball pit. Marla, although hesitant at first, helps. Meanwhile, Carlton encounters a deactivated crawler while crawling through the Hide-and-Seek Hallway.

entities.name: Balloon Boy
entities.description:
Balloon Boy is an animatronic in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Twisted Ones. Unlike in the games, there are multiple Balloon Boys, used to distract Charlie and her friends.

The Balloon Boys are animatronics made to look like little boys selling balloons. With the illusion discs on, they are about four feet tall. The Balloon Boys have round heads and round bodies, with their arms almost as long as their legs. Most wear red-and-blue striped shirts with matching propeller beanies on their heads, but some have different colors. The Balloon Boys are made of plastic, and their faces have triangle noses and cheeks made rosy with two raised dusky pink circles. Their blue eyes are large and wide, and their mouths are open in a grin that bares all their even white teeth. The Balloon Boy’s hands are fingerless balls, each gripping an object. In one they holds a red and yellow balloon nearly half their size on a stick. In the other they raises a wooden sign reading "BALLOONS!"

When the illusion discs are destroyed, the Balloon Boys are revealed to be small wind-up toys.

In the underground pizzeria, Charlie starts feeling dizzy before hearing a voice call out "Hi" and "Hello", and believes at first that the voice was coming from a real child. Charlie moves deeper into the pizzeria and finds a Balloon Boy, who made her scream after it moved toward her. As she tries to find a place to hide, the lights and sounds created by the illusion discs and the environment overwhelm her, making her dizzier. A horde of Balloon Boys then begin swarming Charlie, their appearances altered and distorted by the discs to appear as real children. She is later saved when Jessica, John and Clay Burke find her. Clay shoots the lights that are creating the illusion, reducing the Balloon Boys to plastic animatronics.

entities.name: Bonnie the Rabbit
entities.description:
Bonnie the Rabbit is one of the animatronics in the Five Nights at Freddy's novel trilogy. He is the guitarist of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza created by Henry Emily. He appears an antagonist and supporting character in the first two novels respectively.

Bonnie's appearance is similar to his game counterpart, being a life-size animatronic rabbit about the size of an adult or taller. His body is segmented like an artist’s model, with each limb made of distinct, squarish pieces, separate at the joints. Bonnie has bright blue fur, a squared-off muzzle with a giant permanent smile, and thick-lidded pink glass eyes that are wide and chipped. He also has long ears, large blue paws, large padded feet, and a wide, square face. Bonnie holds a red bass guitar, and around his neck is a bow tie that matches the instrument’s fiery color. A bolt anchors him to the stage.

In The Twisted Ones, Bonnie appears more withered and dirty, as his blue fur is stained and matted. He still holds a red bass guitar in his hand, though it is battered and broken. Half of Bonnie’s bright red bow tie has torn off, giving his face a lopsided look.

Prior to becoming the bass guitarist at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, Henry worked on Bonnie and the animatronics at his home, hanging their suits in the attic. One day, he showed three endoskeletons off to his daughter Charlie, who managed to identify each based on the simplest of features. Once the restaurant was opened by Henry and William Afton in Hurricane, Utah, the town came alive. Bonnie was particularly adored by a little girl named Jessica, who found him to have an understanding look and would discuss her problems with him. When five children disappeared at the restaurant in 1985, it was closed down.

entities.name: Charlie's Project
entities.description:
Charlie's Project is an experimental robot created by Charlotte Emily for her robotics class in college. Consisting of two faces on a length board, her goal was to teach robots natural spoken language by having them listen to people talking around them and to them. While Charlie never managed to get them working properly, components of her experiment would later be used by her friends to sneak past hostile animatronics.

Charlie's project is two mechanical faces held upright on metal structures and attached to a length board. The identical faces are smooth, nearly featureless and made of malleable plastic. They are said to look like unfinished statues, with blind eyes that are only raised bumps in the molded plastic. The faces also have lips that move but never part. At the back of their heads are networks of casing, microchips, and wires. The length board the heads are wired to is a large, black box with knobs and buttons. Charlie’s experiment needs to be plugged in with a cord, and a small black switch activates it. Upon activation, an array of red and green little lights blink and tiny cooling fans start.

While in college at St. George, Charlie works on a project to teach natural spoken language to computers and programming. Using spare parts from her father's house, including Theodore, she creates two plastic faces held upright on metal structures and attached to a length board. There are two components to her project, the first being switches that make them move and talk only to each other. The other component is a repurposed hearing aid that allows the faces to listen to everything around them. This is always on, however they only collect the data and not interact with it. When Charlie isn’t working on them, she covers her experiment with a pillowcase.

One day, Charlie arrives at the dorm a little under an hour before her date with John and decides to work on her project more. Upon activating them, the two faces look at each other with constrained movements and speak a total of six words before stopping. Charlie turns them off and begins adjusting wires until she hears Jessica arriving and quickly covers them with the pillowcase. Jessica convinces her to show off the project, but when she becomes concerned Charlie quickly turns it off again and lovingly replaces the pillowcase. She then explains that she isn't exactly programming the faces to do anything, rather she's helping them learn on their own. When Charlie returns to the dorm to get ready for her date, she glances at the faces under the pillowcase and worries that, like Jessica, John wouldn't understand it if she showed him.

entities.name: Chica the Chicken
entities.description:
Chica is one of the animatronics in the Five Nights at Freddy's novel trilogy. She is the backup singer of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza created by Henry Emily. Chica appears an antagonist and supporting character in the first two novels respectively.

Chica's appearance is similar to her game counterpart, being an animatronic chicken about the size of an adult or taller. Her yellow body is inexplicably covered in fur and segmented like an artist’s model, with each limb made of distinct, squarish pieces, separated at the joints. Chica is bulky with thick black eyebrows, large purple eyes that can glow a harsh yellow or orange, and a beak with teeth. She also has a tuft of feathers that sticks up in the middle of her head and long, orange chicken legs with silver talons on her feet that are inches long and sharp as knives. Chica wears a bib around her neck with the words LET’S EAT! set out in purple and yellow against a confetti-covered background. She also holds out a cupcake on a platter. The cupcake itself is somewhat disturbing, with eyes set into its pink frosting and teeth hanging out over the cake, a single candle sticking out the top.

In The Twisted Ones, Chica appears more withered and dirty with her bib having been torn. The words LET'S EAT!!! have faded with time, along with the damp and mildew of Clay's basement. Chica's cupcake sits alone, a few inches away from her.

Prior to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, Henry worked on Chica and the animatronics at his home, hanging their suits in the attic. One day, he showed three endoskeletons off to his daughter Charlie, who managed to identify each based on the simplest of features. Once the restaurant was opened by Henry and William Afton in Hurricane, Utah, the town came alive. When five children disappeared at the restaurant in 1985, however, it was closed down.

entities.name: Ella
entities.description:
Ella is a humanoid animatronic created by Henry Emily. She resides in one of three closets in Charlotte's room, only coming out when a wheel is turned at the foot of her bed. While Charlie believed Ella was yet another toy made by her late father, she would later uncover the truth behind Ella's creation and learn she's far more complex than initially assumed.

The Ultimate Guide Description: "(Spoilers) A highly complex humanoid animatronic, the youngest incarnation meant to house Charlie's consciousness. After Charlie "grew out" of Ella's size, Henry reprogrammed her as a plaything for Charlie. She occupied a closet, and would exit it on a track to serve tea."

Ella is a child-size animatronic doll standing at 81 centimeters tall with delicate features. She also has shiny, synthetic brown hair and wide, glassy eyes that are said to look realistic. Ella wears a dark, crisp plaid dress and shining patent leather shoes, an outfit identical to one Charlie wore when she was her height. She also holds a teacup and saucer in her tiny hands like an offering, although in The Twisted Ones and The Fourth Closet she holds a tea tray in front of her. Since Ella mostly resides in her closet, she is the most intact of Charlie's toys.

When Ella's illusion disc is turned on, she turns into Charlie at about three years old. She has short, frizzy brown hair and a round face set in a happy smile, with her chubby hands gripping the tea tray.
