entities.name: Foxy the Pirate
entities.description:
Foxy is one of the animatronics in the Five Nights at Freddy's novel trilogy. He is an entertainer of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza created by Henry Emily. Foxy appears an antagonist and supporting character in the first two novels respectively.

Foxy's appearance is similar to his game counterpart. He is a large pirate fox with a rotting eyepatch over one of his plastic silver eyes and a large, sharpened metal hook for a hand. Foxy's narrow, reddish face is a canine rictus with a snout and ghoulish smile. His robotic endoskeleton is encased in hollow body parts matted with dark red fur, but only from the knees up. Foxy's scrappy fur does not sufficiently cover his skull, and there are also areas on his body where the metal is exposed.

In The Twisted Ones, Foxy appears more withered and dirty, with his fur covering ripped in more places. John can see more of his endoskeleton than before.

Foxy resided in his own special party room at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, a popular restaurant in Hurricane, Utah opened by business partners Henry Emily and William Afton. He could be found in Pirate's Cove, which was typically out of order. Henry's daughter, Charlie, was afraid of Foxy however and always hid under the tables. When five children had disappeared at the restaurant in 1985, it was closed down and construction began on a mall. The mall was built over Freddy's but never finished, abandoned for the next ten years.

entities.name: Fredbear
entities.description:
Fredbear is a spring lock suit created and primarily worn by Henry Emily. He was used in Fredbear's Family Diner alongside Spring Bonnie until the restaurant's closure. Fredbear would later be used by William Afton to lure and kill Michael Brooks, who possessed the animatronic.

Fredbear is a yellowish-brown bear nearly identical to Freddy Fazbear, just with yellow fur. When possessed by Michael he seems to be empty, as his jaw hangs open and his eyes are empty except for two tiny glints of light deep within the recesses of its eye sockets. In The Twisted Ones, however, Fredbear is said to have lifeless, shining plastic eyes.

Fredbear was the titular mascot of Fredbear's Family Diner, a small diner in New Harmony, Utah owned by Henry Emily and William Afton. The costumes at the diner were designed to both be worn by others and be used as working animatronics, with mechanisms called spring locks holding back all of the animatronic parts. Henry typically wore the Fredbear costume, dancing and miming along with songs for guests and his own children. On Halloween of 1983, however, one of his children would be kidnapped and killed, leading to the diner's closure.

Two years later, William Afton would lure five children away from Freddy Fazbear's Pizza's dining room and into a small storage room, killing them and stuffing their bodies into the animatronics. One night, he put on the Fredbear suit as the animatronics began to malfunction and approached the table by the stage. William was seen by John and the two briefly made eye contact before John's attention was brought back to the stage when the animatronics onstage stopped moving. William then quickly grabbed a child named Michael Brooks and lured him away, killing him and stuffing him in the Fredbear suit. Michael's disappearance haunts his friends and they all began moving away from Utah, with only Carlton Burke staying in Hurricane. Freddy's also closed down shortly after, with none of the children being found.

entities.name: Funtime Foxy
entities.description:
Funtime Foxy, also known as Mangle, is a minor antagonist in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Fourth Closet.

Funtime Foxy is a glossy Foxy animatronic garishly painted pink and white. It has pointed pink ears, yellow eyes, and painted red circles for cheeks. Funtime Foxy also a red bow tie, and it has metal plates that split away from the center of its torso, arms, and legs.

Funtime Foxy's metal plates lift out, split again, and fold back, leaving only its large, grinning canine head untouched while the rest of its body mangles and transforms into a semi-arachnid form. It has long and multisegmented metal limbs like a spider’s legs, covered in springs and wires. Some limbs have hands, others don’t. Mangle’s head is suspended in the air by rods and beams. It also has a second head, which is a vaguely human, skinless metal skull with a set of yellow eyes connected to the mass by cables and cords. A red bow tie joins their necks.

At some point in time after Funtime Freddy, Funtime Foxy is injected with remnant from the Amalgamation as it is revealed that Susie has some control over it. Mangle/Funtime Foxy first appears at the start of Chapter 13, when it opens the door to the room Jessica and the missing children are being kept it. It peaks its fox head into the room first, then fills the room with its long limbs. Mangle grabs two of the children, Lisa and Jacob, but Jessica manages to free Lisa before it retreats. Jessica and the children are then saved by Carlton and Marla. Carlton gives Jessica his earpiece and she joins Marla in helping the children escape the pizzeria while Carlton goes to save Jacob. As the group walks down the hall, the lights overhead burst and they hear a metallic rattling in the ceiling. Then, Mangle slowly descends from an open duct and the group run away. Lisa, being the smallest, falls behind and Jessica saves her from being grabbed again. Eventually they reach a pair of double doors and Marla jams a sign post into the door handles.

entities.name: Minor Animatronics
entities.description:
This is a list of minor animatronics from the Five Nights at Freddy's novel series, The Silver Eyes, The Twisted Ones and The Fourth Closet. They have a very small role in the series and all their names are undisclosed.

After Charlie's mother left, Henry began building a mechanical toy for her. It was a little dog toy who tilted its head side to side. Once it was finished, it made Charlie happy.

William Afton traps a kidnapped Carlton Burke inside a heavy, barrel-shaped torso of a spring lock suit with wide shoulders. The mascot costume is only a torso and arms that hang limp and empty from the sides. Its head has been removed and set a few feet away on a cardboard box. The costume's fur is dirty and matted, and its presumably bright blue color has faded into a bluish color similar to beige. On the back of the costume is a series of ten leather and metal fasteners. Its species is vague and isn't easily identified.

Graphic Novel #1: The Silver Eyes depicts this animatronic to be slightly based on a beaver. Its head has buck teeth, shorter ears, rosy turquoise cheeks, and darker blue eyebrows. The costume has a large, sky-blue, barrel-esque torso equipped two small buttons on a cyan heart-shaped underbelly. Unlike most spring lock suits, it only has four fingers instead of the usual five.

entities.name: Spring Bonnie
entities.description:
Spring Bonnie is a spring lock suit created by Henry Emily and primarily worn by William Afton. He was used in Fredbear's Family Diner alongside the diner's mascot Fredbear until the restaurant's closure after William used the suit to abduct and kill one of Henry's children. Spring Bonnie would continue to be favored by William and used in his numerous murders until he himself would be killed by the spring locks in the suit, although his death wouldn't last.

Spring Bonnie is a patchwork, ragged yellowish-brown rabbit with a face similar to Bonnie’s, just with yellow fur. He also has lifeless eyes and two rows of horrid and yellow smiling teeth. When William puts the Spring Bonnie costume back on ten years later, it is musty and peeling at the edges of the mouth. The giant, absurd-looking rabbit costume also has big, matted paws and two gaping holes for eyes that are dark and hollow.

In the graphic novel rendition, Spring Bonnie is nearly identical to Bonnie, with gold fur and a red bowtie on his chest.

Spring Bonnie was an animatronic performer at Fredbear's Family Diner, a small diner in New Harmony, Utah owned by Henry Emily and William Afton. The costumes at the diner were designed to both be worn by others and be used as working animatronics, with mechanisms called spring locks holding back all of the animatronic parts. William typically wore the Spring Bonnie costume, dancing and miming along with songs for guests. On Halloween of 1983, however, William put on the suit and made his way to a closet where Henry's children Charlotte and Sammy were sleeping. He looked at the two for a bit before grabbing one of them and taking them away to kill them. This would lead to the diner's closure.

entities.name: Stanley
entities.description:
Stanley is an animatronic unicorn that trundles around on a circular track in Charlie's room. He was one of the many toys built by her father Henry and sat alone in her room for years after his death, becoming damaged by the elements.

The Ultimate Guide Description: "A white unicorn animatronic created by Henry for Charlie. Stanley travels on a track around Charlie's room."

Stanley is a little unicorn made of metal and painted glossy white. He also has bared teeth and shiny brown eyes. Stanley's hooves are attached to grooves in the floor, allowing him to trundle around the room on a circular track. When Charlie returns to her father's house, Stanley’s paint is chipped and peeling. His face has also given over to rust, including on his cheeks and around his lively eyes.

In The Twisted Ones, Stanley has been torn from his track. His legs are twisted and his hooves are missing chunks. Stanley’s missing pieces are still attached to the grooves in the floor.

entities.name: Suicide Bot
entities.description:
The suicide bot is an endoskeleton constructed by Henry Emily to commit suicide. The machine is mentioned in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Silver Eyes and physically appears in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Fourth Closet, where it stands deactivated after having fulfilled its purpose.

The suicide bot is a tall, roughly human shaped endoskeleton with a bare metal face. Its facial features are scarcely formed, crude, and shapeless. They are contorted and almost grotesque with a weeping expression. Its blind eyes are only raised bumps, similar to those on a statue. The back of its skull is open, exposing the circuits, and the rest of its skeletal body is naked metal strung with twisting wires. In its hand is a massive knife, which looks similar to a sword according to John.

In the graphic novel adaptation, the robot heavily resembles Endo-02 with a knife on a ball joint replacing its right hand. In The Fourth Closet graphic novel, however, it instead has two regular hands and carries the knife in its left hand.

Its only function seems to be stabbing someone with its blade when activated. The blade is capable of piercing multiple bodies, seen in The Fourth Closet.

entities.name: Theodore
entities.description:
Theodore is an animatronic rabbit and was the first toy built by Henry for his daughter, Charlotte Emily. He sat alone in Charlie's room for years after Henry's death, becoming damaged by the elements. When Charlie moved to St. George for college, she reclaimed Theodore in order to study him and use his parts for an experiment.

The Ultimate Guide Description: "A small purple rabbit animatronic created by Henry for Charlie. It could wave, tilt its head, and repeat a recording from Henry saying 'I love you, Charlie.' Charlie later takes Theodore apart for her robotics project."

Theodore is a dark purple rabbit the size of a three-year-old child with shining plastic eyes, a cotton-ball tail, a dapper red bow tie, and thin, plush threadbare fur. He also had a button at the base of his neck. When Charlie returns to her father's house, Theodore's front is now gray with age from years of sitting in the sunlight and one of his long floppy ears hangs loose by a single rotting thread, the green plastic of his circuit board visible through the hole. In The Twisted Ones, he gets taken apart and used for Charlie's project.

In The Freddy Files, Theodore is depicted with uneven blue eyes, red cheeks, and a light pink pad on the palms of his hands and feet. He sports a pair of teeth on both his upper and lower jaw, which later becomes chipped due to years of deterioration. The graphic novel uses a similar depiction, although Theodore's fur appears more pink and he only has two front teeth. He's also notably less damaged.

entities.name: Twisted Bonnie
entities.description:
is one of the four twisted animatronics and an antagonist in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Twisted Ones. He is the twisted incarnation of Bonnie, which was created by William Afton to hunt down and kill Charlotte Emily.

Twisted Bonnie is an eight-foot tall misshapen Bonnie. His head is too large for his body, with glowing white-hot eyes. Twisted Bonnie’s mouth has several rows of gleaming teeth. Its normal form without his illusion disc is never described other than being made of plastic.

In the official teasers, Twisted Bonnie is a large, blue-purple animatronic rabbit with an organic-looking body. He sports articulated ears, each split into three segments. His suit is badly damaged, including a massive hole on his chest that exposes his endoskeleton. He also has boils on his arms and legs, spikes protruding from his upper arms, wiry whiskers similar to Nightmare Bonnie, and an additional bottom jaw that is separated into two protrusions sticking out of the bottom of his head. On his hands are hook-like black claws.

Twisted Bonnie, along with Twisted Wolf, first appear in Chapter 13 at the underground pizzeria. The two of them are surrounding Charlie, John, Jessica, and Clay Burke from escaping. William appears and introduces himself as Springtrap, and instructs that he needs something from Charlie, and they'll leave the group unharmed, however the four of them manage to escape, and William orders the animatronics to get them.

entities.name: Twisted Chica
entities.description:
is a twisted incarnation of Chica with an organic look. She is only mentioned in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Twisted Ones.

Seen in LadyFiszi's official artwork, Twisted Chica's grotesque appearance is faintly similar to Nightmare Chica, but with half of every part closely looking organic, mostly colored in yellow sporting small growth-like warts. She has a large, fang-filled orange beak, also sporting toothed maws around the upper part of her body; including the joints of her arms and on the stomach. The upper arms are the same orange as her legs, with fingers sporting razor-sharp talons. Her head has puffier cheeks, pupilless magenta eyes with eyelashes, pink eye-socket areas, and three large sack-like growths from the top of her head acting like her feather tufts. Similar to Nightmare Chica, Twisted Chica wears a torn bib with "LET'S EAT!!!" text.

More sickening parts for her appearance includes a mutated, organic-looking pink cupcake with gnarly teeth merging from the left side of Twisted Chica's head, along with another menacing-looking cupcake attached to the lower right side of her hip which is yellowish-golden in color. Both cupcakes possess lit candlesticks.

Twisted Chica never physically appeared in the whole story of The Twisted Ones. However, the possibility that she may exist was brought up by Charlotte Emily upon finding their hiding place:

entities.name: Twisted Foxy
entities.description:
is one of the four twisted animatronics and an antagonist in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Twisted Ones. He is the twisted incarnation of Foxy, which was created by William Afton to hunt down and kill Charlotte Emily.

Twisted Foxy is made of rusty metal and has lifeless, round plastic eyes. He has no fur, and his face and body is smooth. Twisted Foxy has a short muzzle and oval ears sticking out from the sides of his head. He’s very large, likely reaching eight feet tall when standing. Running down the center of Twisted Foxy’s face is a long, straight split, exposing wires and a line of metal frame. A thick plastic material is stuck to his face in large patches. Twisted Foxy has no tail or other animal appendages. The left side of his skull has been crushed, with insides broken and half the wires torn out. Just behind Twisted Foxy’s left eye, a piece of the casing is missing and a mass of plastic with a tangle of wires running in and out of it can be seen. One of the circuit boards is melted. One of Twisted Foxy’s arms seems fine, but on the other both the shoulder and elbow joints are bent out of shape. His chest opens like an iron gate, its metal pieces sliding out of place to reveal a dark, gaping pit where sharp spikes and spring locks are just barely visible.

Upon activation, Twisted Foxy’s changes forms. His casing appears to have skin and fur, though they are blurry, flickering like a trick of the light. Twisted Foxy's fur bristles and his skin moves as if there is muscle and sinew underneath. Inside Twisted Foxy’s chest cavity is a flat disc, about the size of a half-dollar coin, which emits a high-pitched frequency. It should be noted that the twisted appearance of a twisted animatronic is due to a high-pitched frequency emitted from a disc shaped device attached to the animatronic that was developed by William Afton. This device disrupts the natural processes of the brain causing onlookers to see the illusory twisted appearance or a very pretty version that is described like looking like "candy", based on how they subconsciously view what they are looking at.

In the teaser illustrations, Twisted Foxy looks similar to Nightmare Foxy, in that he has a dark color scheme, glowing eyes and fur covering his left hand, but unlike Nightmare Foxy, Twisted Foxy's snout is intact, and sports less rips overall, but his endoskeleton can still be seen underneath the rips in his suit. His endoskeleton's jaws appear to be more flesh-like as opposed to robotic, his hook is different from the hooks of Foxy's other counterparts, and he has a strange, fungus like material around the handle of his hook. As seen from his Funko plush product, his legs do not seem very different from his classic counterpart.

entities.name: Twisted Freddy
entities.description:
is one of the four twisted animatronics and an antagonist in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Twisted Ones. He is the twisted incarnation of Freddy Fazbear, which was created by William Afton to hunt down and kill Charlotte Emily.

Twisted Freddy's normal appearance is a large, blank figure resembling Freddy Fazbear. He has a large metal face, a protruding snout, two rounded ears on the sides of his head, and a perpetual smile. Twisted Freddy's crude metal frame is covered with a layer of gelatinous plastic, giving it an organic, almost embryonic, appearance. He has no fur, instead having a sleek, smooth, and featureless head. Twisted Freddy has a filthy, battered black top hat. His torso is connected to the head by a wide neck. Twisted Freddy has chest plates, which looks like sharp, uneven metal teeth.

When Twisted Freddy's illusion disc activates, he smooths over, becoming less crude. He has a pitch-black top hat perched on his head and cocked slightly to one side, giant cheeks, and a button nose. Twisted Freddy’s head is lively and full of movement, covered in wavy brown fur and bouncy cheeks. He’s also somewhat disjointed, as though every part of his face is moving independently. Twisted Freddy’s head can fold outward, his python-like jaw making motions of chewing and his cheeks and chin dislocating. His mouth is a vortex of fur, teeth, and wire. He also has claws. Twisted Freddy's mouth is unhinged and swings unnaturally. Towards the end of the story, his shiny blue eyes turn a searing red color.

The interior of Twisted Freddy is large enough to hold an adult inside. The captive's limbs are inside the animatronics'. Springlocks restrain them and attempting to move could set them off, but this can be avoided if the occupant is careful and know what they are doing. The twisted animatronics kill by setting off the springlocks. Twisted Freddy’s eyes can roll fully back and look at his captive.

entities.name: Twisted Wolf
entities.description:
Twisted Wolf, also known as The Wolf, is one of the four twisted animatronics and an antagonist in Five Nights at Freddy's: The Twisted Ones. It was created by William Afton to hunt down and kill Charlotte Emily.

Twisted Wolf is a misshapen wolflike figure with a sleek snout and usually stooped over. When Charlie first encounters it, she finds it in the middle of shifting forms. Twisted Wolf's normal appearance is a tattered metal framework, partly coated in rubbery translucent skin. Its eyes are stark white bulbs. Twisted Wolf's chest splits open with tooth-like ribs folding outward. When its illusion discs are active, it appears as a groomed and agile figure covered in silver hair. Twisted Wolf has a silver wolf's mane that runs over top of its head and down its back. It also has shining blue eyes, claws, and long, silken ears.

In the official teasers, Twisted Wolf is depicted as in the middle of changing forms. The right side of its body more closely resembles a wolf, being very furry and with its silver mane running over the top of his head and down its back, and the right hand and right foot being smaller. The left side however, is more robotic, with a visible endoskeleton, rubbery translucent skin, a wider left eye socket, and spikes protruding from its left arm.

The wolf is first seen by Charlie in Chapter 8. Clay Burke was in his police car along with Charlie, John, and Jessica, who were all taking a nap. He watches from afar the mounds that were made by the twisted animatronics that the teenagers discovered in a women's backyard, as one of them was housed by Twisted Freddy. Tired of waiting, he decides to go and check on the mounds. This awakens Charlie, and she wakes up John and Jessica so they can accompany her. To their surprise, the mounds were gone. Clay runs back to the car, and Charlie tries to catch up but she suddenly hears a high-pitched scream. She then sees the wolf, who stares at her for a moment, then spasmed alarmingly with his chest splitting open. A woman fell from inside him. The wolf then heads into the woods, disappearing into the dark. Clay approaches from behind Charlie and tries to assist the woman, who was still alive, while John and the others get help.

entities.name: RWQFSFASXC
entities.description:
, also known as Shadow Bonnie or RXQ for short, is a mysterious shadow counterpart of Toy Bonnie from the Five Nights at Freddy's series. He first appeared in Five Nights at Freddy's 2.

RWQFSFASXC is a shadowy, silhouetted version of Toy Bonnie with white eyes and teeth. He seems to have a full set of teeth visible, with an additional upper pair as opposed to Toy Bonnie's buck teeth. He also appears to be shorter, and the division of his torso and pelvis is more clearly defined. It is unknown whether or not these differences have any relevance.

Other than appearing as mysterious and mildly ominous, there is nothing major to describe RWQFSFASXC's personality. This is also applied to Shadow Freddy.

entities.name: Shadow Freddy
entities.description:
is a mysterious shadow variant of Freddy Fazbear that appears in the Five Nights at Freddy's series, first debuting in Five Nights at Freddy's 2. His origin is unclear, and his appearances are generally limited to Easter eggs.

Shadow Freddy has exactly the same appearance as Golden Freddy's "withered" appearance from Five Nights at Freddy's 2, albeit being recolored dark purple. Unlike Golden Freddy, he has large glowing bright eyes and teeth.

In Five Nights at Freddy's 3, Shadow Freddy lacks the glowing white effects for his eyes and teeth. Instead, his colors are sickly dark green; comparable to those of the Phantom Animatronics. This, however, could simply be the light of the office reflecting off of him.

Shadow Freddy's demeanor, other than appearing and disappearing randomly was left unexplored in FNaF 2. His ordinary personality reveals to be nothing more than mysterious, dark, and not much is seemingly yet to be known about him.

They are invented and established by robotics industries, mainly Fazbear Entertainment, Inc., Afton Robotics, LLC, and Fazbear Funtime Service.

entities.name: B-7
entities.description:
B-7 is the main antagonist of B7-2, the first story from Tales from the Pizzaplex 8: B7-2. It is a paranormal entity that was detached from the protagonist Billy after the events of B-7, the third story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 2: HAPPS.

B-7 is made up of everything removed from Billy, held together with wires and Billy’s own connective tissue and flesh. This includes tall dark-gray-metal-and-plastic prosthetic arms and right leg and black eyes. B-7 speaks with a damaged synthesizer that was previously in Billy's throat. It has a vaguely human-shaped metal-and-plastic head. Two of the plates that were put in Billy’s cheeks part as it speaks. B-7 bleeds blood and motor oil.

B-7 is an evil entity who wants to reattach himself with Billy or another human body at all costs.

B-7 is the animatronic name Billy gave himself sometime after his 19th birthday. He began to have body parts replaced or removed, replacing some with robotic parts to become more animatronic-like. At the end of the story Billy realizes what he had truly become and regrets everything, running away and hiding in a car in a junkyard. Billy wakes up with the car about to be destroyed.

entities.name: Bobbiedots
entities.description:
The are helper bots that appear in Bobbiedots, Part 1 and Bobbiedots, Part 2 from the fourth and fifth books respectively in the Tales from the Pizzaplex book series. There are two generations of Bobbiedots: the first generation are physical animatronics, and the second generation are holograms.

The Generation 1 Bobbiedots in Abe's apartment are physical animatronics that are now decrepit and scorched. They all have a glowing oval on their forehead with their respective color. They also have wires which connect into the apartment.

The Generation 2 Bobbiedots are holograms and they are pretty similar to the Generation 1 Bobbiedots. They have gray skin and wear a white and gray bell bottom suit with a stripe in their respective theme color. They have a small oval on their forehead in their color. Their facial features are also in their color.

The Bobbidots all reside in the apartments of the Fazplex Tower. They can control all the appliances in the apartment to fit what the apartment owner wants. However, depending on the role they were programmed with, they can also control certain appliances that other Bobbiedots can't. For example, Gemini is in charge of media and entertainment, so she can put on movies in the TV and put music on whenever the owner likes. Generation 1 could control the appliances, but were limited by the wires connected to the apartment. The Generation 2 were holograms that can be used via glass panels on the walls.

entities.name: Bonnie the Rabbit
entities.description:
Bonnie the Rabbit is a minor recurring character in the Tales from the Pizzaplex series and is one of the main mascots of the Freddy Fazbear's Pizza family entertainment restaurant chain.

Bonnie is a large purple animatronic rabbit with lighter highlights on his ears, stomach, paws, and muzzle. He has a red bowtie and carries a red guitar. In the graphic novel adaption of Pressure, Bonnie is shown to be a blue rabbit with white highlights and red eyes.

Bonnie, along with Freddy and Chica, appears in the Freddy and Friends cartoon TV show that Billy watches.

Bonnie appears as, what Luca thinks is, a statue in Urban Legends Role Play Auditorium.

entities.name: Buddytronic Dolls
entities.description:
The Buddytronic Dolls are robotic dolls that are sold at the Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex's Buddytronic Boutique. They are little dolls that you choose the pieces, and a machine makes it for you. They appear in the book Tales from the Pizzaplex 6: Nexie's first story of the same name. Many appear throughout the story.

The Buddytronic Dolls are electronic toys that are able to be customized via a assembly machine in the Buddytronic Boutique. They all have endoskeletons and processors that make the Buddytronic's move (albeit a little awkwardly according to Astrid) and are able to speak to their owners', with no preset lines to repeat over and over again. When idle, they hung limply and sweetly, like a floppy teddy bear or ragdolls in the owner's arms.

Nexie is the main antagonist of main story, she is a broken version of Lexie caused by the glitching Storyteller Tree. She is owned by Astrid Eriksen.

Lexie is a Buddytronic doll created by Astrid. However, the machine malfunctions and instead makes Nexie. Later in the story, Astrid's Farfar buys her a new Lexie, which Nexie mutilates and crushes into pieces.

entities.name: Chica the Chicken
entities.description:
Chica the Chicken is a minor recurring character in the Tales from the Pizzaplex series and is one of the main mascots of the Freddy Fazbear's Pizza family entertainment restaurant chain.

Chica is an anthropomorphic animatronic yellow chicken wearing a white bib displaying the text "LET'S EAT!!!," with confetti scattered around it; and is holding an animatronic cupcake. She has three tuffs of hair on the top of head and the lower half of her legs and feet are colored orange, with her feet being 3-toed. She has red-orange eyes and a yellow beak, unlike her game counterpart, which has an orange beak; though this could be an error made by the artist for Pressure.

Chica is a character in the Freddy and Friends cartoon, alongside Freddy Fazbear and Bonnie.

Chica is one of the several mascot costumes that are in the Urban Legends Roleplay Auditorium. Luca sees several girls arguing over which one of them should be Chica.

entities.name: Delilah the Mermaid
entities.description:
Delilah the Mermaid is an animatronic mermaid, at Freddy's Fantasy Water Park, residing in the park's main attraction, Freddy's Sea Life Mechaquarium. Her role in the Tales from the Pizzaplex story, Submechanophobia, is to act as an introduction to various obstacles Caden the protagonist will face throughout the story. She is also featured on the front cover of the fourth Tales from the Pizzaplex book, and is interestingly the only animatronic in the story to be referred to with gendered pronouns.

Delilah's appearance is described differently in the story to how she is depicted on the front cover of the book.

In the story, she is described collectively with the other underwater animatronics as being old and rundown, with chipped paint, spots of rust and some broken pieces you wouldn't notice at a glance. As an individual, she has tangled, faded red hair that waves in the water, with one eye missing and the black socket it was in left fully exposed. She's also described as having crooked arms, but this may be because she was requiring a motor reset at the time.

On the front cover, she has long blonde hair that's coloured a greenish yellow, with both eyes still present and bright pink. Her humanoid upper body is light blue and her mermaid tail is green with a scaled pattern. Instead of human ears, she has light blue, somewhat see-through fins that match the fins on her lower arms. She appears to have sharp nails, and exposed wiring at some of her joints, with the lower part of her jaw being unhinged, and broken enough that you could mistake her for not having one anymore. There's also several instances of cracks and broken holes in her casing, which is likely a reference to how the underwater animatronics are described in the story. She's decorated with a pearl circlet, seashell, coral and other such ocean based necklaces, and what appears to be small pebbles strung very loosely around her waist, with some gold coins attached like charms on a charm bracelet.

entities.name: DJ Music Man
entities.description:
DJ Music Man is a DJ animatronic from Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex who makes minor appearances in the Tales from the Pizzaplex Series.

DJ Music Man appears in the story Bobbiedots, Part 1 from the book Tales from the Pizzaplex #4: Submechanophobia. He appears in a segment where Abe is training Preston to be a Pizzaplex technician. He is stated to have had an "experimental bouncer mode" which was removed. However, some of the code stayed, causing DJ Music Man to be aggressive, sticking his hand through the restroom door and nearly grabbing Preston.

entities.name: Elizabeth
entities.description:
Elizabeth, also known as One, is one of the main antagonists and twist deuteragonists in Bobbiedots, Part 1 and Bobbiedots, Part 2 in the fourth and fifth books from the Tales from the Pizzaplex series. She is one of the first-generation, also known as gen1, Bobbiedots.

One looks similar to Gemini, with her blue coloring, but damaged and scorched. She is missing an arm and the lower part of her face covering, exposing a blackened-metal, tooth-filled mouth and jaw with scorched, barren metal teeth. One’s remaining arm is missing its white exoskeleton below the forearm, so her remaining hand is nothing but battered, inky metal. Her rubbery black cables emanate from the crown of her head, similar to a topknot ponytail. Both of One’s eyes shine blue, and she has a glowing blue oval on her forehead, just like the gen2 Bobbiedots. Her voice box is damaged.

At the end of the story, Abe manages to find Elizabeth a new arm from the sewers.

While most of One's personality is unknown, she is designed to be protective of the apartment's tenant and of the Fazplex Tower, with the latter overriding the former. When Landon planned to burn down the building, she was forced to turn hostile and kill him.

entities.description:
Foxy the Pirate is a minor recurring character in the Tales from the Pizzaplex series and is one of the main mascots of the Freddy Fazbear's Pizza family entertainment restaurant chain.

Foxy is an anthropomorphic animatronic fox with red fur, an red-orange body, and darker red highlights in his inner ears. He wears an eye patch over his right eye and has a hook in-place of his right hand. He has yellow eyes, three tuffs of hair on the top of his head and on his shoulders, and a few golden teeth.

Appears on the Fast Freddy as a jumpscare in the middle of the rollercoaster.

Luca sees a girl wearing a Foxy costume in Urban Legends Role Play Auditorium. Inside, a Foxy statue, being puppeteer by ropes and pullies, swipes its hook at Maddy.

entities.name: Frank the Diver
entities.description:
Frank is shown very little in the Submechanophobia story. It's only directly described as a vintage diver, with a metal helmet.

As with all of the animatronics of the Mechaquarium, Frank is described as old and rundown, with chipped paint, spots of rust and a few broken pieces you wouldn't notice at a distance. How relevant this particular description is to Frank specifically is unclear, as its physical state is never commented on.

On the first book cover, it retains its book description as it's most likely modelled on vintage diving suits. The suit appears to have a light, washed out brown colour for the fabric, with a brighter, more colourful brown for its gloves. The material appears quite thick, and the gloves have a prominent cuff that seemingly sits a little below its elbows. Its helmet is spherical, the base colour of which is a dark brown. The round window in the front of the helmet has a bronze coloured frame, with a hinge its left side and a screw to fasten it shut on the right. This frame matches the band of bronze that goes around the circumfrence of the helmet through the middle and links up with what appear to be two other windows, one on either side, that have square, metal grates over them. On the left of the helmet with the fastening screw, there's small dots in this metal band, but none on the other side with the hinge. Underneath the glass window on either side are two knobs that look like an arcade game joystick, but with small, thick pieces of metal through the circular end that both curl upwards and away from the window above. They look like they could be intended as something that's turned in order to further fasten the helmet to the wearer.

Around the diver's neck, there's two more bronze bands and the metal from the helmet goes past them a little ways to sit the helmet on Frank's shoulders. Beneath this part of the helmet, is a darker brown metal, that reaches partway down the front of the chest, with more bronze framing it's edges. There are two bronze metal fastenings near the middle of this chest pieces that seemingly connect it to the frame. A brown leather belt-like object is wrapped over Frank's shoulders and cross over the front of the chest, through a bronze, square loop, and curve back towards eachother as they go further down and off the bottom of the image. There's various dots that could represent small holes in this belt, both above and below the loop, but don't go up far enough to reach the shoulder, and are unevenly spaced. A corrugated tube comes down from behind Frank from somewhere above the top boundary of the image, and loops over the shoulders, and reaches low enough down the chest to be level with the loop where the belt overlaps. Finally, this depiction of Frank appears to be wearing a belt of sorts just below the lower boundary of the image due to the solid, boxey pouches that are still visible.
entities.short_description: Frank is shown very little in the Submechanophobia story. It's only directly described as a vintage diver, with a metal helmet.

entities.name: Gemini
entities.description:
Gemini, also known as One, is one of the main deuteragonists and true main antagonists in Bobbiedots, Part 1 and Bobbiedots, Part 2 in the fourth and fifth books from the Tales from the Pizzaplex series.

Gemini is one of the second-generation (also known as gen2) Bobbiedots in the Fazplex Tower. In Abe's apartment, she is in charge of entertainment and media.

Like the other Bobbiedots, Gemini is a holographic girl with gray skin, a large heart-shaped face, arched brows, a large oval spot on her forehead, a large circle on top of her head, and a small protrusion for nose. Her dominant color is bright blue. Gemini's bright blue pigtails resemble streams of light more than actual hair, and her ears are covered in a set of headphones featuring upright antennae that end in glowing little blue circles. She’s as slender as Olive. Gemini has unnaturally large, bright blue, catlike eyes, blue bow-shaped lips, and glowing blue fingertips. She also wears a gray-and-white bell-bottomed bodysuit striped bright blue.

Gemini is shown to be very energetic and has a passion for entertainment and music, with her always suggesting and putting on music whenever Abe is hurt or sad. She is also shown to have a liking to Abe, but it is unknown if it is genuine or just part of her programming.

entities.name: Glamrock Endo
entities.description:
Glamrock Endo is a minor recurring character in the Tales from the Pizzaplex. They are the Endoskeletons of the Glamrock Animatronics.

In the Bobbiedots, Part 2 story, a group of Glamrock Endoskeletons is seen walking through the Sewers of the Pizzaplex. Abe doesn't know if they've hurt anyone.

In the Nexie, Endo Warehouse appears in the story. And at the end of the story, it is implied that Astrid's skin was put over a Glamrock Endoskeleton.

entities.name: Hank the Hammer
entities.description:
Hank, like all underwater animatronics in the Mechaquarium, is described as old and rundown, with chipped paint and rusted spots.

Despite its name, it is not described as a hammerhead shark. Hank is a plain grey in colour, and has a rust spot on its tail in the shape of a hammer. As its size isn't specifically called out, unlike Sly the Shark's and Mac the Muscle's, it can likely be assumed that Hank's size is somewhere inbetween theirs.

Hank does not have a described personality. It is only described as swimming slowly under normal conditions, like all other underwater animatronics.

The name 'Hank the Hammer', was chosen by Roy, an employee at Freddy's Fantasy Waterpark. Despite Hank's name, it is not described as a hammerhead shark, but instead was given the nickname 'the Hammer because of the rusted spot on its tail that is in the shape of a hammer.
entities.short_description: Hank, like all underwater animatronics in the Mechaquarium, is described as old and rundown, with chipped paint and rusted spots.

entities.name: HAPPS
entities.description:
The Helpful Automated Pipe Protection Server, also known as HAPPS, is the titular main antagonist of HAPPS, the second story from Tales from the Pizzaplex 2: HAPPS.

HAPPS is about two and a half feet tall and made of plastic, metal, rubber, and foam. Instead of having legs and feet, he has big black rubber treads that he uses to get around. HAPPS's torso is shaped like an isosceles quadrangle made of gray metal. HAPPS has a couple of small doors in his torso which stores a telescoping extender ending in a curved sponge, which acts as a third arm. Extending from the sides of his torso are articulated gray metal arms with black-and-yellow security stripes painted on his biceps and end in big white foam hands. HAPPS's round plastic white head sits on the short edge of the torso, and on top of it is a flashing yellow security light. While his body appears tanklike, his face is described as having an industrial look with bright yellow eyes, round cheeks painted with black-and-yellow stripes, and a large tilted grin full of big backlit teeth.

When Aiden and Jace kick HAPPS, they crack his face and snap his arm joints, leaving his hands dangling and giving them jagged articulation. After the pipe falls, he gets even more shattered, with one of his eyes dark, the yellow security light gone, and his grin now resembling more of a sneer, with half of his glowing teeth gone and his up-curved mouth shattered on one side. Although there's no clear damage on HAPPS's torso, his programming has been damaged as his speech is incomplete and his voice drops a couple octaves. His foam hands and spiky metal pinchers are ripped off, giving him sharp metal shards at the end of his arms. One of HAPPS's treads is hanging partially off its runner and the other is askew, making him consistently lurch to the right. The struggle between the two slows him down. HAPPS's telescoping extender is also damaged and appears more like a serrated knife.

HAPPS is a janitorial and maintenance animatronic who resides inside Freddy's Fortress. He keeps kids safe and sanitizes the tubes and also opens mirror partitions which close off broken or off-limits areas of the maze.

entities.name: Isabella
entities.description:
Isabella, also known as Two, is one of the overarching antagonists and twist deuteragonists in Bobbiedots, Part 1 and Bobbiedots, Part 2 in the fourth and fifth books from the Tales from the Pizzaplex series. She is one of the first-generation, also known as gen1, Bobbiedots.

Two, compared to the other broken gen1s, is far more ravaged and decrepit. She is just a stripped-down metal endoskeleton topped by a mutilated one-eyed skull. Two's lower jaw is broken, flopping to the side. She also has sharp metal fingers and a glowing green eye. Two’s cables are laid bare, with sparking copper wiring sprouting from the top of her mangled cranium. Her hip sockets are ragged as both limbs have been torn away, leaving her a stark metal torso and skull streaming exposed wires.

Two weeks after the gen1s are defeated, Abe manages to find new legs for Isabella and gets nearly enough pieces of plastic exoskeleton for Sasha to form an entirely new one for Isabella.

She was programmed with protecting the tenant and the tower back when they were active. When she and the other gen1 Bobbiedots heard that Landon Prout was planning on burning down the Fazplex Tower, they were frighted and decided to kill him which led them to being broken and decrepit.

entities.name: Jelly People
entities.description:
The Jelly People are the main antagonists of Under Construction, the third story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 1: Lally's Game.

The jelly people are smooth, gelatinous, vaguely human-shaped creatures with slick, translucent skin. Beneath the skin, faint pale blue filaments similar to veins extend through their bodies. Maya says they appear unfinished and compares them to uncooked dough. They are stated to grow unnaturally fast, almost to adulthood in days. They are also described as feeling squishy, cold, slimy.

The first appearance was a baby, and then they started to spread across streets and stores. By the end of the story, Maya's entire house gets flooded with them, and she is trapped under.

entities.name: Lally
entities.description:
Lally is the main antagonist of Lally's Game, the second story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 1: Lally's Game. He was the mascot and animatronic doll used for the Lally's Game attraction.

Lally is estimated to be between three and four feet tall. Mostly white and smooth with a plastic or rubber outer shell, he is bald with articulated arms and legs, and black joints between each limb. The area joining Lally's neck and torso is also black. He has vaguely humanlike features, with a round face, small ears, a small nose, faint raised eyebrows over lidless black eyes, and some subtle muscular definition in the torso and limbs. Lally's mouth is a barely-upturned curve with thick lips.

While the functionality prior to the story is unknown, Lally seemingly a still statue with no movement as the mentioned goal of the game was to put Lally in a hiding spot and pretend to look around for him. At some point, presumably after the attraction collapses after workers attempted to remodel it, it has gained the ability to move, as it then proceeds to torture Cade by killing every girlfriend he has due to his attraction's "Two players only" rule.

Lally was the star animatronic of the attraction Lally's Game in the Pizzaplex, a game intended for lonely children. Apparently, the child would hide Lally and then try to find him, like a pretend game of hide-and-seek.
entities.short_description: Lally is the main antagonist of Lally's Game, the second story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 1: Lally's Game. He was the mascot and animatronic doll used for the Lally's Game attraction.

entities.name: Mac the Muscle
entities.description:
Mac the Muscle is one of the least described animatronics in the book and story, Submechanophobia. It is a dark blue in colour, and is the largest of the three sharks in the Mechaquarium, but is not the largest animatronic in there.

As all of the underwater animatronics are described together, it can be assumed that Mac the Muscle is also old, rundown and rusted in spots, with chipped paint and a few unnoticeable broken pieces.

Mac's personality is not described in the story, however, we can assume that it also typically swims at a generally slow pace, like all other underwater animatronics.

The name 'Mac the Muscle was chosen by park employee, Roy. It's not explained what his reasoning behind the name was specifically, but it could be attributed to Mac being the largest of the shark animatronics. Like the other animatronics of the Mechaquarium, Mac the Muscle was left mostly uncared for during the waterpark's several year closure, and was not renovated upon its reopening. Mac is rarely mentioned throughout the story, as it doesn't break down like Delilah the Mermaid, Hank the Hammer, or Polo the Serpent, and it doesn't play a major role like Zeus the Sea Dragon.

entities.description:
Marco is a faded purple, long tailed sea serpent animatronic. Marco is Polo's twin, and both are described as smaller then Zeus the Sea Dragon, and as having snakelike bodies.

As all of the underwater animatronics are described, Marco is old and rundown, with chipped paint, spots of rust and a few broken pieces you wouldn't notice at a glance.

Marco is mentioned to have a flicker of yellow light in its eyes for a moment, but this is brushed off as not possible, as there is no power to it at the time.

Marco and Polo are known to hide in obscure locations around the Mechaquarium. As with the others in the Mechaquarium, Marco swims at a generally slow pace under normal circumstances.

entities.name: Mini Bot 5000
entities.description:
The Mini Bot 5000 is a minor character in Frailty, the first story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 1: Lally's Game. It was a robot made as part of a group project for Jessica and Robert.

The Mini Bot 5000 is a small robot that was melded together with various metal part from the junkyard and the rest having been bought from the hardware store, its flat tray lying on his back. It's arm was fused with aluminum tubing, with its wires tucked inside. When they were testing it, it was not yet painted.

When they start presenting it, they painted some of its part of Robert's favorite color; blue.

The Mini Bot 5000 was made as part of a group project by Mrs. Willoughby, with Jessica and Robert being paired up together. They first went to Robert's house, with Robert working on soldering the wires into the miniature bot. After finishing, Jessica comes up with the name Mini Bot 5000, with it gaining a chuckle out of Robert

Mentioned in Pressure as a character within a video game that is housed in a music box and is referred to as a "ghost." Puppet is mentioned again in GGY, being displayed on the artwork for the arcade cabinet "Puppet's Basketball."

In Dittophobia, Ballora is found frozen on her stage in the dancing floor of Circus Baby's Entertainment and Rental.

entities.name: Moondrop Hologram
entities.description:
The is the main antagonist of Somniphobia, the first story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 3: Somniphobia.

Moondrop the jester is a plastic figurine within the Moondrop's Dream Sphere. He resembles his animatronic counterpart, with half of his face is a smiling pale crescent moon while the other half is eclipsed in darkness. Moondrop wears a cap and puffy blue pants decorated in stars and a gray top with a frilly collar. Bells hang from his hat, both wrists, and tips of his shoes. When the Dream Sphere is activated, Moondrop’s eyes glow red.

On the book's cover, Moondrop's left eye remains white with pink spirals, while the right eye has the inverse effect of being pink with white spirals.

Moondrop is used in a Fazbear Entertainment themed Dream Sphere, which can be used for educational purposes. The Dream Sphere hypnotizes people, causing them to see things written down on paper manifest into pictures. These dream spheres are sold at Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex and cost a thousand tickets to buy. The Dream Sphere packaging recommends that the sphere be only used for 10 minutes a day. When Sam Barker goes over the time limit, his personal memories start seeping into the simulation.

entities.name: Nexie
entities.description:
is the main antagonist of Nexie, the first story in Tales from the Pizzaplex 6: Nexie.

Nexie is a blonde-haired Buddytronic doll with the pieces that Astrid picked out put on in strange ways. One of her round blue eyes is much higher than the other, and her lower eyeball is bulging. Nexie's full, pink plump cheeks are low on her face, appearing more like jowls. Her rosy, pouty mouth and the upturned nose are too close together, with her nose practically resting on her rosy upper lip. Nexie's mouth also doesn't close properly, making it appear like she's baring her even, small white teeth. Her three long braids originate at the base of her skull instead of at the top, jutting upward and then knotting together and spraying outward widely like a big spider. Nexie's head is much too small for her nearly three-foot-tall body. Her arms jut from her sides instead of from normal shoulders, and her legs start at her waist, right next to where the arms start. Nexie's neck is too long, and her chest is too compacted. She also has short-fingered hands and plastic skin. Nexie has a simple blue dress with a little flounce around its hem and a darker blue bow around its waist. In the front, below the waistline, the dress has big patch pockets in the same dark blue as the bow. Nexie also has a straw hat with a wide brim and a blue bow. Because of her proportions, however, her clothes fit poorly. Nexie's hat sits low on her forehead, and her dress is scrunched up, wrinkled, and nearly ripping at the shoulders.

Astrid removes Nexie's hat, as it's just too big to stay on due to her weird braids. Later, Astrid manages to fix Nexie's arms and legs so they extend from her shoulders and hips.

Nexie was created when the Buddytronic Boutique Shop's systems malfunctioned during a power outage. Despite her disfigured appearance, Astrid still loved her. Nexie was self-conscious about her appearance and wanted Astrid's help to get back on track. Astrid tried to give Nexie new, smoother arms and legs, but it wasn't enough. She wanted a full endoskeleton. Unhinged, she grabbed scissors and peeled off part of her skin, revealing her endoskeleton.
entities.short_description: is the main antagonist of Nexie, the first story in Tales from the Pizzaplex 6: Nexie.

entities.name: Nightmare Bonnie
entities.description:
Nightmare Bonnie, also referred to as The Bunny or The Rabbit in the story, appears in Dittophobia, the third and final story of Tales from the Pizzaplex #8: B7-2 as one of the secondary antagonists torturing Rory. It was built by William Afton.

When torturing Rory, Nightmare Bonnie is a large, tattered purple-blue rabbit creature, with long, mottled rabbit ears and an open-mouthed face displaying pointy teeth and pointy nails on the tips of its fingers. Once the hallucinogenic gas stops getting dispensed, the Rabbit is an oversized mechanical puppet, hung on a flimsy metallic skeleton.

In Dittophobia, Bonnie is one of the few nightmarish creatures that torture Rory every night as he breathes in hallucinogenic gas. It enters Rory's bedroom through the door on the left side of his room, slowly inching its way to his bed, eventually leaning forward, pressed against his bed, reaching out for Rory. After the gas stops getting dispensed, Rory finds Bonnie inside the left hall, revealing it to be a mechanically-controlled animatronic puppet, with tears on its fur revealing more of its flimsy, metallic skeleton that helps it move.

While Nightmare Bonnie appears to be a moving animatronic, in reality, the nightmares true forms are mounted suit parts on rolling mechanical stands to emulate animatronics hunting someone, being turned into monsters by illusions as the result of hallucinogenic gas.

entities.description:
Nightmare Chica, also referred to as The Chick or The Chicken in the story, appears in Dittophobia, the third and final story of Tales from the Pizzaplex #8: B7-2 as one of the secondary antagonists torturing Rory. It was built by William Afton.

While torturing Rory, Nightmare Chica is a large, tattered yellow chicken-like animatronic with a massive mouth full of sharp teeth. Its lower jaw is separated from the top, allowing Rory to see his rooms wallpaper behind the chicken. It has massive hands with long, razor-like fingers, which held a bright pink cupcake. After the nightmare, Chica is revealed to be an an oversized mechanical puppet, with tattered fur hung on a metallic skeleton.

In Dittophobia, Chica is one of the few nightmarish creatures that torture Rory every night as he breathes in hallucinogenic gas. It enters Rory's bedroom through the door on the right side of his room, along with its nightmarish cupcake companion, slowly advancing its way to his bed. After the gas stops getting dispensed, Rory finds Chica at the end of the right hall, revealing it to be a mechanically-controlled animatronic puppet, with tears on its fur revealing more of its flimsy, metallic skeleton that helps it move.

While Nightmare Chica appears to be a moving animatronic, in reality, the nightmares true forms are mounted suit parts on rolling mechanical stands to emulate animatronics hunting someone, being turned into monsters by illusions as the result of the hallucinogenic gas.

entities.name: Nightmare Freddy
entities.description:
Nightmare Freddy, also referred to as The Bear in the story, appears in Dittophobia, the third and final story of Tales from the Pizzaplex #8: B7-2 as one of the secondary antagonists torturing Rory during his night terrors. It was built by William Afton.

When Rory is having night terrors, Nightmare Freddy is large, frightening, mutilated brown bear wearing a black top hat and bow tie. It has sharp, large teeth and its jaw can open "impossibly wide." But, once the nightmare ends, the Bear is seen as an oversized puppet with tattered fur, hung on a flimsy, metallic skeleton.

In Dittophobia, Freddy is one of the few nightmarish creatures that torture Rory every night as he breaths in hallucinogenic gas. It rises from under Rory's bed and opens its jaw wide to bite down on Rory's flesh. After the gas stops dispensing, Rory finds Freddy housed beneath a trap door hidden by a rug in the bedroom. It is seen to be a mechanically-controlled animatronic puppet, with tears on its fur, revealing more of its flimsy, metallic skeleton that helps it move.

While Nightmare Freddy appears to be a moving animatronic, in reality, the nightmares true forms are mounted suit parts on rolling mechanical stands to emulate animatronics hunting someone, being turned into monsters by illusions as the result of hallucinogenic gas.

entities.name: Olive
entities.description:
Olive, previously named Two, is one of the main deuteragonist and true main antagonist in Bobbiedots, Part 1 and Bobbiedots, Part 2 in the fourth and fifth books from the Tales from the Pizzaplex series.

Olive is one of the second-generation (also known as gen2) Bobbiedots in the Fazplex Tower. In Abe's apartment, she is in charge of news and information from the outside world.

Like the other Bobbiedots, Olive is a holographic girl with gray skin, a large heart-shaped face, unnaturally huge catlike eyes, arched brows, a large oval spot on her forehead, a large circle on top of her head, bow-shaped lips, and a small protrusion of a nose. Her dominant color is neon green, with two long, bright neon green pigtails that resemble streams of light more than actual hair. Olive has a pair of round gray glasses. She’s also a little taller and sleeker than Rose. Olive has green-tipped fingers and wears a white-and-gray bell-bottomed bodysuit striped neon green.

Olive has a very sarcastic personality compared to the other Bobbiedots. She has a voice that sounds young, similar to Rose, but more spoiled-brat sarcastic than her. However, in actually, she thinks that she is very superior compared to other humans. She is also manipulative to Abe, making him feel more safe with them.

entities.name: Pizzaplex Ballora
entities.description:
Ballora is the main antagonist of Cleithrophobia, the third story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 3: Somniphobia.

Ballora, just like her previous counterpart, is a metal animatronic designed to look like a ballerina. She has blue metal hair caught up in a bun and held with a metal fan-shaped flamenco-dancer-style comb. Ballora also has purple eyes with long eyelashes, a ton of teeth, and pink blush on her sculpted cheeks. She wears a blue leotard and tutu. Ballora's limbs are articulated, and in most of her design sketches she stands with her arms lifted over her head. Grady describes Ballora as "'pretty' in a weirdly robotic way." Her endoskeleton is a combination of metal and thick rubber-encased wires arranged in a way that resemble musculature.

The version of Ballora that Grady encounters in the tubes is just her upper body, which is attached to a robotic mechanism that moves her through the venue.

Ballora appears as the main antagonist of the story Cleithrophobia and is the animatronic mascot of Ballora's Fitness and Flex, a fitness exercise venue with the main gimmick being a climbing rink that can be found beneath the main level of this story's version of Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex.

entities.name: Polo the Serpent
entities.description:
Polo is a pale pink, sea serpent animatronic. Like its twin, Marco, Polo is described as being smaller than Zeus the Sea Dragon and as having a snakelike body.

As with all of the underwater animatronics, Polo is old and rundown, with chipped paint, rusted spots and a few broken pieces you'd miss at a glance.

Polo and its twin Marco, are both known for hiding in obscure places around the Mechaquarium, and as with all other underwater animatronics, normally swim at a generally slow pace.

Polo is one of the many underwater animatronics in Freddy's Sea Life Mechaquarium. It was given its name by water park employee Roy, because of its tendency to hide in the ocean decor of the Mechaquarium. Marco and Polo are both well known for hiding, and were both possibly named after the swimming pool game 'Marco Polo', where one player who can't see, must search for and catch the other players by shouting 'Marco', so that the other players must shout 'Polo'. Like all of the animatronics at the water park, Polo was left mostly uncared for during the park's several year closure and no money was spent on renovating it for when the park reopened.

entities.description:
Rose, previously named Three, is one of the main deuteragonists and true main antagonists in Bobbiedots, Part 1 and Bobbiedots, Part 2 in the fourth and fifth books from the Tales from the Pizzaplex series.

Rose is one of the second-generation (also known as gen2) Bobbiedots in the Fazplex Tower. In Abe's apartment, she is the diet and lifestyle Bobbiedot.

Rose is a bright-faced holographic girl with long, hot-pink pigtails that look like streams of light rather than actual hair. She wears a white-and-gray bell-bottomed bodysuit striped with the same hot pink. Rose has a large heart-shaped face with unnaturally huge, hot-pink, catlike eyes. Her arched brows are the same pink as her hair, as is a large oval spot on her forehead and a large circle on top of her head. Rose’s bow-shaped mouth, which is under a small protrusion that is her nose, is the same color. Her pigtails are topped by hot-pink-and-gray bows. Rose has a gray skin, a round belly, and rounded shoulders. The bottom of her shoes glimmer as bright pink as her eyes.

Rose has an upbeat personality, with her always talking in a high pitched voice, similar to that of a "perky cheerleader". She is sometimes doing kawaii and cutesy poses around Abe. However, she also shows that she does eat a lot, much to the annoyance of Gemini and Olive.

entities.description:
Sly is one of the better described of the three shark animatronics. It's the smallest of the three, with a light blue colour, beady eyes and a small tail.

As all animatronics of the Mechaquarium are described, Sly is old and rundown, with chipped paint, spots of rust and a few broken pieces you wouldn't notice at a distance.

Sly is known for sneaking around the faux rocks and plants of the Mechaquarium and it swims at a generally slow pace under normal circumstances.

Sly the Shark, was named by water park employee Roy, after how it sneaks around the decor of the Mechaquarium. Like most of the attractions and animatronics of Freddy's Fantasy Water Park, it was left mostly uncared for during the park's several year closure, and neither Sly, nor the other animatronics were renovated before the water park reopened.

While at first glance, they seem to be a loving family, when in actuality they are a trio of vaguely humanoid bots using illusion discs sent by Fazbear Entertainment LLC to get Steve to comply with them.

Main Article: Steve Snodgrass (Tales from the Pizzaplex) Or were you looking for Steven (disambiguation) or his core series counterpart?Steven Snodgrass is the main protagonist of the story. He was a ordinary guy who worked at a gas station before getting involved with Victoria and their new "family".

Victoria is the antagonist of the story and the "wife" of Steve Snodgrass.

Avery & Abigail are the "children" of Steve and Victoria Snodgrass.

entities.name: Springtrap Cosplay
entities.description:
The Springtrap Cosplay in the Tales from the Pizzaplex series is a suit worn by Luca in Pressure, the second story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 3: Somniphobia.

The Springtrap Cosplay is a ratty-looking, puke-yellow-green rabbit suit with matted, putrid fur that feels crusty and scummy. Its old with reddish splotches, torn ears, and patches of fur ripped away, exposing the suit’s substructure in several places. The suit is big and baggy, and it comes in two pieces. The first is its big, ghoul-eyed, toothy-mouthed head. The head has exposed yellowish teeth, and its mouth is described as a “grim maw of desolation.” A wire sticks out from its jaw, more protrude from a hole in the fur on its head, and even more extend from beneath its dark eye sockets. The other part of the suit is its body, with hidden closures up the front allowing people to step into it. The covering of the suit’s big, fuzzy, skeletal-looking hands is missing a good chunk of fur, exposing metal on numerous fingers. It also has oversized feet which shoes can fit into.

The Springtrap suit is big and baggy, and both its fur and the metal skeleton beneath it stretch to accommodate people's heights. There’s a mechanism on the back of the suit’s head that keeps it locked on.

Springtrap appears in the beginning of Pressure as an old suit that Luca is made to wear to act in his and his friends' roleplaying game at the Urban Legends Role Play Auditorium in Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex.

entities.name: The Mimic
entities.description:
The Mimic is the main antagonist of the Tales from the Pizzaplex series.

The Mimic officially debuted as an experimental artificial intelligence in the late '70s. It was created by Edwin Murray to copy any movement it saw and care for his son, David Murray, whilst Edwin worked. Soon after David tragically gets hit by a white van, Edwin beats Mimic using a metal pipe out of pure grief and inadvertently infects it with his agony, making it immensely violent and hostile. Ever since then, Mimic has been violently murdering people in gruesome ways. However, after a construction worker, by the name of Gil, plugged his laptop into the endoskeleton and instructed it to remove the limbs and heads of the remaining endoskeletons at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza Place, Mimic began violently tearing off the limbs and heads of nearly every construction worker.

In the story The Mimic, the Mimic's original, primitive-looking endoskeleton body is just a robotic torso with arms and a head. It's made out of cannibalized machinery, such as wiring from unused rooms, pistons from a defunct industrial washing machine, and steel, spools, gears, and springs from a Leavers Machine. The Mimic's skull started out as two large white doll's eyes placed within a boxy piece of metal housing from a broken-down compressor. To make it look more like a real head, a narrow protuberance that juts up from between the eyes is formed using a rounded bit of metal from the guts of the Leavers Machine. Under the eye housing, a hinged “jaw” is welded in place, formed out of parts of the Leavers Machine's guide bars. The Mimic has a big, white-toothed mouth made from a set of novelty chattering teeth. A large processor is welded to the back of the skull and a tangle of wires are run all around the skull. They stretch towards the back of the skull, dive in and out of both eye sockets, snake through the mouth, and extends down the articulated neck that in turn connects with a metallic spine, which connects with a slightly curved makeshift rib cage, and the rib cage is linked to two robotic arms that end in pincerlike hands.

Two weeks after David's death, the Mimic is beaten with a metal rod. One of its eyes is dangling out of its socket and hanging against its cracked fake teeth. The metal used to form the Mimic's forehead and jaw are crimped together, compressing its face. Its broken teeth are shoved back into its head, caught up in torn and tangled wires. The rest of the Mimic's wiring has been raggedly pulled away from its metallic spine, which is bent backward. Its rib cage is crushed in numerous places, its arms hang askew, and its pincers are mutilated. Months later, a team sent by Fazbear Entertainment takes some legs off of nonfunctional animatronics and adds them to the Mimic, restoring it to a functional state.

entities.name: Victoria
entities.description:
Victoria, also known as Three, is one of the overarching antagonists and twist deuteragonists in Bobbiedots, Part 1 and Bobbiedots, Part 2 in the fourth and fifth books from the Tales from the Pizzaplex series. She is one of the first-generation, also known as gen1, Bobbiedots.

Three looks similar to Rose, with her bright pink coloring, but is severely damaged. The top of her face and one of her eyes are missing, exposing blackened metal beneath the smooth plastic surface. Three’s white exoskeleton is cracked, revealing part of her metal rib cage. The rest of her exoskeleton mirrors Rose’s feminine form, except for an open midsection that reveals black wires and servos. Three’s hair is made of long, black, rubbery, plastic-covered power cables that cascade from her skull like a tangle of wriggling snakes, reminding Abe of Medusa. She has one hot-pink eye, a hot-pink glow from her chest area, and a hot-pink light panel on her right thigh and on a power box midway along one of her cables.

Two weeks after the gen2s are defeated, Abe manages to find a replacement eye for Victoria. Using the pieces of plastic exoskeleton Abe found, Sasha replaces Victoria’s missing pieces.

While it is unknown how her personality was like before, it is shown that she cared about protecting the Fazplex Tower and it's tenant. When Landon Prout was planning to burn down the tower, she was forced to become aggressive and kill him.

entities.name: Waterpark Animatronics
entities.description:
The waterpark animatronics are an assorted group of underwater animatronics of Freddy's Fantasy Water Park and appeared in the first story of Tales from the Pizzaplex 4: Submechanophobia. All but one of these animatronics are a part of the water park's main attraction, Freddy's Sea Life Mechaquarium, with the one not featured there being in the workshop for repairs.

The water park animatronics are described as old and run down, with rusted patches, chipped paint and a few broken pieces you wouldn't notice at a distance. They are completely waterproof, and are rarely removed from the Mechaquarium. They normally move and swim quite slowly in the water, and only move quickly in a nightmare dream sequence from the story, Submechanophobia. They seem to get their power wirelessly, or perhaps, through the water, as once the power to the Mechaquarium is turned off, all animatronics deactivate. This is, however, left unexplained as it isn't relevant to the plot of the story.

Each underwater animatronic has an openable panel on their back for maintenance, that contains several wires and a button that resets the animatronics motors. These are also waterproof, and allow very simple maintenance to be done within the Mechaquarium, without removing the animatronic or draining the water. As these animatronics are rather old, and have been mostly unkept for a few years up until the start of Submechanophobia, their wires come loose and they need a motor reset fairly frequently. Once the motor reset button is pushed, the animatronic jerks and flails for a few moments before going still again. To perform this maintenance, the power to the Mechaquarium is shut off, and the animatronics deactivate. When this happens, they settle in place, either floating at the surface, sinking to the bottom, or remaining mostly stationary inbetween. When no wires are loose and a motor reset doesn't fix the problem, the animatronic is removed from the Mechaquarium for more extensive repairs in the workshop at Foxy Island's Water Slides, to the East of the Mechaquarium.

Zeus the Sea Dragon is a large sea dragon animatronic, and plays a major role in the story. Zeus is better described than the other animatronics and is the one who sets Caden on the path to unravelling the story's mystery. It actively saves Caden's life and is the biggest and scariest of the Mechaquarium animatronics. Interestingly, it is also referred to as a 'he' once, making it the second animatronic to recieve a gendered pronoun (the other being Delilah the mermaid) in the story. It is also featured in the backgrounds of both of the front covers for the Submechanophobia book.

entities.name: Zeus the Sea Dragon
entities.description:
Zeus is a huge, green sea dragon and is the largest of the underwater animatronics of the Mechaquarium. It has a reptilian body, metal spikes for spines along its back and tail, and is described as being the scariest of the animatronics. Zeus has wings on the sides of its body, with small, clawed hands and feet, a large jaw and sharp teeth. Some of its teeth have broken off, and oil has built up around its mouth over the years, giving the appearance of dried blood. It has the longest tail and a scaled snout, with its green paint looking like its been rubbed off over time in some places on and around its head. Like all of the underwater animatronics of the water park, Zeus is described as old and rundown, with chipped paint, spots of rust and with broken pieces you wouldn't notice at a distance.

In the first and second iterations of the front cover for Tales from the Pizzaplex 4: Submechanophobia, Zeus is primarily a dark green in colour, with a lighter, more faded colouring to the underside of its lined neck. Its face is rather chunky with rounded edges, a thick nose bridge and is shaped like a cone, being larger at the neck and narrowing down the snout. The snout has two small, black nostrils at the end and it's lower jaw is dropped, seemingly hanging open, but not appearing to be broken. The inside of the lower jaw is coloured faded pinks and greys, with four whiskers on the end of its chin, off-white, sharp teeth and a hole where a tooth is missing. Its eyes are white, with the iris and pupils being so faded they can barely be seen. One is set in Zeus' face, while the other appears to have somewhat popped out of its socket, with both of them aimed in slightly different directions. The popped out eye on the far side of the face is either leaking oil, or the metal of the face has broken away around the underside of it. There's large, torn fins at the back of its upper jaw on either side of its face, with a much larger and more broken fin partway down the back of its neck. They're an off-white kind of grey, with a sandy brown, material to create the webbed effect of fins. The joint where the back of the head meets the long, serpentine neck is open and exposed, showing two round, metal discs on a single metal rod. While the dark green of its body is textured, it does not appear scaled like the story describes, and instead, appears as a mostly flat and worn metal surface. This image of Zeus is much closer to the foreground in the first iteration of the front cover than the second, where it's been flipped to face the left instead of the right.

entities.name: Aimee
entities.description:
Aimee is the main protagonist of Find Player Two!, the third story in Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Aimee is small and skinny with long blonde hair that she ties in a braid or a ponytail. She's pale skinned with small features and bright-blue eyes that are slightly slanted. Aimee's eyebrows have a severe arch, and she has an upturned nose and a slightly pouty mouth.

Aimee still looks similar ten years later, as she’s petite and slender with the same facial features and same way of tying up her hair, however she now uses makeup and is stronger and athletic. She tends to wear sweaters, like a bright-yellow one she wears when returning to her hometown. When Aimee confronts Emmett Tucker, she’s wearing a fitted scoop-neck pale blue sweater and tight navy-blue pencil pants.

Aimee is quiet and nerdy, preferring to read than to play in the loud Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. She gets annoyed by Mary Jo and their personalities seem to clash, but sticks with her because she feels bad for her. Likewise, after Mary Jo disappears Aimee feels a huge amount of guilt and responsibility for it.

entities.description:
is a major character that appears in Dance with Me, the second story in Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer. He's the muscle of a group of thieves that steal from others to survive and share amongst each other.

AJ is a big and bulky black guy with broad shoulders. Kasey says he has the appearance of a former high school football player.

AJ and Jack have a habit of being reckless and blowing through the money they steal. In contrast to Jack, however, AJ is far more calmer and serious. He cares for Kasey like a sister.

AJ, along with Jack, encounter Kasey. They stated that they've been watching her, and invited her to be apart of their group. They are thieves who steal money for food to sustain themselves. She agrees.

entities.name: Alec
entities.description:
is the protagonist in Lonely Freddy, the second story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He is a troubled teenage boy who rebels against what's considered good and enjoys being different from everyone else. As Hazel's, tenth birthday arrives, Alec begins plotting against her to expose his younger sister as the spoiled brat he's certain she is.

Alec is said to be bigger than others his age. He has unruly blond curls, light-green eyes, slightly crooked teeth with braces, and lanky limbs. Alec also has a turned-up nose that he shares with his mother.

Alec enjoys being boundless and living by his own rules, believing that being “bad” is subjective and a construct that can be worked around. He feels that he’s been judged his entire life and prefers his aunt Gigi over his parents since she isn’t constantly trying to “fix” him behind his back, which he finds out through eavesdropping. Alec is deliberate in how he presents himself and uses deflection to hide his true feelings, only showing negative traits and bullying others. This seemingly leads to constant nightmares, which makes him more resentful of others. Only Hazel tends to catch him off-guard, and he is especially mean towards her. Alec coldly dismisses Hazel and constantly tries to find a hidden agenda whenever she tries to get along with him. After seemingly ruining Hazel’s birthday, he breaks down and feels shame.

Alec was born on August 18th, and his named was created as a mixture of "Alexander" and "Eric" as his parents couldn't decide a name. In preschool, Alec realized he was bigger than the other kids and used his height to move to the front of lines with ease. The other kids didn't object to the games he dictated and he never had to look for a seat at the lunch table. One day, Alec's preschool teacher pulled him aside and told him he was a bully, which he assumed was positive and smiled at. His teacher gave him a horrified look and walked away, and the expression haunted Alec as he grew older. Alec eventually concluded that others determination of bad behavior was based on comparison to others, and he tried to find what others considered good and bad.
