entities.name: Alec's Family
entities.description:
Alec's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Alec from Lonely Freddy, the second story of Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch.

Alec is the protagonist of the second Fazbear Frights book's second story.

Ian is Alec and Hazel's father. He named Alec as a combination of "Eric" and the name Meg wanted. "Alexander." When Hazel was born, he and Meg began scolding Alec more and constantly praised Hazel. Ian joined Meg as she used The Growing Child to come up with exercises the mold Alec's behavior. They try having Alec name himself, have him plant a garden, and try having a family camping trip, but all three end in disaster. Ian loses faith in the books as Meg moves on to a new one called The Plan Planner. A week before Hazel's tenth birthday party, Meg tells Ian about a plan created using Chapter Five. Ian expresses his confusion over the multiple books and his little faith in them, but Meg asks if he has an alternative ideas. Not ready to give up, he goes along with the plan.

The next day, Ian and Meg constantly scold Alec in order to get him to behave better. However, Hazel begins to act worse, "accidentally" dropping Ian's shirts in the mud and talking back against Meg during dinner. The following day, when Ian tries to scold Alec for scratching the side of his car with his bike, Hazel unapologetically takes the blame instead. After dinner, Ian and Meg try to discuss Hazel's shift in behavior, but when asked if Meg looks haggard Ian doesn't refute the claim. Meg gets upset as Ian tries bringing the topic back to their kids, but Meg insults his parenting and starts an argument between them.

entities.name: Amber
entities.description:
Amber is a major character in Blackbird, the first story in the book of the same name. She's Nole's cheerful girlfriend who brings him comfort while he's being haunted by the Blackbird.

Amber has wild, shoulder-length, wavy blonde hair, blue eyes, and is in good shape. She has freckles going across the bridge of her nose and the top of her chest. Amber also has a bow-shaped mouth. Like Nole, she usually wears faded jeans, white tank shirts, and, when the weather allows it, leather jackets.

Amber is nice, cheerful, and carefree. She likes to tease others, with a hint of sarcasm slid into mostly everything she says. Amber can be sincere as well and cares for those she’s close with, like Nole. She can also be somewhat superstitious, believing that guilt and emotions give off energy like yin and yang.

Amber has been in many of Nole's classes the previous year and this year, however he's never really thought of her as pretty until recently. She is in the same film class as Nole and Sam, and she's partners with her friend Darla. The two teams are the last two left in class, and while Nole is explaining his idea for a horror story plot around a creepy animatronic, Amber and Darla are in a silent disagreement. Eventually they settle on the plot for their film, and Amber lightly teases Nole and Sam as they head out. Nole teases back as Darla and Amber begin discussing a poetry reading for their English class. Later that day, Amber joins Nole and Sam as they eat a pepperoni-and-jalapeño pizza. She asks about their film, telling them that hers is about knitting and will have plenty of blood. Nole tells Amber their film is about a bird, and she asks Sam for confirmation.

entities.name: Andrew
entities.description:
, also known as the Shadow Child, is a major character who first appeared in the Stitchwraith Stingers as a ghost inside the Stitchwraith. He is the main antagonist of The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. Due to his actions, he can be considered an unintentional antagonist in the epilogues, as well as some of the Fazbear Frights stories.

Andrew is described as a cute little boy with curly black hair and rosy cheeks. He wears a cheap alligator mask that obscures his forehead and eyes in The Man in Room 1280. Andrew is described to have a toothy grin that's more devilish that endearing. He also appears as a child-sized shadow.

In The Man in Room 1280, he is extremely determined to make sure William Afton stays alive and is tortured, going as far as to prevent anyone and everyone from killing him. Throughout the epilogues, Andrew is shown to be very cynical and easily aggravated, evidenced by him snapping at Jake initially when meeting him. He has a tendency to be aggressive when provoked, such as when he tried to kill Larson for pulling a gun on him in self defense.

At some point before the events of the story, Andrew was murdered by William Afton. However, Andrew managed to attach himself to William's soul, allowing Andrew to mentally torment William. Later, William becomes the victim of a huge fire and is taken to Heracles Hospital. Although William has lost his face and most of his skin has burned off, exposing his organs and bones through the translucent black remains of his flesh and is taken off life support, Andrew refuses to let William die.

entities.name: Angel
entities.description:
Angel is the titular main protagonist of Gumdrop Angel, the first story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel. She is a young and talented performer that is held back by her family, who shower her younger step-sister Ophelia with more attention. Angel eventually takes her frustration out on Ophelia after her birthday party, eating a special gumdrop nose from Freddy Fazbear's Pizza.

Angel inherited her mother’s bouncy blonde hair (although Angel's is shoulder-length), bright blue eyes, pleasant and pretty features, and slender body. Rather than wearing a ton of makeup, Angel simply lines her eyes with kohl and keeps her lips glossed. She’s into retro thrift store clothes and likes playing with scarves, jewelry, and other accessories, keeping an extra scarf or strand of beads in her purse to change her look when suited. When visiting Freddy's, Angel does some cool loops with a seventies belt around her narrow waist and wears a filmy sixties peasant top under it that clings to her just right. She also wears jeans and sandals.

After eating the gumdrop nose, a rash and red, pink, and gray gumdrops grow on her body until she fully turns into a Birthday Gummy.

Angel is very envious and resentful, with a strong hatred for her family because of their unfair treatment. She is especially hateful towards Ophelia, getting rather aggressive with her and claims to only feel an ounce of kindness due to her stepsister's ugly appearance. Angel wants to escape her family and use her skills as a talented actress, singer, and dancer to become the center of attention. While she's confident in her looks, she doesn’t like taking advantage of others using them. Having learned to do everything by herself, Angel prefers being tough and independent. She can get rather snarky when she's angry and blurts out whatever she’s thinking. Angel is also rather squeamish, especially in regards to eating animals.

Myron is Angel's stepfather. He only cares about Ophelia and spends his money solely on her. Angel resents this since Myron wastes his money on frivolous things to make Ophelia happy, while refusing to pay for important things for Angel like college loans. Myron doesn't see Angel as a part of his family, and Angel refuses to see him as family either.

Myron is tall, and has dark brown hair all over his body. Angel thinks he looks like a gorilla and can't understand why her mother finds him handsome.

entities.name: Arthur Blythe
entities.description:
is one of the protagonists of The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. He is a middle-aged priest who tries seeing the good in places where others would be less optimistic. Arthur’s faith and optimism is put to the test when he's called to Heracles Hospital to deal with a special patient in room 1280.

Arthur looks older than he is due to his thick wavy hair turning mostly gray when he was 37-years-old, and deep emotions have carved lines on his face. He has wide-set brown eyes that he believes to be boring and simple but others see as gentle and warm. Arthur is also short and slight. His mouth curves upward, even when his face is expressionless. He has thick gray brows and a slightly weak chin. Although he doesn't have to, Arthur likes to wear a long, flowing black cassock. He also wears black leather shoes, a plain black-banded watch, and a satchel slung across his body.

Arthur is a man with strong faith, but is willing to exercise prudence at times too. His faith makes him kind and meek, and he doesn’t often get frustrated due to his beliefs. Arthur is also optimistic and chooses to see hope, love, and joy over pain, struggle, and sorrow. This can make him somewhat idealistic, determined to see the good in everything and do his job to the fullest. Arthur makes himself happy with a couple of indulgent flairs, although his job suppresses most of his idiosyncrasies. He also loves mystery and adventure books and movies.

As a priest, Arthur visits many places to give the dying their last rites. He has been to car crashes, airplane crashes, and all types of natural disasters. Arthur has also prayed over people missing limbs, eyes, and large chunks of their bodies. One of these men gifted Arthur a fully restored 1953 bicycle with gleaming chrome fenders and shiny red paint named Ruby. Arthur rides Ruby everywhere he goes. At home, Arthur is very close with his housekeeper, Peggy. One day, Arthur visits Heracles Hospital to met with the head nurse, Nurse Ackerman. All he is told by Nurse Ackerman is a room number before she sends him away.

entities.description:
Avery Family from Dance with Me, the second story Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer comprises the relatives of Sarah Avery.

Sarah Avery the mother of two young children that Kasey and Jack rob outside of Circus Baby's Pizza World. She's a small woman with brown hair.

After leaving Circus Baby's Pizza World with her daughter, Isabella, and her son, Sarah struggles to find the car keys in her purse. Kasey notices she looks a little dazed and assumes it's from all the bright lights from the kiddie pizza emporium. When Isabella tells her how pretty Circus Baby is and asks to put her hair in pigtails, Sarah says yes to both and tells her to hold her brother's hand. When Isabella begins to feel sleepy, Sarah puts her goody bag in her purse. Once Sarah finds her keys, she reaches down to carry Isabella and her purse is stolen by Kasey.

Eventually, Kasey uses Sarah's drivers license to find her home. She knocks at her door and Sarah answers wearing track pants and a T-shirt from a 5K run for charity. Kasey explains who she is and returns her wallet, telling Sarah that she's changing and is hoping for her forgiveness. Sarah forgives, as few people admit they've done wrong, and invites Kasey inside for tea. Isabella is in the kitchen and asks if they know Kasey, and Sarah explains that they're getting to know her.
entities.short_description: Avery Family from Dance with Me, the second story Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer comprises the relatives of Sarah Avery.

entities.name: Avila Family
entities.description:
The Avila Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Oscar Avila from Out of Stock, the third story of Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch.

Oscar Avila is the protagonist of the second Fazbear Frights book's third story.

On a Friday in late October, a patient at Royal Oaks becomes paranoid that the cat in his room will steal his soul, and Ms. Avila has to call Oscar out of class to help calm him down. Once he's done, she praises him and tries asking Oscar to pick up some yogurt, but he rushes out the door before she can. Ms. Avila is later told by the receptionist that he and his friends went to the mall. The next day, Ms. Avila reads in the newspaper about an incident at the Emporium where security was called and a couple kids ran off with a toy. When Oscar wakes up and goes to eat breakfast, she confronts him about what she read and points out that he and his friends were there. Oscar tells her that it happened after they got there, and she stares at him for a long time before finishing off her coffee and throwing the newspaper in the recycling, not saying another word.

The day before Halloween, Ms. Avila calls Oscar and tells him that many people have called in sick due to the storm and she needs his help tomorrow. Oscar initially isn't listening, but he quickly remembers the next day is Halloween and tries objecting. Ms. Avila questions if they're too old to be trick-or-treating, but Oscar snaps and complains that she expects him to be older than he is because of his dad's death. He then angerly admits to having stolen the Plushtrap Chaser right as the phone line cuts out. When Ms. Avila returns home the next day, she discovers most of the doors heavily damaged. Oscar promises to spend the next weekend patching them and saving up for a new garage door, but his mother doesn't seem to notice, emotionally distraught over what Oscar said. Oscar later finds Ms. Avila in the break room of Royal Oaks that night and gives her favorite chocolates. She then pulls him in for a very tight hug and apologizes for depending on his so much. Oscar tells her it's okay and lets her hug him for a good long while.

Barry is good-looking with auburn hair and freckles. When he was younger his hair was more red than auburn.

Barry is mature and courageous, not scared easily by small things. While he likes to tease his friends, he cares for Hudson and tries looking out for him.

In his high school years, he was a novelty to the cheerleaders and fans alike.

entities.name: Beatrice Thomas
entities.description:
, aka Nurse Thomas, is a major character in The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. She is a nice yet simple nurse working in the hospice wing of Heracles Hospital. Beatrice can be considered an antagonist due to her opposition to Arthur and the patient.

Nurse Thomas is round and sweet looking with curly graying black hair. She’s also described as grandmotherly-looking.

Nurse Thomas is decently nice, but also very simple and rather forgetful. She is very emotional and has a strong love of people, doing things that she deems necessary to help others. Beatrice also loves growing flowers, cooking large dinners, and needlepointing Bible verses. She can be idealistic at times, but when there’s clear signs of danger she’ll face reality.

Not a lot is known about Nurse Thomas from prior to the events of The Man in Room 1280, but she loves growing flowers, cooking her family large dinners, and needlepointing Bible verses. She became a nurse because she loves people and wishes to server them however she can.

Kimberly Bergstrom is a major character in the second Fazbear Frights book's first story.

Greg had met her and her husband in the past, finding Mrs. Bergstrom to be nice. One day, she and Kimberly return home and as they're hiding inside Mr. Bergstrom finds Greg hiding in the bushes. She's terrified to hear that her daughter is in potential danger, but her husband calls the cops and has Greg arrested.

Greg had met him and his wife previously. One day, Mr. Bergstrom returns home and a gust of wind blows his red baseball cap off his head and towards a bush. As he goes to retrieve it, he spots Greg hiding in the bush and recognizes him. Greg frantically tries to warn Kimberly about Fetch and the potential danger she's in, but Mr. Bergstrom becomes furious by Greg's claims. He calls the police, claiming Greg is stalking Kimberly and demanding he be arrested. When a cop arrives, Mr. Bergstrom reports Greg's break-in at the old pizzeria.

Mrs. Blair is Mason's mother. She's a successful real estate agent whose face is plastered on billboards. Sarah assumes she and her family live in a mansion on the fancy side of town.

Blair is an English-language name of Scottish Gaelic origin. The surname is derived from any of the numerous places in Scotland called Blair, derived from the Scottish Gaelic blàr, meaning "plain", "meadow" or "field".

entities.name: Bob Mackenzie
entities.description:
Bob Mackenzie is the protagonist of Bunny Call, the first story in the book of the same name. He is a frustrated father who, after being dragged to a summer camp for a week, signs up for a mean prank the camp offers.

After twelve years of marriage, Bob has thinning, graying short hair, soft jowls, tired dark brown eyes, and his lips are usually clamped into a downward curve. He loses his muscular build as he is unable to work out. Bob's eyebrows also get bushy.

Back in high school, Bob was a jock. He had long thick black hair, a sharp jawline, mischievous eyes, and a wide, carefree grin.

Bob is rather introverted, wanting time to himself and desiring relaxation, peace, and quiet. He also likes doing things either in solitude or with his wife, Wanda. Bob knows a good deal about form, function, energy, and landscape. He often has a sense about when land and nature welcomes a structure or doesn’t. Bob hates following schedules and lists, and feeling overwhelmed by his obligations. While he loves his family, he also feels he has no control over his life and becomes frustrated and resentful. Bob tries restraining his aggression with sarcasm and dry humor, which doesn’t usually land. He is instead soothed by memories of his childhood and the sounds of nature. Bob's pessimism and anger makes him act rather selfish and childish, clouding his better judgment. He's initially delighted and pleased to have signed up for the Bunny Call, but later feels guilty and is riddled with anxiety. After successfully defending his family, Bob has a renewed happiness and love for his family.
entities.short_description: Bob Mackenzie is the protagonist of Bunny Call, the first story in the book of the same name. He is a frustrated father who, after being dragged to a summer camp for a week, signs up for a mean prank the camp offers.

is the second main character in Together Forever, the third story of Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Brittany has nails painted purple with gold swirls, shiny blonde hair, big bright blue eyes, high cheekbones, a pert nose, full lips, a perfect petite figure, and the most up-to-date fashions and makeup like lip gloss. For most of the story, she wears a chocolate-brown faux suede miniskirt with two diagonal zippers forming a V in the front, a flouncy chocolate-and-black geometric-patterned blouse, and black platforms. When working on Rosie Porkchop, she changes to denim.

entities.name: Chip
entities.description:
is a major character in Into the Pit, the first story from Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit. He is a young boy that Oswald befriends when visiting Freddy Fazbear's Pizza in the past. He appears in an expanded role in the story's video game adaptation, Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit.

Chip is around the same age as Oswald, wearing a polo (light yellow, then baby-blue, and later peach-colored) with the collar turned up, tucked into what appears to be a pair of dad jeans. He also wears huge white tennis shoes. Chip has poofy hair which he spends a lot of time fixing.

In the graphic novel, Chip has blonde hair and blue eyes. In the game adaptation, Chip has curly brown hair, a yellow baseball cap and shirt, a blue vest, jeans, and black shoes.

Chip is kind and far more laid-back than his friend Mike; Oswald sees him as "cool." He is the first to reach out to Oswald, and is very friendly and inviting towards him; he also immediately notices that Oswald is new, implying he knows most of the children in town. He is also rather generous, never once having asked for Oswald to pay for any of the games or food the three indulge in. He does occasionally joke about how out-of-touch Oswald seems to be, but is excited to one day take him to the movies. While he likes the arcade at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, he dislikes the animatronics and finds them creepy. He also is afraid of clowns.

entities.name: Chris Watson
entities.description:
is the main protagonist of He Told Me Everything, the third story of Fazbear Frights 7: The Cliffs. He is a snobby teenage boy who desperately wants to be rich and successful, which he hopes becoming part of his high school's Science Club will help him achieve.

Chris has short, neatly cut sandy-brown hair that he maintains with some gel. On the first day of school, he wears a polo shirt and khakis.

Chris is a science nerd who loves learning. He is also a snob who wants to be seen as prestigious and fantasizes about living a higher-status lifestyle. Chris is embarrassed by his parents as he believes they're unrefined, although he still wishes to give them a successful and rich life. He's also annoyed by his friends as he believes they lack maturity and ambition, leading to him abandoning them for higher-status friends. Chris always desires owning more elegant things and is disappointed by the cheaper things his family compromises with. Despite his desires to be independent, he recognizes his youth and begrudgingly follows his parents’ orders. Chris still gets rather squamish when it comes to dental matters and he cheats during the lock-in with an old baby tooth. When he finally realizes that the Faz-Goo is replacing him, he regrets his past behavior and tells the clone to be nicer than he was.

Chris is preparing for his first day of high school and makes sure to have a good first impression. He despises his family's low status and is eager to join the school's Science Club, known infamously in the town. He especially looks forward to the after-school experiment held by the teacher, Dr. Little, as it was a "life-changing" experiment that made the students popular in school.

entities.name: Christine Wilber
entities.description:
Christine Wilber is a major character from Blackbird, the first story in the book of the same name. She's a young woman that Nole ruthlessly bullied in junior high, and years later desperately seeks forgiveness from.

Christine has blonde hair, a bow-shaped mouth, wide cheek-bones, and small, close-set blue eyes. She also has freckles and slightly crooked teeth. In junior high, Christine was overweight with long, stringy hair that she never washed enough. She also wore thick glasses and strange clothes.

In her sophomore year of college, Christine is now fit due to her dancing. When Nole arrives at her room, she's wearing a full-length, skintight light blue leotard.

Back in junior high, Christine was rather awkward due to her low self confidence. After relentless bullying, she got angry and decided to treat herself well. Christine stepped up and began to love herself, finding comfort in the things she liked. By the time Christine is in college, she’s become very confident with extraordinary elegance and precision in what she does. She’s also rather cheerful and kind. Christine has some small quirks, like clasping her hands together and having trouble figuring out what words to say.

entities.name: Chuck Dinglewood
entities.description:
Chuck Dinglewood is the deuteragonist of Step Closer, the first story in the book of the same name. He's Pete’s younger brother who, despite his best efforts not to, constantly annoys his older brother.

Chuck has braces and carries around an inhaler in the pockets of his shorts.

Chuck is rather cowardly, afraid of breaking the rules and scarring easily. He is also very curious and nerdy, asking questions constantly to learn more about things. After his parents’ divorce, Chuck tries to keep himself busy by doing things he likes, such as hanging out with friends, playing online video games, and solving puzzles. He tries to be on good terms with Pete, but everything seems to annoy him and the two are constantly fighting and calling each other names. Despite this, Chuck is very forgiving of his brother and tries helping him.

Chuck always goes to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza after school with his friends and his older brother, Pete, who babysits him due to their parent's divorce. One day, while watching him at Freddy’s, he decides to scare Chuck by taking him to the maintenance room to see Foxy. Chuck escapes as Pete tries to start up Foxy, as Chuck is afraid of Foxy. Pete's shirt gets caught on a nail as he tries to catch him. Pete manages to escape and the brothers return home. When they arrive, their mom shows them brochures about being organ donors.

Cindy is freckled, redheaded, and small for her age. She has bulging hazel eyes and her hair is springy curls. Cindy prefers wearing gingham, polka dots, animal prints, and little floral patterns. For most of the story, Cindy wears a full-skirted short dress. The next day, Cindy wears a new red dress with poufy sleeves.

entities.description:
Cindy Lee Mackenzie is a major character in Bunny Call, the first story in the book of the same name. She's Bob's sweet young daughter who's high energy and excitement towards Camp Etenia annoys him.

Cindy is pudgy with curly auburn pigtails and freckles.

Cindy is very cute and enthusiastic with tons of energy, getting her family amped up. She is also extra-sensitive and is hard to calm down when upset. Cindy also loves bright and cute things. Like her mother, Wanda, and her older siblings, she's a light sleeper and gets upset over loud noises and being woken abruptly.

Cindy is the youngest of the three children. Bob said that the first two children were manageable, but Cindy was the one that made him lose all his free time.

entities.name: Connor Billings
entities.description:
Connor O. Billings is a major character from Hide-and-Seek, the third story in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He's Toby's competitive and arrogant older brother who's always doing better than him.

Due to his job, Connor's button-up shirts, cheeks, and arms are usually covered in black grease. Black oil is also under his fingernails.

Connor is highly competitive, driven by a need to always be the best at everything seemingly as a result of his mother leaving at a young age. When things don’t go his way, he tends to get very aggressive and mopes around. Due to his usual success, Connor is rather loudmouthed and arrogant, constantly rubbing his fortune in Toby’s face. His confidence and conversational nature allowed him to excel at school, and his competitive nature made him rather outgoing and great at sports. Connor also shares his obsession with sports with his father, which the two bond over. While Connor does care for Toby, his need to be better makes him rather ignorant to his feelings.

Cyril is short and skinny with boyish features and limp brown hair.

In the graphic novel, his hair appears to be cut in a bowl cut.

Cyril is rather timid and somewhat pessimistic. He is also very nerdy and enjoys spending time with his mother, which makes him the target of bullies. Cyril is also shown to be easily pressured into doing things, especially by Greg.

entities.name: Dale
entities.description:
Dale is a major character from Sergio's Lucky Day, the second story in Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel. He was Sergio's imposing yet friendly boss during his time at an architectural firm.

Dale is big and muscular with a shaved head.

Dale is a friendly manager who, despite his teasing, cares for and wishes the best for his employees. Still, he can be stern and serious when called for, and when Sergio quits he becomes furious.

Dale is Sergio Altieri's supervisor and a senior manager in their architectural firm. Before working as an architect, Dale used to be a football player. When he approaches Sergio to tell him he got the project manager job, Sergio accidentally knocks his coffee mug over and he catches it. Dale gives it back and shakes Sergio's hand once he's done with his moonwalk. He tells Sergio to be careful what he wishes for and that's he's gone and done it, and when Sergio asks for an explanation he tells Sergio the job is difficult and he may need to start sleeping in the office. He laughs about it but Sergio begins to have doubts. Dale reserves a steakhouse's meeting room for Sergio's promotion dinner, which twelve of the fourteen architects working in Sergio's department show up to. Once most people have finished, Dale stands and taps his water glass so Sergio can give a speech.

entities.description:
Dan Harbor is a major character in Hide-and-Seek, the third story in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He's Toby's friendly boss and owner of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza and Games.

Dan has a big chest with meaty arms but short, skinny legs. He also has a thick beard.

Dan is a friendly boss that’s always nice towards his employees. He enjoys having families together and entertaining them, which is why he loves Freddy’s. When others disrespect the restaurant and destroy his property, Dan gets very upset and annoyed.

entities.name: Darrin
entities.description:
Darrin, aka Uncle Dare, is a major character in Fetch, the first story of the Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He's Greg's flamboyant and rich uncle who he enjoys spending time with much more than his parents.

Dare is six-foot-five with broad shoulders. He also has a huge head, a graying goatee, and long hair that's dyed purple and worn in a braid. Dare tends to wear bright-colored suits and ties paired with patterned shirts, and on his right index finger is an onyx and gold ring.

Dare is flamboyant and fun, even when it comes to food. He loves and cares for his family, even if his brother-in-law doesn't respect or care for him back. Dare is especially close to Greg and is very accepting of him, not caring for his likes and dislikes.

Darrin is a wealthy, successful inventor of car parts. This mixed with his incredible luck with investments and money in general allows him to live on a ten-acre estate with a workshop. This put him at odds with his brother-in-law, Steven, who he constantly fought with. Dare still deeply cared for his only sibling, Hillary, and this love extended onto Greg when he was born. Dare would be incredibly supportive of Greg's interests, make him gifts, and teach him things, such as yoga.

entities.description:
is the protagonist of 1:35 A.M., the first story in the book of the same name. She later briefly appears in the tenth Stitchwraith Stinger. Delilah is a young woman who becomes extremely exhausted and pessimistic after her divorce. One day, she purchases an electronic doll in hopes that it's alarm clock aid against her exhaustion, but is instead haunted by it.

Delilah has wavy shoulder-length dark hair and dark eyes. She used to wear makeup, but after her divorce she decides to keep her face bare. Even without makeup, Delilah is pretty, with a modeling agency having told her that she's a large chin away from having classically beautiful features.

Delilah is said to have an “obsessive personality,” meaning she’ll latch onto a perspective and have difficulty letting go. Following her divorce, she takes on a negative outlook on life and becomes stuck in a state of perpetual exhaustion. Delilah also seems to suffer from brain fog and depersonalization, making it hard to think clearly and stay in sync with her senses. She loves sleep but is unable to get enough due to her work schedule, and her low energy makes her quick to frustration. Delilah is entertained by looking through garage sales, wanting to know what people used, collected, loved, and don’t want around anymore. It was theorized by her therapist that this gives her a glimpse into family life, reminding her what “normal” looks like. Unlike her friend Harper, Delilah tries to have grounded beliefs, even refusing to believe her experiences with Ella were supernatural.

Delilah entered the foster care system after her parents both died when she was eleven. She bounced from home to home, finally landing in a house with a couple where the husband was a former military man who imposed strict rules on those living there. The other foster kid there was Harper, and the girls became friends in their less-than-ideal situation.

entities.name: Devon Blaine Marks
entities.description:
is the main protagonist of The New Kid, the third story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM. He is a very troubled teenage boy who's desire to fit in with others at his school leads him down a dark and twisted path. Depending on how one interprets the story, Devon could be considered the main antagonist.

Devon is 5'9" with dark hair worn long and messy. He considers himself too skinny for his height. Devon’s teeth are super crooked, his ears are big and stick out of his hair, his neck is long, and his dark eyes are small and close together. He also has chewed-on cuticles and bitten-down nails. Due to his family's poor income, Devon only wears jeans and T-shirts.

Years of living outside social groups has taught Devon to hide his emotions and keep a neutral face. He is made bored by school and doesn’t care enough to “apply himself,” as his mother says. Devon also loves darkness, finding it to drown out the craziness that is real life. Unlike his best and only friend Mick, Devon has outgrown his childish behavior and has grown a hatred for things he thinks are childish. As a result, he is dismissive of Mick’s feelings most of the time and gets annoyed by him. After years of rejection, Devon grows a strong desire to try and fit in, leading to concerning and somewhat sociopathic behavior. He becomes obsessed with Heather, desperate to get her attention to a point where he stalks her in order to learn more about her. While Devon initially feels good around Kelsey, he quickly begins to resent how easily Kelsey fits in and makes friends. As Devon becomes increasingly delusional over Heather, his anger and jealousy towards Kelsey gets worse. Devon also isn’t honest and can be very aggressive, mercilessly killing a crow for pooping on his shoulder. Only Mick seems to temporarily negate his aggression thanks to their decade long friendship.

Devon was born to an abusive father who threw things at his mom. When Devon was three his dad left, leaving Devon and his mom alone. Devon's mom works as a house cleaner and doesn't make much money, leaving Devon with very few clothes and few options to eat for food. At school, he usually gets Bs and Cs with the occasional D because he doesn't care enough to truly focus on his work. He and his best and only friend Mick would hang out at an abandoned gas station. Devon enjoyed their hide-out as he could forget about school and the pressure being put on his mother to "be somebody" and not end up like her. Over their ten years of friendship Devon and Mick would constantly do things with each other, saying they were in it together. Eventually Devon gains a desire to be seen as cooler, and in an attempt to do so he slashes his jeans, tears his T-shirts, and slouches more. After a lecture from his mother he stops doing this.

Dinglewood's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives from Step Closer, the first story of Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer.

Pete Dinglewood is the main protagonist of the story.

Chuck Dinglewood is the story’s deuteragonist and Pete’s brother.

Lucy is Pete's aunt on his father's side. Bill relates to Pete being the brother of Chuck with him being the big brother of Lucy. He seems to be uncomfortable with Lucy's husband.

entities.name: Dirk
entities.description: A dirk is a long-bladed thrusting dagger.  Historically, it gained its name from the Highland dirk (Scottish Gaelic biodag) where it was a personal weapon of officers engaged in naval hand-to-hand combat during the Age of Sail as well as the personal sidearm of Highlanders. It was also the traditional sidearm of the Highland Clansman and later used by the officers, pipers, and drummers of Scottish Highland regiments around 1725 to 1800 and by Japanese naval officers.

entities.name: Dominic
entities.description:
Dominic is a major character in Gumdrop Angel, the first story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel. He is the young assistant manager of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza who meets Angel during her step-sister's birthday party.

Dominic is a cute and attractive young man. He's slightly taller than Angel and has broad shoulders, narrow hips, and is fit. Dominic also has dark hair, dark eyes, and strong features.

Dominic is charming and friendly. As an assistant manager, he makes sure that the customers are happy, and he does so by treating them with respect and demonstrating his kind, gentle nature. Dominic's also shown to be rather intelligent, constantly telling clever yet cheesy jokes and having a great memory. However, due to his cooperation with the horrific transformation of young girls into gumdrop statues and him winking at Angel as Ophelia's Birthday Gummy is being revealed, he may possess a rather sadistic side. Still, Dominic is shown to care about Angel and is remorseful when he learns she had eaten the gumdrop nose.

Dominic works part-time as an assistant manager at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza while also attending Graves Academy, a private school for intelligent kids. Due to his position, he is aware of the horrific truth behind the birthday gummies and helps prepare them for birthdays.
entities.short_description: Dominic is a major character in Gumdrop Angel, the first story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel. He is the young assistant manager of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza who meets Angel during her step-sister's birthday party.

entities.name: Dr. Little
entities.description:
Dr. Little is a major character in He Told Me Everything, the third story in Fazbear Frights 7: The Cliffs. He is a highly energetic science teacher who encourages his students to partake in a strange experiment to be accepted into his Science Club. Dr. Little can be considered the story's main antagonist.

Dr. Little, true to his last name, is a small man with glasses and a mustache. He wears a white lab coat with a collared shirt and a brightly colored necktie printed with the design of a DNA helix. Dr. Little will sometimes wears safety goggles over his glasses, which make his eyes look huge and insectoid.

Dr. Little is very energetic and enthusiastic towards science, usually demonstrating experiments involving fire or carefully controlled explosions. While he claims to not have his students work on anything that would put them in danger, his heavy encouragement to participate and stay committed to the lock-in shows a more sinister side to him. Dr. Little also has a morbid sense of humor, joking about dismemberment and death to his students.

Dr. Little is the teacher of the sophomore science class, as well as the leader of the Science Club. He is revered in the town for the "life changing" experiments he hosts in his class and club. This year, his experiment involves Faz-Goo.

entities.name: Dr. Talbert
entities.description:
is a scientist who studies and collects Remnant. He appears in the epilogues of the Fazbear Frights series.

Dr. Talbert has a long, craggy, lined face and graying bushy black hair. In a photo Jake sees, he’s wearing a lab coat.

Doctor Talbert is a scientist who specializes in Remnant, a mysterious bubbling liquid mercury. He studied it because his daughter Renelle was sick as a kid, and he wanted to use remnant to hold onto the good memories in case he lost her. He created a heart shaped pendant made from Remnant. Renelle eventually got better, and he gave her the pendant as a gift.

At some point, his wife dies and the family is torn apart. Dr. Talbert dives deeper into his scientific studies as a coping mechanism and goes as far as kicking Renelle out of his house, sending her to a boarding school.
entities.short_description: is a scientist who studies and collects Remnant. He appears in the epilogues of the Fazbear Frights series.

entities.name: Duane
entities.description:
Duane is a major character from What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel. He is one of Hudson's friends who, while childish about it, tries to include him and makes sure he's alright while part of the construction and set up crew at Fazbear's Fright Horror Attraction.

Duane is muscular with black hair long enough to wear in a glossy ponytail. He wears tight black shirts to show off his muscles.

Duane is very playful and immature, retaining his childish innocence and always telling really bad dad jokes. He isn’t afraid of anything, always the first to charge into dangerous situations. While Duane does care for Hudson, his immature nature causes him to be a jerk and speak without thinking.

Duane, along with Barry, offer Hudson a temporary job at Fazbear's Fright before they all plan to join the Navy. However, Hudson's body was so damaged that he couldn't qualify for it. While he and Barry are setting up the new animatronic, he gets mad at Hudson for being scared. The morning after Hudson's death in the oven, Duane and Barry smell something bad in the kitchen and investigate.

entities.name: Dylan
entities.description:
Dylan is a lanky boy with horn-rimmed glasses, frizzy hair dyed fire-engine red, and braces. He tends to wear shiny silver earrings and a black leather jacket. Dylan gives his short fingernails black polish.

Dylan is very friendly, sophisticated, and knowledgeable. He has a love for weird and dark stories, enjoying the dark and twisty works of Edgar Allan Poe and [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._P._Lovecraft H. P. Lovecraft] amongst other classic horror. Dylan also shows interest in role-playing games and Gothic jewelry, such as Victorian mourning jewelry.

Dylan grew up in Toledo, with cool parents who were supportive of his interests in classic horror and other twisted stories. For his birthday, he was given a hardcover copy of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Call_of_Cthulhu_and_Other_Weird_Stories The Call of Cthulhu and Other Stories]. Dylan and his family moved to town just a week before winter break.

On his first day of high school, Dylan gets chicken nuggets and french fries for lunch and approaches Millie as she's reading "The Fall of the House of Usher." He asks to sit next to her and Millie jokingly asks her imaginary friend if he can sit, which Dylan finds amusing. Dylan then explains that he's new and doesn't know anyone yet. He notices Millie's story and comments that he's a fan of both Poe and H. P. Lovecraft, telling Millie she'd love his dark and twisty stories. Dylan then asks if the school is as lame as it seems and tells Millie she's the only person there that seems cool so far. Millie compliments his jacket and he compliments her jet Victorian mourning jewelry. Millie goes on to explain her favorite kind, but Dylan cuts her off and correctly guesses that it's the type where they weave the hair of the deceased into the jewelry. The bell rings and Dylan asks if it's okay with Millie and her imaginary friend if he sat with them again tomorrow.
entities.short_description: Dylan is a lanky boy with horn-rimmed glasses, frizzy hair dyed fire-engine red, and braces. He tends to wear shiny silver earrings and a black leather jacket. Dylan gives his short fingernails black polish.

entities.name: Dylan Cooper
entities.description:
Dylan Cooper is a minor character in Into the Pit, the first story from Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit, and a secondary antagonist in the video game adaptation. He's a bully at Oswald's school that enjoys picking on others.

In the book, Dylan is only described as "the tallest kid in fifth grade," who clearly enjoyed looming over others. In the game, he has short brown hair, pale skin, and a gray baseball cap. He has a gray jacket, red t-shirt with a gray skull on it, baggy jeans, and blue shoes.

Dylan is a bully, who enjoys picking on others. He likes being tall so that he can look down everyone. He has been bothering Oswald since preschool, and "was the kind of kid who'd pick on anything that made you different."

Dylan Cooper is a bully at Westbrook Elementary and Westbrook Middle School, picking on anything that made others different. He is roughly ten years old as of the plot of Into the Pit. When he was in preschool, there was a cartoon about a big pink ocelot named Oswald, which lead to Dylan and his friends calling Oswald "Oswald the Ocelot." In fifth grade, they were taught about Lee Harvey Oswald in U.S. history, leading to worse name-calling from Dylan.

entities.name: Edward Colter
entities.description:
is the protagonist of Friendly Face, the first story of Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Edward shares many physical characteristics with his mother, such as their hazel eyes, small nose, wide mouth, strong jaw, and auburn hair, although hair is shorter than hers. He and Jack are both considered short for their age

Edward tends to be rather clumsy due to him having issues with hyper focusing. He's also rather nerdy when it comes to science and math.

Edward and Jack were friends ever since they were babies, and the two grew up together. One of Edward's earliest memories is a time right after Christmas. His father had gotten him a huge set of building blocks, and he and Jack built a massive castle. Then, Edward decided to be a dragon and he destroyed the castle. Jack responded by throwing his arms up and shouting "Earthcake." When Edward was three, his father left and moved to the other side of the country. The only time he ever gets anything from his father is on Christmas and his birthday, where he sends $20 and card from him, his new wife, and his three new kids.

entities.name: Emmett Tucker
entities.description:
Emmett Tucker is a major character who debuts in Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster's third story, Find Player Two!.

Emmett is a tall and skinny guy in his early forties with long, greasy hair. He has dark, almost-black eyes. Emmett has yellowed and crooked teeth, and his face heavily wrinkled, getting compared to a wrinkled Halloween mask by Aimee. He wears stained, baggy clothes.

After being released from prison ten years later, Emmett has replaced his long hair with a buzz-cut, a scar bisects his left cheek, and he’s lost a few teeth. His skin is so thin that his veins are visible.

Emmett originally appears to be a creepy man stalking children at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. However, this is not the case. It is revealed that he was looking for his daughter and was in the middle of a custody dispute with his ex-wife.

entities.name: Evan
entities.description:
Evan is a major character in The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He was a caring father who tried looking after his son, Jake, while also serving as overseas as a soldier. He was also the secret identity of Simon, a pretend friend that "lived" in a cabinet in Jake's room.

Evan was described as a man with a buzz cut.

Evan is a confident and determined man who tries to stay optimistic, always giving positive encouragement. He's also rather charming and can make others laugh easily. Evan can be rather superstitious, believing that love and intention can give life. He also has an insatiable desire for knowledge, owning many fiction and non-fiction books of different genres.

After his wife's death, Evan's son suffered brain tumor and he has to call him almost every day. First few months later, Evan gave his son a positive encouragement in hopes to get the brain tumor cured, saying "Keep your chin up," and Jake gleefully accept it. However, the surgery is unsuccessful and Jake has to go through radiation and chemotherapy, and he thus starting to get sullen. Evan tried to encourage Jake for months but he kept refusing to accept the cheer. Evan decided that Jake needed to believe in someone who could pull him out of the horror of his daily life and lead him into the joy of different possibilities, and thus "Simon" was born. Using a backup monitor linked to a hidden one inside the cabinet in Jake's room, Margie would call Evan and have him speak to Jake as Simon. Evan decides that Jake would respond more to someone his own age, so he uses a voice distorter to turn his voice into that of a little kid's.
entities.short_description: Evan is a major character in The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He was a caring father who tried looking after his son, Jake, while also serving as overseas as a soldier. He was also the…

entities.name: Everett Larson
entities.description:
Everett Larson used to consider himself a decent-looking guy in his thirties. Nowadays, he has deep lines forming around his eyes and mouth, which is all he can pay attention to when he looks in the mirror. Larson has dirty blond hair, freckles, blue eyes, and a wide mouth. He describes his face as being hard and closed. Larson wears black slacks, a gray sports jacket, and a white shirt.

He seems very caring towards his family but it’s not shown much due to his job as a detective. He learns to balance life between his work and family, as well as fight for them. Larson has a soft spot for cats and finds them adorable, despite being allergic to their fur. Larson takes his job seriously and wants to protect the innocent, willing to go toe to toe with powerful creatures for the safety of others.

Detective Larson has stayed up late working at the police department. He should have left by now, but he wasn’t in a hurry to get back to his empty apartment. Ever since his wife, Angela, left him, filed for divorce, and tried to make sure he saw their seven-year-old son, Ryan, as little as possible, Larson didn’t see the point of going home. Chief Monahan arrives and gives the detective an envelope. Larson doesn’t bother to open it, which is a case about an urban legend that no one else wanted to take: The Stitchwraith.

Larson doesn’t want to accept it and says he considers him an urban legend. Monahan replies that he’s no longer one. A local teenager, Sarah, had disappeared a week before, and students from the same school she attended, testified that she turned into literal garbage. This morning, the witnesses saw the psychologists again, and say that they believe what they saw, as do the others who’ve claimed to have seen the Stitchwraith.

entities.name: Fairchild Family
entities.description:
The Fairchild family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Danny Fairchild from the tenth book's Sea Bonnies story.

At one point, Rory plans to have a “swing-off” with Danny during recess.

When Mott is in need of a distraction for Rory to dispose of the Sea Bonnies, Danny and his mother conveniently arrive to ask Rory if he wants to join them on Dapuppy’s first leashed walk.

Mr. Fairchild recently got Danny a puppy. Mr. Fairchild kept asking, “Where’s da puppy?” which led to the puppy being named that. Afterward, Danny bugs them to get a kitten to name in a similar manner.

entities.name: Fitzsimmons Family
entities.description:
The Fitzsimmons Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Millie Fitzsimmons from Count the Ways, the third story of Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit.

Millie Fitzsimmons is the main protagonist of Count the Ways, and later reappeared in the final Stitchwraith Stingers from Fazbear Frights #11.

The unnamed grandfather of the Fitzsimmons family is the grandfather of Millie, Cameron, and Hayden. He is the secondary main character of Count the Ways. He is a collector of mechanical objects and owns an old Victorian house.

Jeff Fitzsimmons is Millie's father and Audrey's husband. He is said to be rather ridiculous, flighty, and impractical. Millie calls her parents ridiculous, flighty, and impractical. Jeff and Audrey are considered jokes in the town, famous for their tendency to enthusiastically start projects and then abandon them. When Millie was ten, her parents had bought a run-down but once-beautiful colonial house and attempted to refurbish it, but after three months they ran out of time, money, and energy. As a result, the living room and kitchen were brand new but the bedrooms and bathroom were still run-down. Jeff had also begun repainting the front and one side of the house but gave up due to how expensive and exhausting painting was, as well as not liking ladders.
entities.short_description: The Fitzsimmons Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Millie Fitzsimmons from Count the Ways, the third story of Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit.

entities.name: Fremont Family
entities.description:
The Fremont Family comprises the relatives of Mia Fremont from The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights #5: Bunny Call.

Mia Fremont is one of the main protagonists in The Man in Room 1280. She is a perky and energetic nurse who works at Hercules Hospital.

Lucas is Mia's younger cousin. Not much is known about him other than that he is a bit mischievous and was always up to no good.

Category:Fazbear Frights: Characters Category:FF5: Characters
entities.short_description: The Fremont Family comprises the relatives of Mia Fremont from The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights #5: Bunny Call.

entities.name: Gabrielle
entities.description:
Gabrielle is a girl Oswald meets on the first day of school in Into the Pit. She also appears in the game and the interative novel adaptations.

In the original short story, Gabrielle is described as having curly black hair and big, brown eyes.

In the graphic novel, she has light skin, shoulder-length hair, a blue tank top, pink pants, and black flats. In the videogame adaptation, she is of African descent, with dark skin, bushy hair, a turquoise blouse with matching shoes, and a blue skirt.

Gabrielle is a shy but friendly girl who is the first new student in Oswald's town in a long time. Her main trait is that she loves to read Greek mythology and other tales of heroes, with a specific Greek myth book being a comfort book for her to read when she needs to be brave. She says that seeing heroes battle monsters can put her relatively minor problems into perspective.

entities.name: Gene
entities.description:
Gene, also known as Gene Junior, is a character in In the Flesh, the second story of Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. He is a depressed hacker who uses his skills to get an early copy of Springtrap's Revenge.

Gene is overweight due to his depression and mother’s cooking.

Gene is a very intelligent and nerdy person. He is also rather depressed and lacks confidence in most of his abilities, but prides himself on his gaming and hacking skills.

entities.name: Gigi
entities.description:
Gigi is a major character in Lonely Freddy, the second story from Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. She is Alec and Hazel's aunt who tries convincing her younger sister that their behavior is normal.

Gigi has no children and no desire for any, but is happy to give advice to her younger sister whenever she needs it. When Alec was ten, she suggested that Meg not single him out and that they switch to organic milk, having found studies that claimed the added hormones in regular dairy increased aggression in kids. Meg tells Gigi that Alec seems to be in his own world, but Gigi tries to offer an optimistic outlook and says Alec will be a great leader one day. Meg then tells Gigi she wants Alec to be more like a kid named Gavin, but Gigi finds his constant smile creepy and not desirable.

Just three days before Hazel's tenth birthday party, Gigi meets up with Meg, Alec, and Hazel at Freddy Fazbear’s Family Pizzeria. While Alec and Hazel play arcade games, Gigi joins Meg as she discusses plans for Hazel's party with a Party Prepper, unable to aid Meg in adding things to the package as she doesn't quite understand what Freddy's has to offer and is repulsed by the food. Eventually Meg asks Hazel if she wants to go into the Wind Tunnel for a chance to win a Yarg Foxy. Confused, Gigi asks what a Yarg Foxy is and the Party Prepper points towards the prize counter, explaining it can swing a hook. Gigi then asks about the Lonely Freddys, so the Party Prepper does a demo for it. Gigi makes a rude remark about unwanted kids and asks why the Yarg Foxy can't just be bought. When Alec kindly convinces Hazel to add the Wind Tunnel to her party, Gigi is shocked and asks if Meg switched to organic milk.

Back at Meg's house, Hazel continues to misbehave in front of Gigi and storms off to her room when Meg confronts her. Gigi brushes off Hazel's behavior as her just turning a certain age, then notices The Plan Planner. Gigi tells Meg that, while she thinks her and Ian are good parents, she wonders if their attempts to make Alec and Hazel "normal" have had the opposite effect. Meg snaps at her older sister then tells her she just wants to be a normal family. Gigi responds that Meg already is one. Category:Fazbear Frights: Characters Category:Fazbear Frights: Alec's Family Category:FF2: Characters

entities.description:
Girard's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Pickle Girard.

Ory is Shelly and Pickle's younger brother.

Mr. Girard is Shelly, Pickle, and Ory's father. He is a smart person and travels to do consulting for big companies.

entities.name: Granny Foster
entities.description:
Granny Foster is Hudson's grandmother who appeared in What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel.

Granny Foster's appearance had sharp features and she stands 5 foot and 1 inches. She had thick, wrinkled, dark skin like "cracked feathers" due to going out in the sun frequently, and her jaw-length hair was white. She also had unusually bright blue eyes.

She wears big men's plaid flannel shirts with baggy jeans. She had a deep and gravelly voice, with her guttural tones described as if a demon was talking.

She is an agnostic seer, claiming to be able to see the future but hesitates to tell anyone about it. She does not believe in any belief systems, including voodoo, but she likes using voodoo dolls to mete out justice to negative people, believing that the dolls were "a hoot". Granny Foster is able to practice some voodoo arts and also use herbs to heal whatever needs to be healed.
entities.short_description: Granny Foster is Hudson's grandmother who appeared in What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel.

entities.name: Greg
entities.description:
Greg is the protagonist in Fetch, the first story in the book of the same name. He is a nerdy teenage boy who hopes to use controversial science in order to control the world around him and get what he wants, which leads him to discovering an animatronic that seems to align with his goals.

Greg has a long face, eyes that are close together, and a small nose. He has long, wavy blond hair, average height, muscular arms and legs, and a “great smile”. Despite his muscles, Greg has narrow shoulders and a thin torso with a slight chest.

Greg is very nerdy and loves all forms of science, his passion earning him the title of teacher’s pet. He doesn’t like stereotypical masculine things like cars and sports, causing strife between him and his father. Greg desires more control in his life and plans to manipulate the Zero Point Field in order to get whatever he wants. Greg's endeavors in controlling the field has led him to become egotistical and somewhat controlling over his friends, persistently begging them into joining him in his experiments while also hiding his true intentions from them.

Greg grew up with a decently successful family. His father, a contractor, worked for long periods of time in order to afford big houses and expensive cars. Greg's uncle Darrin, however, was a wealthy, successful inventor of car parts and had amazing luck with investments and money in general. While Greg's father hates Dare, Greg loves him. When Greg was about four years old, he began to cry over a stuffed octopus in a claw machine he was unable to get. Dare tapped the glass of the machine with his right index finger and told Greg in a deep voice that he had "the Magic Finger of Luck." Dare managed to get the octopus first try, starting an ongoing joke that almost always worked.
entities.short_description: Greg is the protagonist in Fetch, the first story in the book of the same name. He is a nerdy teenage boy who hopes to use controversial science in order to control the world around him and get what he wants, which…

entities.name: Greg's Family
entities.description:
Greg's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Greg from Fetch, the first story of Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch.

Greg is the protagonist of the second Fazbear Frights book's first story.

Darrin, aka Uncle Dare, is a major character in Fetch.

Later, Hillary takes a part-time job as a front desk clerk at one of the hotels. One day, Hillary and Steven get caught up in an intense discussion and simply say "Okay" when Greg asks if his friends could come over. Later, Dare is attacked and gets his finger bitten off. Hillary comes downstairs and finds Greg at the door, and when he notices she's crying she explains what happened. Greg goes outside and eventually Hillary follows him out to inform him that Dare will be in surgery for a while. When Greg is taken to a police station, Hillary travels all the way from Olympia with tears in her eyes. Once home, Steven berates Greg and Hillary steps in, simply saying Steven's name as Greg runs off to his room.
entities.short_description: Greg's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Greg from Fetch, the first story of Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch.

entities.name: Gretta
entities.description:
Gretta is a major character in Find Player Two!, the third story in Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Gretta has short red curls, flawless pale skin, green eyes, and model-worthy features. She rarely wears makeup and cuts her own hair, which results in her curls being asymmetrical.

entities.name: Grim
entities.description:
is a homeless man that appears in the epilogues of Fetch, Bunny Call, and Gumdrop Angel.

He has a long face with a matted beard, and keeps his long string brown hair under a gray hat. He is 5'8, but slouches down several inches. He wears old hiking boots and carries a muddied blanket to prevent being seen.

The events follow directly after Out of Stock, where Grim, who lives near some train tracks, sees the Stitchwraith collecting something from the rails. He looks closer to see that it is collecting the pieces of the Plushtrap Chaser and stuffing them into a bag, before wandering off into the darkness.

After seeing the Stitchwraith, he decides to move into a shed opposite the side of town. He spots the hooded figure again and decides to follow it to investigate. He is brought to a storage warehouse and notices an Ella doll in the bag. Eventually, Grim is too freaked out to stay and retreats.
entities.short_description: is a homeless man that appears in the epilogues of Fetch, Bunny Call, and Gumdrop Angel.

entities.name: Hadi
entities.description:
Hadi is a major character in Fetch, the first story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He's a rather popular teenage boy who unknowingly gets dragged into his friend Greg's experiments with the Zero Point Field.

Hadi has curly black hair. Many girls in his school find him to be good-looking, with no one having anything more negative than "fine" to say about him.

Hadi is relentlessly positive and optimistic, with a sunny disposition that he pulls off flawlessly. He is also rather confident and courageous. Hadi is accepted by the popular crowd despite hanging out with Greg and Cyril, the two nerdiest kids in school. He himself is also rather nerdy, having won a science fair prize and gotten into Advanced Scientific Theory, but still enjoys teasing his friends about their less popular behaviors.

One stormy Saturday night, Greg and Cyril visit Hadi's house to play games and eat junk food. When the seaside Washington town is robbed of power by the latest storm, Hadi convinces his parents to let him and his friends bike to Greg's house to play a new tabletop strategy game instead of playing board games with them. Once there, however, Greg instead enlists them to join him as he breaks into an abandoned pizzeria nearby. The trio manage to break a lock off a heavy service door and jam it open, allowing them to sneak into the pizzeria through a storage room.
entities.short_description: Hadi is a major character in Fetch, the first story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He's a rather popular teenage boy who unknowingly gets dragged into his friend Greg's experiments with the Zero Point Field.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Character / franchise art © Scott Cawthon / Steel Wool / rights holders (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Harper
entities.description:
is a major character in 1:35 A.M., the first story in the book of the same name. She's Delilah's upbeat and spiritual best friend who tries her best to support Delilah following her divorce.

Harper is thin with huge blue eyes and blonde hair she likes to tie up in different styles. When Delilah first talks to Harper about Ella, she has an “exotic Medusa look” with her hair in a dozen or so braids coiled around her head, heavy colorful makeup, and a skintight green dress. Later, her hair is in a long, high ponytail and she wears a fifties-style, full-skirted floral dress with a multitude of bracelets around her thin wrists.

Harper is vivacious and likes to act mischievous, calling herself a free-spirit. She is also very eccentric and spiritual, believing in signs and other ideas that Delilah considers unrealistic. Harper isn’t as easily bothered as her best friend, but also doesn’t process things in an organized way either. Despite their opposing views, Harper and Delilah are very supportive of each other, and Harper is always willing to help Delilah out whenever she needs it.

Harper and Delilah landed in foster care together six years prior to the events of the story. Despite being opposites in both looks and personality, the two teamed up to help each other get through their scheduled life with Gerald, the ex-military husband of the couple that took them in, and were determined to make the foster home their last. They managed to make their friendship work and remained friends after.
entities.short_description: is a major character in 1:35 A.M., the first story in the book of the same name. She's Delilah's upbeat and spiritual best friend who tries her best to support Delilah following her divorce.

entities.name: Hazel
entities.description:
Hazel is a main antagonist of Lonely Freddy, the second story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. She is Alec's nice younger sister who just wants to get along with her older brother and devises a plan so they can work together and get along.

Hazel has fine blonde ringlets that are twisted up in stiff bows. She also has evenly spaced freckles, straight teeth, and light-green eyes.

Hazel is very kind and helpful, helping with chores at home and around her classroom. She is also rather skilled and smart, playing the piano well and getting straight As in class. Hazel is a very caring person, making sure no one feels left out during her birthdays and wanting to be close with Alec despite his hostile attitude towards her, which can make her shy and nervous around him. She tends to follow the rules even when by herself, but is willing to break them for Alec’s sake. Hazel also rarely cries.

Hazel was born in April and named after a beloved grandmother. After her birth, her parent's attitude towards Alec shifted based on her nice and sweat personality. Hazel was showered with attention and praise by her parents, but through eavesdropping she learns that they only do so out of guilt for worrying about Alec, even having moved closer to their aunt Gigi just for him. Hazel would do everything to get along with Alec, such as baking him cookies in her toy oven after their parents ignored his pleas for sweats, laughing at an unintentional joke he made during a camping trip he ruined by scaring her, and adding Alec's name to the card during Mother's Day after he forgot. Despite this, Alec would continue to coldly dismiss Hazel. She eventually takes notice of Alec's love of Freddy Fazbear's and the Yarg Foxy character. Eventually, Hazel decides to get Alec a Yarg Foxy plush and tells her parents that she wants one.
entities.short_description: Hazel is a main antagonist of Lonely Freddy, the second story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. She is Alec's nice younger sister who just wants to get along with her older brother and devises a plan so they can work…

entities.name: Heather Anders
entities.description:
Heather Anders is a major character in The New Kid, the third story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM. She's a popular teenage girl that Devon becomes obsessed with.

Heather is pretty with shiny straight auburn hair. She paints her nails red.

Despite her popularity, Heather is pretty shallow. She believes justice is payback and shrugs any possible negative outcomes from payback off as accidents. Heather has a strong dislike for Devon, being sarcastic around him and giving him scornful looks. She tells Kelsey that she loves DIY and is a really good designer, although Kelsey later claims she wasn’t much help.

Heather is one of the most popular girls in Devon's ninth-grade class. A week prior to the story, Heather complained to her friends about her four-year-old twin sisters, Halley and Hope. Unknown to the group, Devon was listening in. That same day, their English class handed out an assignment to write an original short story, and Devon decided to write about a killer bouncy house eating the twins in order to get Heather's attention.
entities.short_description: Heather Anders is a major character in The New Kid, the third story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM. She's a popular teenage girl that Devon becomes obsessed with.

entities.name: Henderson Family
entities.description:
The Henderson Family comprises the relatives of Gillian Henderson from The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

Gillian Henderson is Margie's close friend and the mother of three children. She sometimes help out in taking care of Jake.

Dave Henderson is Gillian's husband. He is an accountant and was only mentioned once.

Patty Henderson is Gillian's daughter and one of Jake's friends. She was first mentioned by Jake when talking to Simon about his friends. At some point, Margie took Patty to the arcade to win the smiley-face eraser for her, so Margie can use it for the Simon doll.
entities.short_description: The Henderson Family comprises the relatives of Gillian Henderson from The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

entities.name: Hope
entities.description:
Hope is a major character from Prankster, the first story Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Hope is described by Jeremiah as naturally beautiful. She has shoulder-length ash-blonde hair that falls in soft waves around her keen-featured face. Her big eyes are wide-set, brown, and doe-like. Hope’s lips are delicate-looking pink petals. On her right ring finger is a silver ring with an aquamarine in it for her birthstone.

Category:FNAF Articles Category:Fazbear Frights: Characters Category:FF11: Characters
entities.short_description: Hope is a major character from Prankster, the first story Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

entities.name: Hudson
entities.description:
is the main protagonist of What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights #8: Gumdrop Angel. He's a severely traumatized young man who struggles to move on after his abusive step-father and neglectful mother are both killed in a fire. Hudson's friends eventually convince him to become a security guard at Fazbear's Fright Horror Attraction, where he works despite his illogical fear of the old things around the attraction.

Hudson is a skinny six feet, one inch tall man with short blond hair, a few days old pale beard, blue eyes, and a wide mouth full of straight white teeth.

Hudson is a victim of child abuse, reacting mainly out of traumatic responses. Years of living in fear have caused him to be paranoid and easily frightened. Hudson also gets irritated and defensive when confronted about his past, leading to poor treatment from others. While he finds a bit of enjoyment of getting back at those who are mean to him, he never acts on these desires. Hudson is constantly spacing out when he thinks of his past, although he has many suppressed memories and is only able to face his past in snippets. He actively tries to grow past his early life but he still feels alone in the world and doesn't take rejection well, causing him to revert back. Still, Hudson does find comfort when around his friends, Barry and Duane. He tries acting playful and relaxed around them, with varying degrees of success.

Hudson grew up happy and cheerful. He and his best friends Barry and Duane loved going to an old-fashioned soda fountain ice-cream parlor called Charlie's, a tradition they kept into their adulthood. His Granny Foster would always give him wise and spiritual life advice, such as heat and fire purging. However, Hudson's life took a turn for the worse after his father, Steven, took his life after a bad deal cost him his small business.
entities.short_description: is the main protagonist of What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights #8: Gumdrop Angel. He's a severely traumatized young man who struggles to move on after his abusive step-father and neglectful mother are both…

entities.name: Hudson's Family
entities.description:
Hudson's Family from Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Hudson from What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel.

Hudson (full name unknown) was the son of Steven and unnamed mother. He is the employee of Fazbear's Fright: The Horror Attraction and the main protagonist of What We Found. After going through his stepfather's abuse, he still has memories of his painful past which later causes himself to suffer from severed psyche, causing him to experience visual hallucinations in the horror attraction.

Steven was the biological father of Hudson from his childhood. Hudson remembers great memories of his father, and was described to be very fun and attentive. When he played with his son, he is always up for throwing the ball, playing a game, or just roughhousing. However, he struggled with mental illness for many years. When his small business failed and risked his family's livelihood, he committed suicide.

After Steven's death, Hudson's mother was remarried to Lewis.
entities.short_description: Hudson's Family from Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Hudson from What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel.

entities.name: Isaac
entities.description:
is a major character in Out of Stock, the third story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He's one of Oscar's loyal friends who sticks by his side even after he takes the Plushtrap Chaser.

Not much is said about Isaac's appearance other than that he's short. In the graphic novel, he has blond hair covered by a black beanie, blue eyes, and a pointy nose.

Isaac is a very loyal friend, sticking by Oscar’s side even when he gets them into trouble or has to cancel plans. He's very understanding of Oscar’s financial situation and is willing to share with him. Despite Isaac's occasional teasing and playfully smug remarks, he tends to be less courageous than Oscar and Raj.

Isaac had met Raj and Oscar on the playground in third grade, and they've been best friends ever since. He is very understanding of Oscar's different financial situation. Isaac and Raj always change their plans and try to include Oscar whenever they can. At home, Isaac has to care for his younger brother Jordan until his mom gets home from work at three o'clock. He likes to spend his free time spending his allowance at the mall with Raj and hanging out with Oscar.

entities.description:
Isaac's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Isaac from Out of Stock, the third story of Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch.

Jordan is Isaac's brother. Isaac has to walk him home from school, or his mom would freak out.

entities.name: Jack
entities.description:
Jack is a major character that appears in Dance with Me, the second story in Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer. He is part of a group of thieves that steal from others to survive and share amongst each other.

Jack is a sharp-nosed and scrawny white guy with a lot of tattoos. Kasey compares him to a rat.

Jack is twitchy and fidgety, always seeming nervous when he's really just excited. He is also somewhat flamboyant. Jack and AJ have a habit of being reckless and blowing through the money they steal through partying. Jack likes to tease Kasey a lot, but it’s good-natured. He also doesn’t believe in superstition.

Jack, along with AJ, are part of a two-man group who commit petty theft. When they encounter Kasey, impressed by her skill in theft, they invite her to be a part of their group. Kasey agrees.
entities.short_description: Jack is a major character that appears in Dance with Me, the second story in Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer. He is part of a group of thieves that steal from others to survive and share amongst each other.

entities.name: Jack
entities.description:
Jack is the main protagonist of The Puppet Carver, the first story of Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Not much is known about Jack's physical appearance, although he is implied to be somewhat overweight due to Becky saying he could go down a few pant sizes.

entities.short_description: Jack is the main protagonist of The Puppet Carver, the first story of Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

entities.name: Jack Weston
entities.description:
Jack Weston is a deutagonist in Friendly Face, the first story of Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Jack has full, thick lips that are naturally upturned into a smile and warm brown eyes with faint crinkles at the corners due to smiling so often. He also has a slightly flat nose and a broad chin. Jack and Edward are both considered short for their age. Jack has black hair that is the same color as Faraday’s fur.

Jack is smart, good-natured kid. He's rather nerdy when it comes to math and science, and he makes his nerdy nature known in the way he speaks and acts.

Edward and Jack were friends ever since they were babies, and the two grew up together. When Edward and Jack were two-years-old, Edward's father had gotten him a huge set of building blocks for Christmas, and he and Jack built a massive castle. Then, Edward decided to be a dragon and he destroyed the castle. Jack responded by throwing his arms up and shouting "Earthcake." Edward and Jack quickly noted they're outcasts in school and jokingly say they live in their own universe. At the start of junior high, Edward's mother buys him an antique walnut desk, which upsets Jack because his desk isn't as neat. Edward lets Jack use the desk for homework, and for the past two years Jack uses the desk while Edward works on his bed.
entities.short_description: Jack Weston is a deutagonist in Friendly Face, the first story of Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.
