entities.name: Jake
entities.description:
Jake is the deuteragonist of the Stitchwraith Stingers and the main protagonist of The Real Jake. He was a sick young boy who lived with his caretaker, Margie, until his death. Sometime after, he becomes a ghost and possesses the Stitchwraith along with Andrew.

Jake is bald with grayish skin, sunken cloudy green eyes, and dark circles on his cheekbones and under his eyes. His body is also bony. As he got weaker his skin became almost translucent gray, and it’s so tightly stretched on his face that the perfect contours of his facial bones and skull could be seen.

Before the brain tumor, Jake had a round freckled face, bright green eyes, a big smile, and a thick tangle of brown curls that were usually falling over his eyes. He liked having his hair long.

Jake refuses to sit around in bed in pajamas and underwear all day, so he’s usually wearing T-shirts and shorts, such as a pair of green shorts and a tan T-shirt. He also has slip-on sandals under his bed for whenever he moves around. Margie had a shirt with a smiley face wearing a baseball cap with his favorite team's logo made for him.
entities.short_description: Jake is the deuteragonist of the Stitchwraith Stingers and the main protagonist of The Real Jake. He was a sick young boy who lived with his caretaker, Margie, until his death. Sometime after, he becomes a ghost and…

entities.name: Jake's Family
entities.description:
Jake's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Jake from The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

Jake was the only son of Evan and Roxanne. He is the protagonist of The Real Jake and throughout the Stitchwraith Stingers saga. After death, his soul inhabits Simon and, later on, his mask will later be used by Phineas Taggart to create the Stitchwraith.

Evan was Roxanne's husband and the father of Jake. He is a military soldier who is drafted and serving out overseas. He is also the secret identity of Simon, the animatronic doll that sits in Jake's closet. He sadly dies from an IED detonation in the vehicle he was in out at sea, and it's kept a secret from Jake.

Roxanne was Evan's wife and the mother of Jake. She is briefly mentioned in the story. She died when Jake was young. Due to Evan being overseas, Margie is hired to take care of Jake instead.
entities.short_description: Jake's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Jake from The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

entities.name: Jason
entities.description:
Jason is a major character in In the Flesh, the second story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. He's Matt's best friend and roommate who unknowingly annoys Matt with his chill attitude towards life.

Jason is considered sloppy, unattractive, and poorly dressed by Matt.

Jason is always relaxed and easygoing. He is also nice and caring, trying to remain friendly with Matt despite his friend considering him unsophisticated and unambitious. However, Jason isn’t afraid to take action against Matt when he crosses a line.

Jason is roommates with his friend, Matt, living in an apartment. Jason and Matt have a double date with two girls, Meghan and Eva. Matt angrily leaves and makes them pay the bill, much to Jason's dismay. Fed up with Matt's arrogance, he decides to move out.
entities.short_description: Jason is a major character in In the Flesh, the second story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. He's Matt's best friend and roommate who unknowingly annoys Matt with his chill attitude towards life.

entities.name: Jeff
entities.description:
Jeff is a major character in Into the Pit, the first story from Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit, and later makes a minor appearance in the Stitchwraith Stingers. In a constant state of exhaustion, Jeff is the owner and sole employee of Jeff's Pizza.

Jeff constantly looks tired and miserable with dark hair sticking up in weird places and alarming bags under his heavy-lidded, bloodshot eyes. He wears an apron stained with new and old tomato sauce. Oswald says Jeff looks about a hundred years old when he’s probably just thirty and compares his eyes, his apron, and his slow speech and movement to that of a “zombie pizza chef.”

In the video game adaptation, Jeff has darker skin and pale blue eyes. He's seen wearing a blue vest, an orange shirt, orange pants, and black shoes.

While Jeff is exhausted and speaks with a monotone voice, he is ultimately a nice man simply trying to run a business. While he does get upset to see Oswald having hid in the ball pit, his anger quickly fades and he returns to his usual self. In the game, he is a little bit dry and sarcastic, and seems suspicious of Oswald but still gives him keys to different rooms.

entities.description:
Jeremiah is the protagonist of Prankster, the first story in Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Not much is known about Jeremiah's physical appearance besides the fact that he wears business-casual khakis and button-down polo shirts to work. On his birthday, he puts on a jacket.

entities.name: Jess
entities.description:
Jess is a character from The Cliffs, the first story in the book of the same name. She's a bespectacled copy editor that tries to reconnect with Robert after he isolates himself from others.

Jess isn’t described much other than that she wears eyeglasses. In the graphic novel, she has a round face, brown eyes, blue glasses, a pointy nose, and bright red hair that is half shaven. Jess also has black eyeliner and pink lipstick.

Jess is nice and a self-confessed “grammar nerd.” Being a single parent, she relates to Robert a lot and acts caring towards him. Jess also likes joking around and being playful.

Jess was hired as a copy editor for the magazine company at the same time Robert was. They were good friends and used to chat in the past, but when Anna died Robert cut himself off in order to focus his attention of Tyler.
entities.short_description: Jess is a character from The Cliffs, the first story in the book of the same name. She's a bespectacled copy editor that tries to reconnect with Robert after he isolates himself from others.

entities.name: Jessica
entities.description:
Jessica is the one of the main protagonists of Together Forever, the third story of Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Jessica and Brittany are considered the prettiest girls in their class. Jessica has bright-red nails, shiny blonde hair, big blue eyes, high cheekbones, a pert nose, full lips, a perfect petite figure, and the most up-to-date fashions and makeup like lip gloss. For most of the story, she wears a tawny faux suede miniskirt that buttons up at the front, a cream-colored silk tank, and a pair of lace-up booties that match her skirt.

Jessica is shown to be extremely egotistical and have somewhat of a god complex. She believes that she is worthy of royalty status alongside her friend Brittany and viewing their boyfriends as trash that they can replace on a whim. She hates Cindy and Mindy simply because they don't cry or fall victim to her and Brittany's bullying, even willing to program Rosie Porkchop to injure them in retaliation.

Jessica and her friend Brittany were voted as Homecoming Queen and Princess at a school dance. The increased attention they subsequently received inflated their egos, believing themselves to be worthy of royalty. Jessica was also in a relationship with a man on the football team. Jessica dislikes a pair of girls named Cindy and Mindy.
entities.short_description: Jessica is the one of the main protagonists of Together Forever, the third story of Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

entities.name: Joel D'Agostino
entities.description:
Joel D'Agostino is the main protagonist of Kids at Play, the second story of Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Joel inherited his father's strong features and his mother's big and heavily lashed brown eyes. He is tall with narrow hips and thick, wavy black hair. Many girls consider Joel good-looking or gorgeous, with many complimenting his usual outfit of jeans and black T-shirts. However, he rarely takes showers.

entities.name: Julius
entities.description:
is the main antagonist of The Breaking Wheel, the second story in Fazbear Frights 7: The Cliffs. He is a cruel and relentless bully who enjoys tormenting others and bragging about his intelligence. When Reed traps him in his own exoskeleton suit, he is filled with rage and promises to tear the outcast apart.

Julius has artful wavy blond hair that cascades down the back of his head. Shelly says his hair is “dreamy.” Julius is tall and muscular with big, long limbs and a V-shaped torso. Many find him to be attractive. His canine teeth are unusually pointed. Julius always wears expensive clothes, such as skinny black jeans, expensive basketball shoes, designer shirts, and cashmere scarves.

After his prolonged torture in his exosuit, Julius is described by Reed as a fleshy octopus-like mass of pulpy crushed limbs attached to a metal frame. His face is slack due to the bone structure of his forehead, cheeks, and jaw having been pulverized. His features are so distorted that he is said to resemble a crudely sewn cloth doll. His wavy blond hair is now sticky and stringy with congealed blood and fresh blood pools from his face, which is compared to a misshapen sponge. His mouth is sagging and his eyes have rolled back in his head, showing the murky, cloudy whites. His flesh and stylish clothing have been pierced by puncture wounds caused by cracked bones and are smeared with dried and fresh blood. His previously cream-colored scarf looped around his neck is also saturated.

Julius is an odd combination of jock, brain, and bully. He loves to brag about his talents and his self-righteous beliefs to everyone, and he demonstrates his intelligence through his skills at robotics, creating a fully functional exoskeleton suit. When things don’t go his way, Julius will complain and blame his problems on others. He also thrives on insults and bullying, seemingly getting euphoric when humiliating and physically hurting others.

entities.name: Kasey
entities.description:
is the protagonist of Dance with Me, the second story in Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer. She is a homeless woman who steals from others in order to survive. After stealing a pair of novelty glasses, however, Kasey starts longing for a better life and tries changing for the better.

Kasey is small and skinny with an "honest face" and long hair fixed into braids. She usually wears an old jacket, a backpack, ripped faded jeans, and battered boots held together by duct tape.

Despite being a theif, Kasey feels guilty whenever she steals from people. She also doesn’t like partying, usually staying in solitude. Unlike Jack and AJ, Kasey is far more careful and cautious, living with slight worry in the back of her mind. Eventually, she begins to feel sad and regret towards her current life and longs for a more normal life.

Kasey is part of a group of thieves with Jack and AJ. She was kicked out of her mother's house at 17 and later dropped out of high school. Faced with the prospect of working multiple jobs to support herself. Kasey resorted to petty theft. Jack and AJ noticed her skill and invited her to join their gang.

entities.name: Kelsey
entities.description:
Kelsey is the tritagonist of The New Kid, the third story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM. He's a new teen at Devon and Mick's high school who makes friends with everyone, although seemingly prefers being around the two outcasts. Depending on how one interprets the story, Kelsey could be considered the main antagonist.

Kelsey is good-looking with wavy blond hair, blue eyes, straight teeth, and broad shoulders. He usually wears jeans torn at the knees and a watch. On his first day of school, he's wearing cool ripped jeans and a faded black T-shirt. The next day, he wears baggy black pants with a gray T-shirt and a black-and-red plaid shirt tied at his waist.

Kelsey is a very friendly, funny, and charismatic person, which allows him to make friends easily. He is also very observant, constantly evaluating people. Kelsey is very keen on justice, believing it to balance the scales by removing the downside so it can’t outweigh the upside. He likes legal shows and courtroom dramas, claiming to want to be a “real judge” someday. Kelsey also enjoys urban exploring. Despite Heather’s clear interest in him, Kelsey gets rather annoyed by her and her friend group interrupting his plans, although he never raises any objections and simply lets them derail the plan.

Kelsey starts his first day at his new school hanging out near the stairs and watching as other kids enter the school, including Devon. Kelsey manages to become friends with many of the kids at his school, including Mick. Mick properly introduces Devon to Kelsey and they begin to hang out together during lunch. The next day, Mick explains to Kelsey what happened to their old clubhouse. Kelsey promises the pair he will let them use a workshop at a farmhouse his parents purchased for their hangout. The next day, in their social studies class, the topic of justice is discussed. Kelsey explains that justice is something that removes the downs so it doesn't outweigh the ups. Heather, a pretty popular girl that Kelsey was getting along with, views justice as payback, and when asked if payback goes too far simply says that accidents happen. Only Mick and Kelsey don't find the joke funny.

Kelsey is the tritagonist of the third Fazbear Frights book's third story.

Kelsey's unnamed mother packs him lunch and makes great chicken salad.

Kelsey's unnamed father is a contractor.

entities.name: Kimberly Bergstrom
entities.description:
Kimberly Bergstrom is a major character in Fetch, the first story from Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. She's a rather intelligent teenage girl that shares similar interests with Greg, such as researching random event generators.

Kimberly is pretty with long inky black hair and "amazing" green eyes.

Kimberly is shown to be incredibly smart and possibly nerdy, since she’s in Advanced Scientific Theory and has the same interests as Greg. She is also graceful and friendly, and she is said to love dogs.

Kimberly's mother was fifty-one years old when she was born and her father was older, making Kimberly a miracle baby. When Kimberly was in first grade, a new kid named Greg moved in about a mile down the street, although the two didn't meet until second grade. As Kimberly grew older, she became interested in topics related to random event generators, or REGs, such as how they get spikes before big sporting events. She tried talking about the machines to her parents, but both dismiss them.

entities.name: Lewis
entities.description:
Lewis was Hudson's stepfather who appeared in What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel.

He was balding, short, and always smoked black cherry tobacco with his pipe. He wore plaid vests.

Unlike Steven, who was Hudson's biological father, Lewis is a complete opposite. Lewis is a cold, violent, pitiless brute of a stepfather. He is physically and verbally abusive towards Hudson when he was a child, brutally punishing him over the slightest of reasons for years. His assaults and actions gave Hudson severe trauma.

Lewis married Hudson's mother after Steven's suicide. He once slammed Hudson's head for not finishing his homework. When Hudson vomited the floor after smelling reflex, Lewis created a barrier at the doorway of Hudson's bedroom piling up all the toys he owned. Almost every day, Lewis physically beats him up, telling him that he was nothing.
entities.short_description: Lewis was Hudson's stepfather who appeared in What We Found, the third story of Fazbear Frights 8: Gumdrop Angel.

entities.name: Lydia
entities.description:
Lydia is a major recurring character in To Be Beautiful, the second story of Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit. She is the leader of "the Beautifuls," a nickname given to a group of four cheerleaders in Sarah's high school.

Lydia is pretty with long and lustrous honey blonde hair, cerulean blue eyes, a rosy complexion, and a tiny button nose. She’s slender but curvy, and Sarah says she's pretty enough to be a model. Lydia makes sure the Beautifuls wear matching outfits. At the start of the story, she wears a short black dress with a white collar and cuffs.

Like the rest of the Beautifuls, Lydia is incredibly vain. She tends to take advantage of her looks and status to get things she normally wouldn't, such as an older date in order to attend prom. Lydia also judges people based on their looks and wealth, making rude remarks about and mocking an angry saleslady since she works in a department store and barely makes minimum wage.

Lydia is the leader of a group of popular cheerleaders at Sarah's high school, with the other members being Jillian, Tabitha, and Emma. Sarah calls the Beautifuls and wishes to join them, but has low self esteem. One day, Sarah sees them going down the hall in black and white outfits. During lunch, the Beautifuls sit at their own table while Sarah, Abby, and other nerds sit at what they call the "loser table." A few days later, Lydia and the Beautifuls wear cute skinny jeans with fitted jewel-colored tops and matching slip-on canvas shoes. Sarah tries sitting with them during lunch, however they ignore her and continue their conversations without her. Sarah later sees them outside the Brown Cow with their boyfriends.
entities.short_description: Lydia is a major recurring character in To Be Beautiful, the second story of Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit. She is the leader of "the Beautifuls," a nickname given to a group of four cheerleaders in Sarah's high…

entities.name: Mackenzie Family
entities.description:
The Mackenzie family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Bob Mackenzie from the first story of Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call.

Bob Mackenzie is the husband of Wanda Mackenzie and the father of Cindy, Tyler, and Aaron. He is the main protagonist of the Bunny Call story.

Wanda Mackenzie is the wife of Bob Mackenzie and the mother of three children.

Cindy Mackenzie is the daughter of Bob and Wanda Mackenzie, and the sister of Tyler and Aaron. She is the youngest of her siblings.
entities.short_description: The Mackenzie family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Bob Mackenzie from the first story of Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call.

entities.name: Mandy Mason
entities.description:
Mandy Marie Mason is the protagonist of The Scoop, the second story in Fazbear Frights 12: Felix the Shark.

Mandy has heterochromia, with one brown iris and one green iris. To rebel against the school’s obligatory uniform of a plaid skirt, white shirt, cardigan, and knee-high socks, she dyes her blonde hair in different colors such as black, cotton-candy pink, and a purple that fades into a light lavender at the end of the story. Mandy usually puts her hair in two, sci-fi styled buns, although she lets it down past her shoulders at the end of the story. She likes to wear boots, and her usual outfits includes leggings.

entities.name: Margie
entities.description:
30 (The Real Jake)33 (Stitchwraith Stingers)

is minor character in the second Stitchwraith Stingers and the deuteragonist in The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. She was a caring woman who took care of Jake while his father Evan served overseas. After both of their deaths, she continues to live in the house and is interrogated by Detective Larson.

Margie is a pretty young woman standing at a height of five foot three inches. She has almost cartoon-large eyes and shoulder-length light brown hair that's usually damp. Jake says her big eyes make her look like a “cartoon princess.” She has full lips and full cheeks. Margie always wears makeup, specifically mascara and lip gloss.

Margie owned multiple smiley-face T-shirts with various hats, outfits, or expressions imprinted on them to encourage positive thinking. She also wears shorts. On the day of Jake’s death, Margie cuts up all of these smiley-face T-shirts and instead wears an old gray blouse.

entities.name: Margie's Family
entities.description:
Margie's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Margie from The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

Margie is the caretaker and Jake's guardian. She made her first debut in the Stitchwraith Stingers epilogue of Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch, and later appeared in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird as one of the major characters.

Margie's unnamed father appeared only once. Margie receives a phone call from her father, telling her to leave and go back home, but she angrily refuses.

Margie's unnamed mother was mentioned only once. Like her husband, she wants Margie to come back home.
entities.short_description: Margie's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Margie from The Real Jake, the second story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

entities.name: Markham Family
entities.description:
Markham's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Nole Markham from Blackbird, the first story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

Nole Markham is the main protagonist of the sixth Fazbear Frights book's first story.

Mr. Markham is Nole's father. He and Nole's grandpa were also frat boys when they were in college, and Nole carries on the family tradition.

Mrs. Markham is Nole's mother. When he has trouble falling asleep, he remembers advice she gave him on how to relax.
entities.short_description: Markham's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Nole Markham from Blackbird, the first story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

entities.name: Marks Family
entities.description:
Marks's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Devon Blaine Marks from The New Kid, the third story of Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM.

Devon Blaine Marks is the main protagonist of the third Fazbear Frights book's third story.

Mrs. Marks is Devon's mother. She is tall and skinny with short, mussed dark hair, brown eyes with circles under them, and thin lips. Mrs. Marks is a house cleaner.

Mr. Marks is Devon's father. All Devon remembers about his was that he was abusive towards him and Devon's mother, throwing things at them. He eventually left her and Devon when he was three, leaving Devon to live with his mom.
entities.short_description: Marks's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Devon Blaine Marks from The New Kid, the third story of Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM.

entities.name: Marley
entities.description:
is a major character in Pizza Kit, the third story of Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Marley is very pretty, with luxurious golden-blonde hair and big blue eyes with long dark lashes. Her body is slim but curvy enough to be feminine. Marley's toenails are painted baby pink and she has Caucasian skin.

Marley is very carefree. She leans on the railing thinking it is safe. But it wasn't.

Category:Fazbear Frights: Characters Category:FF9: Characters

entities.name: Mary Jo
entities.description:
Mary Jo is a major character in Find Player Two!, the third story in Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Mary Jo has frizzy brown hair, a large mouth with big teeth, caramel-colored skin, big bright brown eyes, a wide nose, and round cheeks. She is pudgy and six-inches taller than Aimee, as well as physically stronger. Mary Jo usually wears stained jeans and a too-tight T-shirt, and she carries around an overstuffed backpack.

Mary Jo is outspoken and rebellious. She is also bossy, which makes Aimee question their friendship. She also has a fear of abandonment after having been abandoned by her parents, to the point where she carries a backpack with supplies in case she needs to suddenly run away.

Mary Jo has been abandoned by both of her parents and has been in foster care with numerous families. Because of this, she carries around a heavy backpack with all the supplies she’ll need to run away, a secret she has only shared with Aimee. The two hang out at Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza, although Mary Jo prefers it more.

entities.name: Mason Blair
entities.description:
Mason Blair is a major characters in To Be Beautiful, a second story of Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit. He is Sarah's love interest who she initially embarrasses herself in front of, then later dates.

Mason is tall with dark-lashed, ocean-blue eyes. He also has straight and white teeth.

Mason is said to be nice and funny. He is also rather laid-back, never raising his voice when annoyed and later finding his minor grievances funny.

One day, Sarah accidently bumps into Mason at school as she's trying to desperately leave the cafeteria, dumping the remains of her salad on his expensive, crisp white designer shirt. He looks annoyed tells Sarah to watch where she's going as he picks a cucumber slice off his shirt, leaving a perfect oily circle in the middle of his chest. Sarah apologies and throws the rest of her food away, running out the cafeteria.

entities.name: Matt
entities.description:
Matt is the main protagonist of In the Flesh, the second story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. He is a narcissistic man who berates and judges everyone in his life. After numerous failed relationships, Matt pours is rage into development of the next Five Nights at Freddy's VR game, unknowingly giving life to his creation.

Matt is considered good-looking with a handsome face and a size 34 waistline. He’s also well dressed. Over time, Matt’s belly gets incredibly bloated, his skin turns yellowish, a hard knot forms on his forehead, his face and hair get drenched in sweat, and his hair gets thinner.

Matt is extremely arrogant and egotistical, believing himself to be a misunderstood genius and constantly seeking admiration through his wealth. He does everything he can to win things, but gets bored maintaining them. This, combined with his lack of empathy towards others, leads to Matt being alone and frustrated constantly. His loneliness and frustration makes him more obsessive over his work, pouring all his emotions into it. Matt also refuses to accept any responsibility, instead blaming everyone else for his misfortune. His distorted view of being wronged and used by others gives him destructive urges, with most of his thoughts being of destruction. Matt also believes women are crazy and abusive, and he tends to judge them purely off looks. He can be absentminded at times, but has an amazing memory when it comes to programming.

Matt is a game developer who got the role of creating the AI in a VR game called Springtrap's Revenge. When he play-tested the game, Springtrap always killed him. His co-worker, Jamie, enters and asks if he needed help. Matt rudely tells her to leave. He play-tested the game again only to get killed by Springtrap again. He then angrily reprogrammed the game to punish Springtrap.

entities.name: Meg
entities.description:
Meg is a major character in Lonely Freddy, the second story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. She's Alec and Hazel's mother who uses books to create what she views as a "perfect" family.

Meg has a turned-up nose and blonde hair like hay, which Alec inherits.

Meg named Alec as a combination of "Alexander" and the name Ian wanted, "Eric." After Hazel was born, she and Ian became more strict with Alec. Meg began looking for ways to mend Alec's behavior into something nicer and more friendly to match her vision of a perfect family. She tried going to her older sister, Gigi, for help and was given a few options, most of which were simply to not outcast Alec and treat him like a normal kid. Meg ignores those suggestions but does switch to organic milk. Eventually, Meg uses a book called The Growing Child to come up with exercises to shape Alec's behavior, as the book argued children need to be self-molded like clay. She and Ian have Alec change his name, try planting a garden, and go camping, but all three end in disaster.

A week before Hazel's tenth birthday, Meg comes up with a plan using Chapter Five of a new book titled The Plan Planner. The chapter states that in order to get a well-behaved, predictable child, parents are to treat them as the opposite of that. She discusses Chapter Five with Ian and convinces him to go along with the plan. The next day, the two constantly scold Alec for his behavior and actions. However, Hazel begins to behave poorly instead, showing Meg a less-than-stellar grade on her spelling test and rudely asking how many cavities Meg had during her last dentist visit. The following day, Hazel burps at the breakfast table when Meg scolds Alec over proper manners, says Meg looks haggard, and asks when Meg had last made an edible vegetable. Meg and Ian try to discuss Hazel's shift in behavior after dinner, but when Ian doesn't refute Hazel's haggard claim the two argue. Eventually they go to bed, with Meg informing Ian that she can't find the book.
entities.short_description: Meg is a major character in Lonely Freddy, the second story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. She's Alec and Hazel's mother who uses books to create what she views as a "perfect" family.

entities.name: Melissa
entities.description:
Melissa is a major character from Room for One More, the second story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM She's Stanley's older sister who tries her best to support him after his girlfriend breaks up with him.

Melissa has curly brown hair that she pulls back into a neat ponytail. She wears button-down shirts and khakis to work.

Melissa is a very responsible person, always being organized and planning ahead. She has a tendency to make others follow her organized schedule, which can make her seem bossy and annoying. Melissa cares for Stanley and can be stubborn when it comes to making sure he’s okay and taking care of himself.

entities.name: Mia Fremont
entities.description:
Mia Fremont is one of the protagonists of The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. She is a cheerful and sweet woman who begins working in the hospice wing of Heracles Hospital around the time strange events begin occurring there.

Mia is a young woman with her blonde hair pulled into a taut ponytail. She has a square face with a wide mouth, lively blue eyes, and bright makeup. Mia’s hands are small and soft. She wears a dark blue nurse’s uniform.

Mia is perky and energetic. She can also be rather curious, constantly eavesdropping on people. Mia isn’t squeamish and enjoys gore, finding it cool to see nature at work. When she initially gets hired to work in the hospice wing of Heracles Hospital, Mia is resentful and nervous, but eventually finds her work satisfying and feels empathy towards the families.

When Mia was a child, she came across an odor in an adjacent apartment and discovered the body of an elderly woman who lived alone. Although she hated the smell, she found the sight of the mass of magots on the corpse to be cool. Later in life, Mia decided to become a nurse, going to nursing school and getting a job at a prison hospital. When she tried looking for better positions, she can only find a job at the hospice wing at Heracles Hospital. Although she felt resentful that her high qualifications and excellent references only landed her a job there, her boyfriend's continual reminder that the job was a stepping stone made things a little better.
entities.short_description: Mia Fremont is one of the protagonists of The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. She is a cheerful and sweet woman who begins working in the hospice wing of Heracles Hospital around the…

entities.name: Michael
entities.description:
Michael is a major character in The Real Jake, the second story in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He is Jake's rich uncle and Evan’s only remaining family.

Michael is never physically described in the story, although he is said to be rich and wears a suit when visited by Jake, Evan, and Margie.

Michael is a very serious person. He is intense about making money and is a numbers genius, but doesn’t know how to connect and feel the way others do. Michael’s way of processing the world makes him rather stiff, awkward, and cold. Jake jokingly asks if he is like a "cyborg with bad programming".

Michael is a rich businessman who lives in Europe. Once, he went to the United States to visit Jake. They had an "awkward, stiff" dinner together that Margie and Jake share an inside joke about.
entities.short_description: Michael is a major character in The Real Jake, the second story in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He is Jake's rich uncle and Evan’s only remaining family.

entities.name: Mick Callahan
entities.description:
Mick Callahan is the deuteragonist of The New Kid, the third story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM. He's Devon's best and only friend who's childish behavior make him an outcast at school.

Mick has a round face with round wire-rimmed glasses, reddish-blond hair with bangs, a freckled forehead and face, a small mouth, and large brown eyes. He’s somewhat chubby and almost as tall as Devon. Mick wears a superhero watch, high-waisted corduroy pants, and button-down short-sleeve shirts.

Mick likes doing whatever makes him happy, which makes him nerdy and childish. He loves eating and using out-of-date or even made up slang. Mick is obsessed with superheroes and sci-fi, constantly talking about those two subjects. He also likes statistics, enjoying baseball just for the stats. Mick has some undiagnosed learning disorders and tends to have attention issues, constantly caught daydreaming and staring out the school windows. Deep down, Mick does care about fitting in at school and is hurt by how much he and Devon are ignored, but is more fearful of rejection and still wants to stay in his fantasy world. He also doesn’t let things bother him so he isn’t miserable all the time. Despite his occasional sharp moments, Mick is rather innocent and naïve, as he is very trusting of his family and friends.

Category:Fazbear Frights: Characters Category:FF3: Characters Category:Fazbear Frights: Callahan Family

entities.name: Mike
entities.description:
Mike is a major character in Into the Pit, the first story from Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit, as well as its adaptations: the video game Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit, and the interactive novel Return to the Pit. He is a young boy that Oswald befriends when traveling to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza in 1985.

Mike is a tall black kid with huge eyeglasses. When Oswald first meets him, he is wearing a shirt with wide red and blue stripes. Later, Mike wears a Back to the Future t-shirt, though the game adaptation gives it a more generic name.

In the game, his two mentioned outfits are combined into a red-and-blue striped shirt with a film logo on it. He also wears a blue baseball cap, jeans, and brown shoes. He has round black glasses and brown hair, and his idle animation involves him pulling out a green handheld game console and playing it.

Mike likes to act rather playful and cocky, but is a good sport towards Chip and Oswald. He is also rather generous, noticing Oswald not spending any money but still choosing to pay for him. He is a bit more of a jokester than Chip, but still good-natured. His favorite movie is Back to the Future, but he finds The Eternal Song boring. He also finds his sister's dolls creepy.

entities.name: Mike
entities.description:
Mike is Colton's uncle in Jump for Tickets, the second story of Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Uncle Mike is trusting and kind to Colton.

Uncle Mike runs a car repair shop. Two days a week, Colton visits to help Mike fix cars, where he learns a lot about mechanical things and Mike sometimes gives him money in return. Mike says that he may hire him in the future.

In order to get the tools necessary to "fix" the Ticket Pulverizer, Colton asks Mike to borrow some tools for a project, which he allows.

entities.name: Mike
entities.description:
Mike is a security guard at an old Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. He appeared in You're the Band, the third story of Fazbear Frights 12: Felix the Shark.

Sylvia describes Mike as a young Caucasian man in his early twenties, wearing shorts and a T-shirt. His appearance akin to that of an college student.

Mike was hired as a security guard at an abandoned Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, the same location where a tragic incident occurred thirty years prior to the events of You're the Band. He is seemingly aware that the animatronics are possessed.

Weeks before the story takes place, Freddy's was broken into and multiple items were stolen, one of them being Freddy Fazbear's mask.

entities.name: Mike's Family
entities.description:
Mike's family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Mike from the first book's Into the Pit story.

Mike is Chip's friend. Both make friends with Oswald, who uses the ball pit from Jeff's Pizza to time travel to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza in 1985.

Mike's unnamed sister is mentioned during the conversation with Chip and Oswald. Mike explains that he sometimes looks at his sister's dolls, which are lined up on the shelf in her room, and feels as if they're staring at him.

Mike's unnamed grandmother is mentioned when Mike tells Oswald that she only gives him money on his birthday, which he assumed Oswald's did as well.
entities.short_description: Mike's family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Mike from the first book's Into the Pit story.

entities.name: Millicent Fitzsimmons
entities.description:
Millicent "Millie" Fitzsimmons is the main protagonist of Count the Ways, the third story from Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit. She's an ice-cold teenage Goth girl who romanticizes Death, using her obsession as an escape from her miserable life. Millie herself doesn't truly want to die, but on Christmas Eve she is trapped within an animatronic and given no choice.

Millie has a gothic appearance. She is pale and wears a sheer light powder to make her face look paler in contrast to her black eyeliner and black clothing. Millie also likes to wear jet Victorian mourning jewelry. On Christmas Eve, she's wearing head-to-toe black and purple clothing with small earrings, a necklace made of jet beads, and a silver cuff bracelet on her wrist. While the story says she goes outside without her jacket, the eleventh Stitchwraith Stinger claims that she's wearing a black sweater.

In the colorized image in The Ultimate Guide, Millie is shown having dark brown hair and brown eyes. She is wearing a purple hoodie, black leggings, and purple bracelets.

Millie's sprite in Into the Pit is in black-and-white and minimalist, so little can be ascertained about her game appearance. She has long hair that is darker than her skin, a gray outfit, and distinctly green eyes.

entities.name: Millie's Grandfather
entities.description:
Millie's unnamed grandfather is a major character who appeared in Count the Ways, the third story from the first Fazbear Frights book. He is an eccentric collector who loves his family and wants to do everything to make them happy, even if Millie doesn't want to be.

Millie’s grandfather has wispy gray hair that is always messy and wild, and he always wears the same "ratty" tan cardigan.

Millie's grandfather is a nice person who wants to make Millie happy and comfortable during her stay with him. After the death of his wife, he became rather lonely and misses her every day. This is possibly the reason why he values making his family happy and why he loves celebrating Christmas. With that said, he isn’t afraid to be stern with Millie when she gets too angry at him. Millie's grandfather is also an eccentric collector, although it’s unclear as to what he collects. He enjoys chocolate and is pretty literate, enjoying the works of Edgar Allan Poe and similar writers.

Millie's grandparents meet in high school during lunch, having a good conversation with each other. They became high school sweethearts, went to the same college, and got engaged during the senior year, marrying in June after they graduated. Millie's grandfather became a math teacher at the local high school, and his students enjoyed his class. Eventually, they moved into a 150-year-old sprawling Victorian house. Millie's grandfather would place his collections all around the house, and he's also spend some time after dinner in the workshop located in the backyard. He and his wife also visited different states, collecting souvenir plates with the names and landmarks of where the two visited. They had two sons: Jeff and Rob.

entities.name: Mindy
entities.description:
Mindy is a major character in Together Forever, the third story in Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Mindy is freckled, redheaded, and small for her age. She has puffy and pudgy round cheeks, straight hair that hangs just below her narrow shoulder blades, a dimpled chin, pudgy arms, pale skin, and reddish-blonde eyebrows. Mindy prefers wearing gingham, polka dots, animal prints, and little floral patterns. She also has sparkling purple shoes with rainbow-colored shoelaces. For most of the story, Mindy wears a full-skirted short dress. The next day, she wears her favorite corduroy jumper with a red-and-yellow frilly blouse.

entities.name: Mott
entities.description:
is the main protagonist of Sea Bonnies, the second story of Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Mott has his father’s plain brown hair. With naturally wavy hair, hooded dark brown eyes, a strong chin, and great teeth, Mott is considered "objectively good-looking." After his 13th birthday he gets taller and begins to work out, getting broad shoulders.

Mott's family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Mott from the tenth book's Sea Bonnies story.

Mott is the main protagonist of Sea Bonnies.

Rory is a major character in Sea Bonnies.

She doesn't believe Mott when he says that the Sea Bonnies are eating him little by little. She gives Mott some cash for him to spend on himself and Rory.

entities.description:
Mr. Harrison is a character from Jump for Tickets, the second story from Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Mr. Harrison is balding, and has a prominent moustache.

Mr. Harrison is described as being fatherly, usually being really gentle with his students. He has been cited playing 'Football' once. He has a particular interest in science, and is going to be on hiatus to Europe.

entities.name: Mr. Thornton
entities.description:
Mr. Thornton is a major character in Together Forever, the third story in Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Mr. Thornton is a short man in his twenties with birdlike features, such as beady eyes, a pointed nose, and fine brown hair. He always wears vests and thick, black-rimmed glasses. For most of the story, Mr. Thornton wears a red-and-gold diamond-patterned sweater vest that hangs loosely over his narrow chest.

Mr. Thornton is considered geeky and nerdy. He has trouble keeping eye contact, never facing straight at the class and focusing his gaze a foot above people's heads. Jessica finds this behavior endearing in a loveable-nerd kind of way. Mr. Thornton also frequently leaves his sentences unfinished and rarely laughs.

Mr. Thornton is the robotics teacher at the high school Jessica and Brittany attend. When Brittany took notice of his habit of leaving sentences unfinished, she had jokingly suggested that he might be an animatronic with advanced programming and a minor glitch that prevented him from completing sentences. A few weeks before the homecoming dance, eight graders Mindy and Cindy joined Mr. Thornton's class due to their gifted knowledge of robotics.
entities.short_description: Mr. Thornton is a major character in Together Forever, the third story in Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

entities.name: Mrs. Crutchfield
entities.description:
Mrs. Crutchfield is a major character in Pizza Kit, the third story in Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Mrs. Crutchfield is tiny and birdlike. At the start of the story, she’s wearing a navy-blue dotted dress that looks decades old.

Mrs. Crutchfield is a strict Home Economics teacher who does things such as set unnecessarily high standards for her students, grading down entire letter grades based on minor mistakes such as not washing an egg before boiling it and slightly overdoing a scrambled egg. She is implied to be known for doing this among former students as Payton's mother describes her as having impossible standards. She also holds very traditional views on etiquette and has low tolerance for jokes in her class as she embarrassed both Payton and her mother over small remarks. However, despite this, she is also shown to care for her students, ordering Payton to call Marley when she first goes missing in the factory.

Category:Fazbear Frights: Characters Category:FF9: Characters
entities.short_description: Mrs. Crutchfield is a major character in Pizza Kit, the third story in Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

entities.description:
Joel D'Agostino (Son)|first_appearance=Kids at Play|occupation=Writer|eye_color=Dark}} Mrs. D'Agostino is a major character in Kids at Play, the second story in Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Mrs. D'Agostino is tall with with a sturdy body and large facial features, such as her big and heavily lashed dark eyes. Joel thinks she would look rather masculine if it weren't for her makeup and her long braided hair that she puts into a topknot whenever she's sleeping. She's always wearing no-nonsense clothes, which are usually dark slacks or high-waisted mom jeans and bright-colored blouses (like magenta and emerald green).

entities.description:
Mrs. Thompson is Payton's mother and a major character in Pizza Kit, the third story in Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Mrs. Thompson wears a nice blue blouse, gray dress slacks, and plumps to work. At home she wears fuzzy pink house slippers.

entities.description:
Ms. Bryant is the manager of the Freddy Fazbear Pizza Kit Factory from Pizza Kit, the third story in Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Ms. Bryant is a pretty, short black woman. During the tour, she wears a net cap and a Chica costume.

entities.description:
Ms. Colter is Edward's mother from Friendly Face, the first story from Fazbear Frights 10: Friendly Face.

Ms. Colter usually looks tired, and she wears her auburn hair in twists. She also wears subtle makeup. Ms. Colter has hazel eyes, a small nose, a wide mouth, and a strong jaw.

Category:Fazbear Frights: Characters Category:FF10: Characters

entities.name: Nate
entities.description:
Nate is a major character in 1:35 A.M., the first story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM He is the stern yet caring middle-aged owner of the diner Delilah works at.

Nate is tall, fit, good-looking, and well groomed. He has short graying black hair and a tidy, closed-trimmed beard. Nate also has pewter-gray eyes.

Nate can come off as rather mean and aggressive, but he’s really hiding a softer side. While he complains about everyone in the diner, as well as the diner in general, he truthfully loves them all. Nate shows off his softer and happier side through teasing. However, he will still put his foot down if he has to.

Nate is Delilah's employer and the owner of the diner. He calls Delilah twice on the day she bought Ella, first when she initially woke up at 6:25 a.m. and a second time at 2:25 p.m. after she's late for her replacement two o'clock shift. As Delilah is throwing Ella away, Nate opens the back door of the diner to let her in. The next day, Delilah arrives at work to discover that Nate had made two to ten her permanent shift. When asked why, Nate explains that he did it so Delilah isn't late, as he's constantly letting her arriving late slide. The two do some light teasing and Delilah starts her shift.
entities.short_description: Nate is a major character in 1:35 A.M., the first story in Fazbear Frights 3: 1:35AM He is the stern yet caring middle-aged owner of the diner Delilah works at.

entities.name: Nole Markham
entities.description:
is the main protagonist of Blackbird, the first story in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He is a cool young man who is haunted by an entity intent on punishing him for his mean behavior.

Nole is six-foot-one with blue eyes, an athletic build, and scruffy blond hair. He also has a white scar below his left knee from falling off his bike after being chased by a goose. Nole usually wears faded jeans, white shirts, a watch, and leather jackets when the weather allows it. He sleeps in just his white boxer briefs.

Nole tries to act cool and confident, usually with nonchalant posturing. He also enjoys having fun, which can make him somewhat of a slacker and clueless at times. Still, Nole cares about film enough to get serious and focus. He's also a minimalist, keeping very little in his room. Nole’s desire to be cool makes him act rather mean, ruthlessly bullying others in junior high. By college he still finds his past cruelty funny and has a habit of pushing too far and getting offensive with his jokes. However, Nole begins to reflect on his past and feels guilty over his actions, leading to him attempting to better himself as a person. When stressed, he’ll usually say his thoughts aloud. Nole can also usually sleep through anything, although his experiences with the Blackbird keep him up at night.

When Nole was in junior high school, he bullied a girl named Christine. Due to the poor state of her clothes, Nole subjected her to constant torment and even convinced his classmates to join in on the bullying.
entities.short_description: is the main protagonist of Blackbird, the first story in Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird. He is a cool young man who is haunted by an entity intent on punishing him for his mean behavior.

entities.name: Nurse Ackerman
entities.description:
is a major character in The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. She is the cold head nurse of the hospice wing in Heracles Hospital. She can also be considered an antagonist, as she opposes Arthur.

Nurse Ackerman is a tall, sharp-edged woman with too many teeth and an unsettling dark-eyed gaze. She is very skinny with a bony back. Nurse Ackerman also has a large mole under her left eye. Her dark blue uniform pants are too short, revealing her black socks and an inch or so of white skin between them and the hem of her pants.

Nurse Ackerman is cut off from her emotions, making her dismissive and unfriendly. She never smiles and is stern with other nurses in the hospice wing, constantly firing orders. Despite the death of her son leaving her heart broken, Nurse Ackerman has a desire to help others who have to walk in her shoes.

Nurse Ackerman lived a fairly normal life until her son Elijah died. After this, she became cold and detached from others who constantly reminded her of the life she had once shared with her son. Despite her frozen heart, she went on to become a hospice nurse to help others who had to be in her situation. As of the events of The Man in Room 1280, she is the head nurse of the hospice wing in Heracles Hospital. She meets Arthur Blythe a week prior to the events of the story, only giving him a room name.

entities.name: Nurse Colton
entities.description:
is a major character in The Man in Room 1280, the third story in Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call. She is a rather serious nurse working in the hospice wing of Heracles Hospital. Nurse Colton can be considered one of the story's antagonists due to her opposition to Arthur and the patient.

Nurse Colton is athletic-looking with brown hair chopped short in a boyish cut, and a great tan.

Nurse Colton is decently nice yet very serious. She considers herself the perfect balance of heart and brain, feeling deeply yet also having a depth of reason. Nurse Colton also believes in the power of intention and human will, which she uses as a nurse to help others.

Nurse Colton's parents died when she was sixteen. Foregoing foster care, she ran away and found a woman who made fake IDs, and got a job on a cruise ship that came with a free roam and board. Over time, she saved up enough money to pay for nursing school, and eventually ended up in Heracles Hospital to use what she knew to help others who lost their parents.

entities.name: O'Neil Family
entities.description:
O'Neil's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Sam O'Neil from Blackbird, the first story of Fazbear Frights 6: Blackbird.

Sam O'Neil is the deuteragonist of the sixth Fazbear Frights book's first story.

Paul O'Neil is Sam's father. He's really nice to Nole and supportive of Sam. Paul helps get the feathers needed for the Blackbird costume. He is devastated when Sam goes missing and his blood is found on the tracks.

Molly O'Neil is Sam's mother. She's really nice to Nole and supportive of Sam. Molly is devastated when Sam goes missing and his blood is found on the tracks.

entities.name: Ophelia
entities.description:
Ophelia is a major character from Gumdrop Angel, the first story of the book with the same name. She's a sweet little girl that tries her best to get along with her older step-sister but is often the victim of Angel's fury because of how often her father spoils her.

Ophelia inherited her father's prominent brow ridge, large nose, small eyes, and long arms. Angel considers her to be ugly, comparing her to a chimpanzee.

Ophelia is very kind, trying her best to include Angel by constantly offering to share and spend time with her. Despite Angel's dismissive behavior she is persistent in trying to get along with her. Ophelia can be rather clumsy, tripping over herself occasionally. She's also obsessed with horses.

entities.description:
Brown (graphic novel)|eye_color=Brown|color=Dark (novel) Light (graphic novel)}}

Ory Girard is a major character in The Breaking Wheel, the second story in Fazbear Frights 7: The Cliffs. He's Shelly and Pickle’s younger brother who starts playing with Pickle's robot, unknowingly causing Reed to panic.

Ory is a combination of his two older siblings, making him not as cute as Shelly but cuter than Pickle. He has a round and somewhat pudgy face. Ory shares Shelly’s large eyes, long lashes, and full mouth, and he shares Pickle’s big, long beaky nose, although it looks more amusing on him than his older brother.

Ory is a rambunctious little kid who likes to have fun. He’s usually only interested in cars and racing, but is surprised by how much fun he has with Pickle’s robot.

entities.name: Oscar Avila
entities.description:
is the protagonist of Out of Stock, the third story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He is a teenage boy who, after a constant string of tragedy and misfortune, decides to take a Plushtrap Chaser toy despite his better judgement.

Not much is said about Oscar's appearance besides his smooth features and dark-brown eyes that he shares with his mother. His shoes are also described as having the wrong logo.

Despite his attempts to be hopeful, Oscar has a rather pessimistic view on life due to a constant string of bad luck and misfortune. He loves his mother and is unwilling to disappoint her, so he usually accepts his losses and lets opportunities pass him by. Oscar eventually becomes more frustrated and begins acting out, such as taking the lifelike Plushtrap Chaser and yelling at his mother. He is quick to regret these decisions and tries his best to rectify things. Oscar has great respect for his friends and will do anything to protect them, like lying to his mother and risking his own life. During his final confrontation with the Plushtrap Chaser he realizes that luck isn’t found, it’s made, and you need to know when to grab hold of it when it is. Oscar also comes to appreciate the smaller things in life, even if his friends would find it silly.

For most of Oscar's life, he's had to deal with constant misfortune and tragedy. When he was rather young, his father went to the hospital for a tonsillectomy and contracted a fatal infection, leaving his mother to raise Oscar alone. The two had to move to the cheaper side of town and limit their luxuries due to a poor income. In third grade, Oscar met Raj and Isaac on the playground and the three became best friends. Oscar also became very close with his mother, even when he'd act up like setting a bat free in their house. As he grew older, however, his mother became more dependent on him. Oscar spends most of his time helping his mom at the Royal Oaks Nursing Home while his friends Raj and Isaac spend their allowances at the mall.

entities.name: Oswald
entities.description:
is the protagonist of Into the Pit, the first story from Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit, and its adaptations: the video game Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit, and the interactive novel Return to the Pit. He's a young boy who, after many boring days in his dying town, decides to enter a strange ball pit that seemingly lets him travel in time, only to find himself fighting to save his father from an aggressive and mysterious Yellow Rabbit.

In the video game adaptation, along with the scrapped artwork for the original story, Oswald has spiky brown hair that is slicked back, light peach skin, and brown eyes (although they are blue on his sprite). He wears deep blue jeans with black shoes, a red and yellow striped t-shirt, and a deep blue opened up hoodie. Descriptions from Oswald's inventory items mention that he has his father's eyes.

The book's description of Oswald is very small; he has freckles and a cowlick. He wears a chain around his neck with his house key on it. In the graphic novel, he has short dark brown hair and usually wears a t-shirt and shorts.

Oswald is somewhat pessimistic due to the closure of a mill which left many without a job. He's also embarrassed by his family and electronics, hiding his outdated technology from others in his class and arguing with his father over his out-of-date tastes. Despite his desire to do more, Oswald is very understanding of his family's and others' financial situation and tries his best to be respectful. He deeply loves his parents despite their differences, and has the same sense of humor as his father.

entities.name: Oswald's Family
entities.description:
Oswald's Family in the first Fazbear Frights book's Into the Pit story comprises the relatives of Oswald.

Oswald is the main protagonist of the Into the Pit story.

Oswald's unnamed father is the deuteragonist of the Into the Pit story.

Oswald's unnamed mother is a character from Into the Pit. She works as a nurse in a local hospital. As a result she doesn't get to spend much time with Oswald other than breakfast, which forces his father to always take care of him and make him his food. When she is available she usually cooks them dinner and has family nights with them.
entities.short_description: Oswald's Family in the first Fazbear Frights book's Into the Pit story comprises the relatives of Oswald.

entities.name: Oswald's Father
entities.description:
Oswald's unnamed father is a major character in Fazbear Frights 1: Into the Pit, appearing in the first story of the same name, as well as its adaptations: Five Nights at Freddy's: Into the Pit and Return to the Pit. He's a somewhat older man who wants to give his son the best, even with his poor income. His capture and replacement by the Yellow Rabbit causes Oswald to step up, sneak out of the house, and find him within the mysterious ballpit.

The book describes Oswald’s father as having stubble. He isn’t a big man, but he still weighs twice as much as Oswald. He wears a red vest to work, white undershirts, and steel-toed brown work boots with thick boot socks. The story's illustration depicts Oswald's father as slightly pot-bellied with slicked back gray hair, a mustache, and a beard. He also has bushy black eyebrows. He wears a pair of blue jeans and white shirt.

In the game adaptation, Oswald's father is plus-sized with brown hair and a beard, a blue t-shirt, blue jeans, and black shoes. When replaced by the Yellow Rabbit, it takes his form except with glowing bright blue eyes.

His age is never specified, but he was around Oswald's age in 1985, which means he was born in the early 1970s. His story takes place over the late 2010s-early 2020s, so he is roughly in his 40s.

entities.name: Oswald's Mother
entities.description:
Oswald's unnamed mother is a character who appears in Into the Pit, the first story from the first Fazbear Frights book.

Oswald's mother has blonde hair pulled back in a ponytail. When making breakfast, she wears a fuzzy pink bathrobe. In both the game and the graphic novel, she is shown wearing her hospital scrubs.

Oswald's mother cares deeply for her son, missing him during work and feeling bad for having such long hours. As a licensed practical nurse, she tends to point out places she finds too germy to play in and can be somewhat over-protective. Oswald's mom also tends to diffuse arguments between her son and husband.

Oswald's mother and father have known each other since high school, having gone on dates at a roller rink and becoming great skaters. Oswald's mom had a steady job at a hospital, which has her working twelve-hour shifts most days. She had once told Oswald that adult life is a difficult balance between time and money, so he doesn't care for her long hours as much as she does. At some point they started a one-night-a-week event known as Family Fun Night, which varied depending on her work schedule. First they'd get dinner at either a pizza, Chinese, or Mexican restaurant, then they'd do a fun activity together. This could either be seeing a kid-friendly movie, going to the bowling alley, or to the roller rink where they'd help Oswald skate by holding his hands and keeping him up. The evening usually ended with a waffle cone at the ice-cream place downtown.

entities.name: Parker
entities.description:
Parker is a major character from Prankster, the first story from Fazbear Frights 11: Prankster.

Parker has brown hair that he puts too much gel on, especially on his forelock. He also has large, unbelievably white teeth and full lips. He goes to work in an impeccable suit. Based on the eyeballs Jeremiah finds during his birthday prank, Parker is implied to have blue eyes.

entities.name: Patricia
entities.description:
Patricia is a major character from Coming Home, the third story in Fazbear Frights 4: Step Closer. She's Susie and Samantha's mother who, after the death of her oldest daughter by the hands of a serial killer, falls into a deep depression.

Patricia is tall and skinny with dark-brown hair, big eyes, and a wide mouth. Before Susie's death, Patricia’s hair was really shiny and bouncy, and she wore long fake lashes and sassy red lipstick. After Susie’s death, Patricia lets her hair go limp, stops wearing makeup, and constantly looks tired. Patricia’s skin has turned so pale that her veins can be seen on her forehead, hands, and arms.

At the start of the story, Patricia wears a wrinkled blue T-shirt and faded jeans. She later wears a wide-brimmed straw hat when talking to Jeanie on the porch.

Patricia used to smile and laugh easily. She was also very serious and protective of her work and flowers, getting angry whenever Susie or Samantha messed with either of them. After Susie’s death, however, Patricia becomes depressed. She cries frequently and constantly blames herself for what happened, torturing herself with the past. Patricia also has trouble going to sleep, only being able to with the help of pills. As a result she also has issues getting up in the morning. Patricia usually has low energy, ignoring her flowers as a result. She also seems to dissociate, stopping in the middle of tasks and staring off into the distance.

entities.description:
is the main protagonist of Pizza Kit, the third story of Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Payton has a short, skinny body without curves. She has dull brown hair and eyes, and she has freckles which she hates.

entities.name: Pete Dinglewood
entities.description:
is the main protagonist of Step Closer, the first story in the book of the same name. He later briefly appears in the tenth Stitchwraith Stinger. Pete is an aggressive teenage boy who is constantly angry following his parents' divorce. After six months of watching over his younger brother Chuck, Pete lashes out and tries scaring him using Foxy the Pirate, but ends up cursed instead.

Pete has freckles and dark hair. He usually wears plain white sneakers and a baseball cap turned backward. Pete wears a hoodie and jeans to the Homecoming festival.

Pete has a bad attitude, feeling like a ticking time bomb. He wants to be free to do whatever he wants, but after his parents’ divorce he is given more responsibilities. Pete used to always finish what he started, but after the divorce he stops caring as much. This includes football, which he used as an outlet for his emotions. Now, Pete is constantly angry and annoyed by mostly everything, especially Chuck. He is also rather mouthy and stubborn, and initially refuses to accept any supernatural elements are at play. Eventually, Pete realizes that all he wants is to have everything back to normal and he actually has an okay life, even if his parents are divorced.

Pete is forced to babysit his younger brother, Chuck, due to their parent's divorce. One day, while watching him at Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza, he decides to punish Chuck by taking him to the maintenance room because he feels annoyed that he can’t be with any one of his friends, especially Maria. Chuck escapes as Pete tries to start up Foxy, as Chuck is afraid of Foxy. Pete's shirt gets caught on a nail as he tries to catch him. The curtains open and Foxy begins to sing a lyric repeatedly about how if you want to become a pirate, you need to lose an eye and an arm first. Pete is mesmerized by it. Pete manages to escape and the brothers return home. When they arrive, their mom shows them brochures about being organ donors, which unnerves Pete.

entities.name: Pets
entities.description:
This is the list of all pets in the Fazbear Frights series.

Annabel Lee is Millie Fitzsimmons's black cat from Count the Ways. She is named after the character Annabel Lee from the poem of the same name by Edgar Allen Poe. Millie thinks the cat has a better name than her. Annabel Lee only appears once, curled up on Millie's bed as she's reading famous poems about death.

Two days after Christmas, Greg misses the bus and has to walk his bike home. When he passes his next door neighbors, their dog launches itself from an outdoor table and throws itself over the short fence right at Greg. He manages to catch the dog just as it hit his chest and snaps at his jugular. Greg pushes the dog back over the fence and runs away as it flings itself against the wooden boards. Greg texts Hadi about the incident and the dog shows up in his nightmares that night. The next day, Greg finds the neighbor's dog dead against the back wheel of his bike tire with its throat torn apart and its belly gutted. After disposing of the body in some bushes, Greg gets a text from Fetch saying, "YW." Greg tells Cyril and Hadi about the dead dog, and Hadi goes to see it.

Oro is Manuel Gomez's yellow Labrador from Fetch. Because Manuel is from Madrid, Oro only understands Spanish. One day, while Manuel is playing with Oro in his front yard, Greg texts Manuel asking for help with his Spanish homework. Manuel left his phone inside, and Greg believes Fetch may try to harm Manuel, so he learns his address and bikes to his house. Once learning Manuel is okay, Greg improves his Spanish while playing with Oro and a red ball.
entities.short_description: This is the list of all pets in the Fazbear Frights series.

entities.name: Phineas Taggart
entities.description:
Dr. was a robotics scientist and a creator of the Stitchwraith from the Fazbear Frights series.

Dr. Phineas Taggart is very neat in his appearance, not wanting to appear sloppy despite being retired and supposedly ugly. He wears a pristine white lab coat that he pulls the tail out from under him and smooths it when sitting, a narrow red tie, and a gray dress shirt with a stiff collar. Phineas keeps his graying hair trimmed short and his round homely face clean shaven.

Dr. Phineas studied the concepts of energy and human emotions. He believes that humans can put up a "protective energy shield" against negative intentions. His most important research on emotions is "agony", which he believed to be the strongest emotion out of all others, enough to affiliate into an inanimate object to bring it to life. For his experiments, he bought "haunted" objects, such as torture devices from online auctions. He dislikes the term though, he'd rather believe them to be "energized by agony” as opposed to the objects being possessed by ghosts.

Every week, Phineas receives a new shipment of emotionally charged objects. One day, he received an endoskeleton for his biggest project yet, along with some other new energized items. Dr. Phineas gets to work on the endoskeleton. He first ripped the head of the Real Jake Doll, a drawn-on white doll, and placed it on top of the endoskeleton. Then, he tore apart Fetch, a scrapped animatronic dog, and put its battery pack onto the endoskeleton. Once the agonized endoskeleton began to move, its metal fingers attempted to touch Phineas. Its battery started to glow red, and Phineas sensed danger and tried to create a mental shield. He died, feeling excruciating pain and his consciousness annihilated.
entities.short_description: Dr. was a robotics scientist and a creator of the Stitchwraith from the Fazbear Frights series.

entities.name: Pickle Girard
entities.description:
Dilbert "Pickle" Girard is a major character in The Breaking Wheel, the second story of Fazbear Frights #7: The Cliffs. He is a teenage science nerd and one of Reed's few friends.

Pickle is short and dark, like his twin sister Shelly. He has unusually deep-set eyes, a nearly black unibrow, a strangely small mouth filled with crooked teeth, and a big, long beaky nose. Despite his eating habits, Pickle is rather skinny.

Pickle is a science nerd who can come off as thoughtless sometimes because he gets wrapped up in his books and projects. He’s also rather matter-of-fact with his behavior and intelligence, which adds to his unintentionally mean demeanor. Pickle is too uninterested in others’ shortcomings to make fun of them like Julius, and he can usually come off as disinterested. He also loves eating and mathematics. Pickle lacks coordination, making him a bit clumsy at times. He also can’t read interpersonal visual cues, struggling to decipher facial expressions, body language, and other social cues. To make up for it, Pickle remembers everything he reads and hears.

Reed had been friends with Shelly and Pickle for nearly ten years around the time the story takes place. In their freshman year, Shelly and Pickle convince Reed to join a robotics class. In the first week of class, Pickle begins to believe that the teacher is an android, and begins planning on proving his hypothesis, however Shelly doesn't let him go forward with any plans.
entities.short_description: Dilbert "Pickle" Girard is a major character in The Breaking Wheel, the second story of Fazbear Frights #7: The Cliffs. He is a teenage science nerd and one of Reed's few friends.

entities.name: Porter
entities.description:
is the tritagonist of The Puppet Carver, the first story of Fazbear Frights 9: The Puppet Carver.

Porter works as a employee at Pizza Playground alongside Sage Brantley, Porter constantly gets yelled at by his boss Jack due to slacking. One day Porter proudly tells his boss about a machine he has been working on. After a while Porter attempts to show his machine to his boss, but it breaks down. Jack fires all of his employees including Porter. Eventually he gets rehired. Porter then decides to work on a newer version of his machine. entities.name: Raj
entities.description:
is a major character in Out of Stock, the third story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He's one of Oscar's loyal friends who sticks by his side even after he takes the Plushtrap Chaser.

Although Raj isn't described in the story, it can be inferred that he is at least of average height. In the graphic novel, Raj is depicted with dark skin, a square jaw, brown spiky hair, brown eyes, and glasses.

Raj is a very loyal friend, sticking by Oscar’s side even when he gets them into trouble or has to cancel plans. He's very understanding of Oscar’s financial situation and is willing to share with him. While Raj will tease Oscar and joke around with him like Isaac, he tends to be kinder and is typically the more rational member of their friend group. He can also be rather moody, especially when things don't go his way.

Raj grew up with a very strict mother who came up with harsh punishments. Once, his sister Avni talked back to her and she was forced to not speak for a week. In third grade, Raj met Oscar and Isaac on the playground and the three became best friends. He spends his free time spending his allowance at the mall with Isaac and hanging out with Oscar. Both Raj and Isaac are very understanding of Oscar's different financial situation, and always change their plans and try to include Oscar whenever they can. Raj also leaves his gaming console at Oscar's house, keeping it away from his siblings and getting to share it with him.

entities.description:
Raj's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Raj from Out of Stock, the third story of Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch.

Avni is Raj's sister. When Oscar entertains the idea of ditching school to get a Plushtrap Chaser, Raj refuses as he is wary of his mother's strict punishments, and he points out that after his sister talked back to her she wouldn't let her speak for a week. By the sixth day, Avni almost forgot how to talk.

entities.name: Reed
entities.description:
is the main protagonist of The Breaking Wheel, the second story in Fazbear Frights 7: The Cliffs. He is a teenage outcast who is relentlessly bullied by Julius. In an uncharacteristic burst of nerve, Reed traps Julius is his exosuit and leaves him alone in the school, but quickly regrets it.

Reed is skinny with unusually long arms. He has a pronounced brow ridge and a jutting jaw that gives him more of an apelike appearance, something Julius made fun of when he was younger. Recently, Reed grows his curly brown hair long to disguise his primate features a little.

Reed is an outcast, having used his overwhelming grief to barricade himself from others after the death of his mother. While he didn't see a point to getting along with others and separated himself from his previous friends, he later befriended Pickle and Shelly. Reed has a vivid imagination, which makes his mind wander at times and lose focus. He's also into computers and has an aptitude for programming, and hopes to combine this with his love of fiction to become a game designer. Despite his interest in computers, Reed is uninterested and confused by robotics. He also shows a complete ineptitude when it comes to engineering and building. Reed lacks initiative and motivation, unwilling to act on his hatred of Julius or his crush on Shelly out of fear and low confidence. When he finally gains some impetus to act, however, he goes against his morals to punish Julius. Despite Reed’s attempts to justify his actions, he soon becomes panicked and filled with guilt.

Reed has been best friends with Pickle and Shelly for the past ten years. When they were five, Reed had attempted to build a log cabin, but it came out messy and wrong. Shelly had found it funny, and continues to remind Reed of this every time they're assigned science models and historical event dioramas. One day, Reed's mother dies and he shuts himself off from all of his friends except Pickle and Shelly. This caused him to become an outcast. Around six years ago, Reed began to get bullied by a kid named Julius.

entities.name: Reed's Family
entities.description:
Reed's Family in Fazbear Frights comprises the relatives of Reed from The Breaking Wheel, the second story of Fazbear Frights 7: The Cliffs.

Reed is the main protagonist of the seventh Fazbear Frights book's second story.

Alexa is Reed's younger sister. Reed plans to build his exoskeleton project to fit over his sister's doll in order to scare her, but he realizes he won't finish in time.

Reed's dad is a single father after his wife died. Reed knows that he tries his best for his family, but he feels more at home in Girard's family.
